News.title: Hundreds of Brits are falling sick after visiting some of the UK’s most affluent beaches ahead of fifth heatwave of year
News.content:
TROUBLED WATERS Hundreds of Brits are falling sick after visiting some of the UK’s most affluent beaches ahead of fifth heatwave of year

HUNDREDS of tourists are falling sick at some of Britain’s most affluent beaches ahead of the fifth heatwave of the summer.

New figures show high reports of illness across the UK’s beaches, those accredited under British Blue Flag meaning they’ve passed strict tests for cleanliness.

Marine conservation charity Surfers Against Sewage (SAS) says it’s received 765 reports of sickness across 406 locations so far this year, reports the Mirror.



Further stats show more than 15,000 days – or 41 years – have been taken off work due to illness contracted from UK’s waters since 2019.



SAS says polluted water has resulted in the likes of ear infections and gastroenteritis, as well as respiratory and skin issues, meaning time off work.

Nearly half the reports so far this year have been since May 1 – with Britain currently experiencing its fifth heatwave of the summer so far.

The Met Office has forecast potential temperatures of 36C next week, with meteorologists predicting the annual record for days exceeding 30C will be smashed.



Beaches with prestigious Blue Flag status have the highest water quality, minimal waste and good biodiversity – as well as being safe and accessible.

Bournemouth tops the list for most reports with 16, while 13 came from Croyde Bay in North Devon, and Polzeath in North Cornwall came third on the list.

Polzeath is a favourite spot for a number of celebrities, as well as former PM David Cameron who bought a £2million home nearby in 2017.

He has been frequently pictured at the beach with wife Samantha – while the likes of Princes William and Harry often surfed there growing up.



Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and TV chef Gordon Ramsey have also made homes in the area.

Other beaches ranking highly on the list include Rest Bay in Porthcawl, Wales, with 12 reports of illness, while Exmouth in Devon has 10, and Portreath, North Cornwall, has nine.

The top 10 is rounded off with Saunton Sands in North Devon, Swanage Central in Dorset and Ogmore in Barry, Wales, all with eight reports – and Woolacombe Village, North Devon, with seven.

However, the location which resulted in the most days off work at 1,014 is St Mary’s Bay in Kent.

SAS, which campaigns against pollution on UK beaches, says sewage dumping is “making us sick” and has been ongoing for “decades”.



Its latest stats show water companies across England recorded 2,487 pollution incidents in 2024 alone – amounting to a whopping 4.7million hours.

Jo Morley, head of campaigns at SAS, told the Mirror: “Thousands of water users are reporting this to us, and this is likely just the tip of the iceberg.

“From gastroenteritis and ear infections, to weeks off work and hospitalisations. This is a public health crisis.”

She added: “There is no official Government data, and no legal protections for people using the water.”

The Sun has approached SAS for more information.

News.title: Devastated dad of teen, 16, reveals moment he realized she’d vanished in middle of night as eerie vid shows last moments
News.content:
FATHER'S ANGUISH Devastated dad of teen, 16, reveals moment he realized she’d vanished in middle of night as eerie vid shows last moments

THE father of a missing teenager has revealed the heart stopping moment he realized she had vanished in the middle of the night.

Sophia Cover, 16, was last seen leaving her home in Naples, Florida, in the dead of night on July 31.



Eerie home surveillance footage from the property in Golden Gate Estates shows the moment the teen creeps out of the home at 12:45am wearing a hoodie with the hood over her head.

A bag appears to be slung over a shoulder as she feels around in the dark to find her way, using no light to see where she is going.





“Someone has my daughter,” her heartbroken father Richard told Gulf Coast News, adding that he believes she is in trouble and was coerced to leave the new family home.

“There is no way that she is going and putting me through this for five days…she is my buddy” he said through tears.

“I think that she left the house because someone either convinced her to, or promised her something and I think that she’s in trouble right now. I think someone has my daughter, is what I believe,” he added.

Richard recalled the moment he realized his daughter was missing when her dog started whining at around 6:15am and he walked around to find the pool bathroom door unlocked.



“Then I walked into her bedroom and she is nowhere to be found,” he said.

Richard, his girlfriend and their four children, including Sophia, had only moved to the area four months before she vanished, and she was due to return to high school in less than two weeks.

Desperate family members have taken to social media to beg Sophia to return home after it was discovered that her iPhone which she took with her had been turned off after the teen disappeared, her aunt revealed on Facebook.



“Every minute without her feels unbearable. We miss her so much and just want to know that she’s safe,” Richard wrote online.

“There isn’t a single day that goes by that I don’t think about you. I miss your smile, your laugh, and hearing your voice. Home just isn’t the same without you here.

“I’m not giving up on you…I love you with all my heart, Sophia. I’ll always be your dad, and I’ll always be waiting for you with open arms. Please come home.”

She is described as five foot seven, 115 pounds with long brown hair and brown eyes.

According to her father, she took a bag filled with clothes, a new pair of Nike sneakers, and a hair straightener.



A multi-agency investigation has been launched but officials say there are currently no leads.

Anyone with any information regarding her disappearance is urged to contact the Collier County Sheriff’s Office at 239-252-9300.

News.title: Moment quivering stalker is found under bedframe by armed cops after hitting 3 people while speeding through city centre
News.content:
THIS is the moment a quivering stalker was found under a bedframe by armed cops after hitting three people while speeding through a city centre.

Joseph Wicks, 27, was arrested and charged with a string of offences including an incident where he struck pedestrians with a car in Colchester, Essex.



Footage shows the moment special officers break down a door before Wicks is discovered cowering under a bed.

One armed cop can be heard saying: “Listen Joe, the game is up mate.”



Police had identified Wicks as the driver of a Fiat 500 which mounted the pavement and hit three people outside a night club in the early hours of November 30 last year.

That morning, he had driven aggressively and dangerously around the city centre, speeding the wrong way down narrow roads and running red lights.

After he hit the pedestrians, who fortunately suffered no serious injuries, Wicks fled the scene and abandoned his car.

As cops worked to trace his finger prints, Wicks launched a campaign of stalking and harassment against a woman.



He reportedly attended her address on May 8 of this year and acted aggressively, banging on her front door, demanding entry and shouting and swearing.

Wicks returned to his parked van and a man who approached him reported seeing a baseball bat and a handgun in the vehicle.

The thug left the area, but continued to bombard his victim with calls and texts.

Due to the report of a potential firearm, specially trained armed officers from Essex Police Force Support Unit began enquiries at a number of addresses linked to Wicks.

The following day, cops tracked down the van and recovered the baseball bat, but no firearm was found.



On May 11, armed police executed a warrant to arrest Wicks at an address in Colchester.

Multiple people in the home denied seeing the offender, but officers searched the property and found him hiding underneath a bed.

Wicks was arrested and charged with a number of offences, including dangerous driving, stalking and three counts of attempting to cause actual bodily harm.

He admitted to all charges put forward apart from possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause fear of violence, which he denied.

The offender was jailed for four years and six months at Ipswich Crown Court on Friday July 31, and disqualified from driving for two years and six months.



Inspector Tom Stokes, of Force Support Unit, said: “In this case, officers were tasked with locating and arresting a man linked to a series of serious offences, including dangerous driving which put members of the public at risk and a report involving what was believed to be a firearm.

“When information suggests there may be a weapon involved, we must plan carefully and act decisively.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The professionalism shown by the officers involved meant they were able to safely enter the address, carry out a thorough search and locate Wicks despite efforts to conceal himself.

“Their actions ensured a high-harm offender was brought before the courts and held accountable for his actions.”

News.title: I’ve looked Tupac Shakur’s ‘killer’ dead in the eye – here’s why his murder trial is set to be bigger than OJ Simpson’s
News.content:
I’VE reported on Tupac Shakur’s infamous murder for the past decade but nothing prepared me for when I came face to face with his self confessed killer and “Godfather Of Compton.”

Sitting in court room 12B at the 8th Judicial District Court of Clark County Court in Las Vegas, murder suspect Duane “Keefe D” Davis glared furiously at me in the public area.





It was October 4 2023 and Davis was in court accused of the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, who died on September 13, 1996, aged just 25, after a Las Vegas drive-by shooting.

The murder has remained unsolved for thirty years – but this could soon change, with Davis landing himself in court after allegedly confessing to the crime.

And as I looked at him across the courtroom with no physical barrier between us, I genuinely wondered whether he was ready to leap out of the defendants’ area, he looked so angry.

Aggrieved that the media had reported on his multiple confessions of being the “shot caller” for Tupac’s death, he seemed ready to deliver the “beating” he had famously boasted about in his memoir and to friends for years.

Thankfully, a team of well trained court security and police officers – along with his leg shackles and handcuffs – seemed to deter his rage from spilling over.

Davis’ screwed-up facial fury has never waned. Even in the most recent court hearing in July, he locked eyes with me with a stare appearing to be be livid at simply reporting his own boasts and taped admissions to police officers.

Over several court hearings, Davis’ loathing of authority have seen him lash out verbally with nonsensical rants at prosecutors, scream about unfounded claims of police brutality and then accuse media of stopping him obtaining bail.





In recent weeks with new lawyer Mike Sanft in his corner, Davis’ temper has cooled.

His previous lawyer Carl Arnold described him as a doting grandfather, who’s happiest tending to roses in his garden, having left his criminal past behind.

It was a far cry from how Davis’ own boasts of the last decade – where he has claimed in media interviews, his memoir Compton Street Legend, and even in police interviews – that he was the key man in the assassination.

Now starting on August 10, a jury will have to decide if Davis’ should spend his life in prison for being the “shot caller” overseeing Compton Crips hunting Tupac and firing the deadly gun on September 7 1996.

Davis has pled not guilty to the crime – claiming that he invented every confession for “fame and fortune” and that his lies “are his first amendment right”.

According to his new lawyer, Davis will not give evidence to the jury and judge Carli Kierny.

Sanft insists that prosecutors have no firm proof that Davis was even in Vegas on the night of the killing, as no murder weapon, vehicle connected to the crime or ballistics linked to Davis have been found.



Since his criminal case begin in September, I have looked into the eyes of Davis, watched him make angry outbursts in court and seethe at prosecutors and glare angrily at media for reporting his wacky behaviour.

Davis is clearly aggrieved that he was arrested – despite his confessions – and livid that he has been in remand for nearly three years.

His initial reaction when he was arrested in 2023 was far cockier, insisting: “I don’t give a s***””, even telling a Metro police officer that this criminal matter is the “biggest case in Las Vegas history”,

However his gangster OG swagger initially disappeared as he turned into a dejected forlorn figure, who raged as prosecutors outlined his case during many hearings.

At times he sunk into his chair, clearly angry at his then-attorney Carl Arnold and appearing to mouth verbal profanities at prosecutors, Marc DiGiacomo and Binu Palal.

During an August 2024 hearing Davis hit breaking point, talking over Arnold and shouting at the judge that he feared dying after alleging he was beaten up in his cell.

In an extraordinary moment, he alleged that two correction officers injured him in his cell and that the district attorneys somehow orchestrated the attack.

The vein on the left side of his bald scalp visibly swelled and his forehead had beads of sweat rolling while he glared venomously at Palal and DiGiacomo. His claims went unproven.



After failing to convince a judge the source of his $750k bail money was legitimate, Davis stared angrily at me and other local media members in the public area claiming “these motherf*****s” were responsible for his time behind bars.

Adding to Davis’ criminal woes, former friends have shared some brutal truths including: “that guy is just stupid” and “he still takes no responsibility for admitting to this crime and finding himself up for murder.”

Another source served up this damning insight: “Davis is a f*****g moron.

“Nobody from law enforcement was interested in him until he started going on TV, YouTube and doing a book boasting about what a badass and gangster he is. I got no sympathy for that dumb mofo.”

Davis gave two interviews on tape to both LAPD and Las Vegas Metro Police admitting the crime in 2008 and 2009.

In those interviews, Davis claimed he and three Southside Crips associates Terrence “Bubble Up” Brown (driver), Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson and DeAndre “Dre” Smith, went hunting for Tupac.

They were out for “revenge” after Tupac beat up Anderson in the MGM Casino earlier following a Mike Tyson fight.

Davis said nephew Anderson fired the lethal rounds from their white rented Cadillac at a red light junction of East Flamingo and Koval Lane.

Tupac was taken to UMC clinic in a coma, with fatal gunshot wounds in his torso, lungs and groin, and passed away six days later.



On the tapes, Davis named Sean “Diddy” Combs, currently serving a four year sentence for sex trafficking, as one of the motivating factors behind his killing.

Combs was dragged in the case, because Davis claimed to police twice that the rapper offered him $1million to take out Tupac and Knight.

Combs has always vehemently denied any involvement in the Ghetto Gospel artist’s death, which now aids Davis’s case.

Combs’ long term rival – Death Row Records and Dr Dre’s ex boss Suge Knight – drove Tupac in his BMW.

For three decades Knight, who is serving a lengthy sentence for murder, has told multiple differing stories about the crime to media outlets.

However he has never appeared under oath in a courtroom to detail what – and more importantly who – he saw that night.

Both the prosecution and defence have considered Knight’s testimony given he is the only living direct eyewitness, aside from Davis, to the crime – following Brown, Anderson and Smith’s deaths.



Knight has made extraordinary conflicting comments in recent years citing that Davis “is innocent”, Anderson never fired at him and even that Tupac is alive living in Cuba.

In a recent podcast Knight promised to beat up Davis in person over efforts to have him appear in this case. It’s uncertain if he will be called up as a witness – or by which side.

TV cameras are expected to capture the fate of Davis, who faces life in prison if found guilty for his role in the murder of Shakur, as in Vegas being an accessory to a murder carries the same punishment as the perpetrator.

In three years, Davis’ legal strategy has been nothing short of extraordinary.

His defense, explained through several different lawyers, is effectively: “I am a liar – don’t believe what I said about Tupac…but believe me now.”

In unusual interactions, Davis’ former lawyer Carl Arnold detailed his successful criminal enterprises, including a multi million dollar West Coast narcotics network and deals with the Colombian cartel – but says he was not in Vegas the night of the murder.

The murder trial is set to include a wild cast of world famous witnesses and key figures.



Mob James – a once feared Compton gang enforcer and bodyguard of Snoop Dogg and Tupac who now counsels kids to steer clear of gang life, says he saw Davis outside of a nightclub close to the murder site.

Reggie Wright Junior is another well known figure from 1990s hip hop scene given he was the ex head of security for Death Row Records.

Famous street king and Southside Crip drug dealer Dirt Rock, real name Devonta Lee, will offer bombshell insight into the night of the killing.

Lee was a roommate of the late Smith, who he claims boasted about murdering Tupac, with Anderson.

Respected Los Angeles retired detective Greg Kading will appear as a witness given his intel led to Davis volunteering to confess to the murder.

Kading, who has won a Medal of Valor, spent three years digging into Tupac and Biggie Smalls’ murders, later penning a successful book on his probe called Murder Rap.

Another potential witness is acclaimed TV producer Mike Dorsey – owner of the popular true crime YouTube channel The Murder Rap, which focuses on the Tupac and Biggie homicide cases.

Retired Vegas police officer Chris Carroll is likely to be called to confirm holding Tupac moments before he slipped into a coma following the shooting.

The rapper’s famous last words to Carroll were “f*** you” when asked who committed the crime.

Tupac, Davis, Suge and Diddy have many star connections too from their past.



Ex girlfriends and close female pals of these men included J-Lo, Madonna, Cameron Diaz and Yung Miami and Lil Kim.

Other stars in their orbit included Snoop Dogg, Dre Dre, Easy E, Vanilla Ice and Jewell.

Rap and hip hop historian Dorsey acknowledged this case as the “craziest celebrity trial in US history”.

Dorsey said: “You start with an icon like Tupac and what was arguably the most famous unsolved murder in history until an arrest was made in 2023.

“Then you add a potential Diddy connection, considering all the legal issues and scandals he’s endured in recent years, plus a notorious figure like Suge Knight who’s serving a 28-year prison sentence for voluntary manslaughter.

“Combine that with Davis D, who has publicly admitted his role in this homicide multiple times; you’re going to have a string of interesting characters appearing as witnesses including former gang members and gang cops.

“I agree with one of Davis’ former attorneys: this case is bigger than the OJ Simpson trial.”

News.title: Cop killers, grooming gang members & cruel mum who allowed baby to die among 1000s of lags who could be released early
News.content:
COP killers, historic paedos – including grooming gang members – and an evil mum who turned a blind eye before her baby died are among the lags who still could be freed early as part of Labour’s soft justice scheme.

Thousands of dangerous offenders will soon be walking UK streets despite Andy Burnham‘s attempts to U-turn the government plans after nationwide outrage.



Under the new Sentencing Act, which received royal assent in January, a swathe of prisoners were set to be released from September in a bid to ease overcrowding.

However, the new PM paused the scheme last month as he ordered a major Ministry of Justice (MoJ) review to identify any grooming gang members who could be eligible for early release.



But it is set to resume instead on October 1 – with thousands of sex offenders, domestic abusers and killers still to see their sentences drastically reduced by two thirds.

Burnham has expressed his frustration that he can only block the release of those serving time for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming convictions.

He said this week: “The truth is I wanted to go even further. I know there will be concerns about who will still be released early for other offences.”

Top lawyer Marcus Johnstone told The Sun: “The early release scheme will undoubtedly result in many more dangerous violent and sexual offenders on our streets.



“These offenders will be released back into the areas where their crimes were committed, possibly without notice or warning to their victims.”

He said releasing criminals halfway through their sentence is already considered by many victims as “an affront to justice” but now the UK will be seen as the “go to” destination to commit serious crimes.

He added: “Little chance of being detected but, if caught, little time behind bars.”

Mr Johnstone – MD of PCD Solicitors – said: “Our prisons are full. We are now releasing dangerous violent and sexual offenders early simply to make space so we can then send new violent and sexual offenders to prison.

“We will then release them early so we can sent more new offenders to prison. One out, one in.”



It comes as the Police Federation threatened the Government with possible legal action over the potential release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

In response, the PM is reported to be preparing to explore “explore every option” to keep Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers in prison despite previously saying he was powerless to stop their release, a government source told The Sun.

A final decision has yet to be made but Whitehall officials are looking at a special exemption for the pair who killed the hero cop, The Telegraph reported.



Meanwhile, five men from Bradford sentenced to a combined 35 years in prison last October for abusing a girl in care from the age of 13 during the early 2000s are among those whose offences are not currently included on the exclusion list.

It’s emerged that offences committed before a change to the law in 2003 will not be covered, regardless of when the offender was brought to justice.

Mohammed Imran Akram, Safraz Ahmed Latif, Wajid Hussain, Mohammed Naheem and Nadeem Ali were all found guilty on various counts of indecent assault and each sentenced to between six and eight years in prison.

Cruel mum Dana Carr, now 27, who turned a blind eye to the horrific abuse Michael Daymond inflicted on little Maya Chappell, could still also be let out early once the scheme resumes in a matter of weeks.



Carr was locked up for nine years in 2023 after being convicted of allowing the death of a child and child cruelty.

Maya’s devastated family were left fuming after discovering Carr could have been back on the streets by Christmas just three years into her sentence, branding it as a “disgusting joke”.

They expressed their delight when Burnham paused the scheme – but Carr could still be released early when it resumes.

Driving offences will not be blocked from early release – with Calvin Buckley devastated to hear Adil Iqbal – who killed his pregnant partner Frankie Jules-Hough in a 93mph motorway crash in 2023 – is set to see his sentence reduced.



“To kill somebody and to have your sentence reduced is just not right. Our justice has been taken away,” Calvin told the BBC.

Vicki Crawford, who was 14 when she was attacked in the 1980s, found out this month that her attacker will also be eligible for early release, despite being jailed in 2024.

She told The Times: “They’ve taken a lazy approach and not looked at what offences mean in real terms. They don’t class mine as serious enough. It’s a total double standard to do that to victims of historical sex offences, because it’s an easy out for them.

“It still feels like yet another betrayal. I’ve had a lot of them throughout the justice system in my own case.



“It scares me that there are going to be a lot of other people that don’t fully understand why they’ve been excluded.”

As part of the scheme, up to 363 offenders convicted of manslaughter could be back on UK streets by 2029 after serving as little as one third of their sentence, according to new analysis of official data.

The figures, reported by the Daily Mail, were compiled by the Tories using stats from the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) to form estimates on the number of killers who received an immediate or “standard determinate sentence”.

Under Labour’s Sentencing Act, passed this year, some killer lags could be released after serving 33 percent of their jail term if they were handed less than four years – providing they’ve shown good behaviour.



Petition to stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper's killers Aileen O'Connor, Thames Valley Police Federation Chair, has launched a petition demanding a stop to the early release of PC Harper's killers. The petition has already soared past 100,000 signatures after it was posted earlier on Tuesday. Hundreds more have taken to the comments to show their support after the Government’s decision on PC Harper’s killers sparked outrage across the country. O’Connor said in the petition that she was “absolutely outraged” at both the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, and Justice Secretary. She challenged them to “explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release”. The decision, she said, “is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family”. O’Connor added they have watched a “justice system that they trusted” fail to recognise the sacrifices made by those who “serve and protect the public”. It sends a “deeply troubling message” about the value the Government places on people who have made those sacrifices, she continued. O’Connor concluded with a defiant message, saying: “I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.” To sign the petition click here.

While those given four or more years must serve half their sentence.

Ministers plan to release 5,000 offenders from prison starting in October as part of the scheme to reduce jail overcrowding.

More than 9,000 domestic abusers are also set to be freed annually within three years as part of the new plans.

The Tory analysis shows 9,371 of these criminals could be out of prison by the end of this Parliament in 2029.



Labour, under Sir Keir Starmer and now Burnham, has already freed more than 70,000 inmates from prison under its existing early release scheme – SDS40 – launched weeks after the party’s 2024 election win.

SDS40 doesn’t apply to those convicted of manslaughter, or other violent crimes, if lags were sentenced to four years or more – but does apply to those serving more than four years, though with some exceptions.

But affords even more liberal reductions for many offenders – with Labour adamant the moves are necessary to reduce prison overcrowding.

The Government has blamed the Tories for failing to put adequate infrastructure in place to properly contain a larger number of prisoners.



PM Burnham – who was sworn into 10 Downing Street on July 20 – announced this week that rapists and child sex offenders would not be eligible for early release as part of the scheme.

In a statement, No 10 said it would ensure that “everything possible is being done so that vile groomers are dealt with in the way their victims deserve”.

But officials warned that the government may lack the legal mechanism to block their early release.

PC Harper’s widow, Lissie Harper, told Burnham: “You should be ashamed.”

She described the planned early release of two of his killers as a “punch in the gut”.



And she has thrown her weight behind an online Thames Valley Police Federation petition to stop his killers being freed.

PC Harper died while investigating the theft of a £10,000 quad bike near Sulhamstead, Berks, in August 2019.

Bowers and Cole, then 17, tried to escape in a car driven by Henry Long, 18.

The 28-year-old officer’s ankles got caught in a heavy-duty tow strap and he suffered ­catastrophic ­injuries as he was dragged in the dark for more than a mile at an average 43mph.

Bowers and Cole were sentenced to 13 years in July 2020, meaning they could be released by October.



Long, the main perpetrator, who pleaded guilty, got 16 years and is not eligible for release under the scheme.

Other child sex offenders who may fall within the scope of the scheme include Kevin Pritchard, 65, who abused three girls aged under 12 between the 1970s and 1990s and was given a 13-year sentence in 2021.

Other potential candidates for early release include Andrew Fox, guilty of offences against two boys in the 1990s and early 2000s – though not investigated until 2017 before being handed a seven-year sentence in 2024.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Piano teacher Andrew Roberts, who abused two boys under 10 at an East Sussex boarding school between 1964 and 1974 was sentenced to six years in 2024.

The Sun has approached the Ministry of Justice for comment.

News.title: Reality TV star, 22, arrested after parading naked in Moscow faces up to six years in jail amid Putin’s porn crackdown
News.content:
A RUSSIAN reality tv star is facing up to six years behind bars amid Vladimir Putin’s war on porn.

Trash blogger Anastasia Bragina is the latest victim of the dictator’s crackdown, after she filmed herself parading naked through Moscow.



Anastasia, 22, recorded the stunt while declaring that she wanted to “break free from all limitations” but was instead put in cuffs.

She is a former contestant on Russian reality TV show Dom-2 (House-2).



The programme sees contestants try to build a house and find romantic partners at the same time.

Anastasia is the fifth prominent Russian influencer to face pornography charges in Putin’s crackdown on OnlyFans and other “Western platforms”.

She was arrested after being accused of “dissemination of pornography among children” by Ekaterina Mizulina, the high-profile head of Russia’s Safe Internet League and a member of Putin’s Civic Chamber.

There were rumours that Putin and Mizulina, 41, were in a romantic relationship two years ago.

Mizulina reported Anastasia to the Interior Ministry and Investigative Committee.

She complained: “The blogger has apparently completely lost her mind and decided to stage a performance in Moscow — she went for a naked walk around the city.



“In that state she walked the streets and entered cafés. Everything was, of course, filmed on video.”

Anastasia was initially fined £38 and held for 14 days.

But just ten seconds after being freed, she was rearrested on more serious charges of “distribution, display, or public demonstration of pornography through social networks, messaging apps, or websites”.



It could see her jailed for six years, although Mizulina is demanding charges that could double the sentence.

She said: “The trash-blogger is publicly corrupting children on her platforms, constantly appearing naked in video circles and also giving schoolchildren various pieces of depraved advice.”

Mizulina – who is spearheading Putin’s crackdown – graduated from London’s School of Oriental and African Studies in 2004.

Her philosopher father Professor Mikhail Mizulin, 71, is a leading academic in Moscow, and her mother Yelena is a pro-Putin senator in the Russian parliament.

Mizulina advocates censorship on the Internet, fines and other sanctions against the media and social networks.



It comes as a string of high-profile Russian content creators have been detained on similar charges.

OnlyFans star Sofya Vershinina, 21, dodged prison but was handed a £45,000 fine and three-year internet ban after being convicted of producing and distributing explicit online videos.

Another model and influencer Diana Shurygina, 27, is currently custody awaiting trial.



Sources say the case against her centres on “intimate content” she allegedly sold to paying subscribers on OnlyFans.

Anastasia Ovsyannikova, 24, known under the stage name Nastya Kholod, was also held on suspicion of illegal production and circulation of pornographic materials.

She and Diana made adult content for OnlyFans together and separately.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alleged German producer of X-rated videos Ludwig Krichker was also detained and his residence was searched with equipment seized.

As Putin continued to take on the Russian porn industry, legal experts warn the net could widen even further to enforce so-called “traditional values”.

News.title: Multiple passengers injured after tourist bus flips over into ditch in horror crash as four rushed to hospital in Norway
News.content:
BUS SMASH TERROR Multiple passengers injured after tourist bus flips over into ditch in horror crash as four rushed to hospital in Norway

MULTIPLE people have been left injured after a tourist bus flipped over into a ditch in a horror crash as four are rushed to hospital.

A total of 34 people were on board the German tour bus when it came off the E6 in Namdalen, Norway.



Two were rushed to Namsos and another two to Levanger, where the highest level of alert was declared and extra personnel were called in.

The terrifying crash unfolded on Saturday morning when the bus suddenly swerved and veered to the right.



It then careered off the road before turning into a ditch.

Shocking pictures from the scene show the bus lying on its right side, with its doors jammed and windscreen partially shattered.



Dramatic footage captures the horrifying moment the vehicle suddenly veers across the road before plunging into the ditch and flipping over.

Emergency services raced to the scene, with a rescue helicopter also scrambled as crews rushed to deal with the wreckage.

Despite the violent smash, no one was trapped inside the bus, operations manager Siv Mamork said.

Police said both drivers will remain at the crash scene until the stricken bus is recovered.



One lane was reopened in the afternoon, but the second remains closed as the recovery operation continues.

Traffic is being diverted around the crash site while crews work to clear the wreckage.

Mayor Elisabeth Vollmo BjÃ¸rnhusdal of the municipality of Namsskogan said a crisis team had been set up following the dramatic crash.

News.title: Victims urged to come forward as police accused of 'litany of failures' over murderer and rapist
News.content:
Police have urged more victims of Simon Levy to come forward, as London's victims' commissioner said a "litany of failures" had allowed him to kill two women and rape a third.

Andrea Simon called for a review on the "failure to monitor him appropriately" when the 40-year-old was known to police as a sexual predator.

British Transport Police said women who recognised Levy as their attacker should report it, while the Met Police said it had investigated whether he had more victims, including further murders.

Meanwhile, the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) said a police constable is under investigation for gross misconduct, and a detective sergeant is facing a misconduct investigation.

On Friday, Levy was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third in London while he was being monitored by the Met Police for being a convicted sex offender. He had previously committed a string of sex attacks.

Levy is due to be sentenced on Wednesday.

News.title: Widdecombe police reopen investigation into incident at Farage's home, BBC understands
News.content:
Counter-terrorism police investigating the killing of Ann Widdecombe have reopened an inquiry into an incident at Nigel Farage's south London home, the BBC understands.

It is understood to relate to what the Reform UK leader described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London said it was looking into an "attempted burglary" at a property as part of the Widdecombe murder investigation, but did not confirm the home was linked to Farage or why it might be connected to the killing of the former MP.

CTP London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation into the Farage incident was handled.

Police said at the time that "damage was caused to a door but nothing was stolen".

Both CTP London and the Metropolitan Police were involved in enquiries. No arrests were made and the investigation was closed.

But on Friday, CTP London said a new line of inquiry had been identified that was not "pursued by them at the time".

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had "decided to independently investigate the conduct of a Counter Terrorism Policing London staff member following a referral received earlier [on Friday]".

A statement continued: "The conduct relates to an allegation the individual failed to identify and pursue a line of enquiry relating to an attempted burglary reported in April 2025."

CTP London said it would "full engage" with the watchdog's investigation, adding: "The victims and families in both investigations have been updated today, and we continue to support them."

Ann Widdecombe, the 78-year-old former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, was found dead at her home in Devon last month with serious injuries.

Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, was later charged with her murder.

Kerry was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on 11 July, before being additionally arrested on 13 July on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe had served as Tory MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

News.title: Fifth heatwave of the year likely next week as temperatures could hit 35C
News.content:
Temperatures on Saturday will begin to climb above average again, reaching the mid- to high 20s Celsius in most of England and Wales.

It will be cooler in Scotland and Northern Ireland at 17 to 21C with more cloud, a bit of rain and a blustery wind.

By Sunday and into next week temperatures will rise even further with many parts of the UK exceeding their heatwave threshold temperature of 25 to 28C, depending on location.

With this hotter weather expected to last well into the week, many locations will have the three consecutive days needed to declare the fifth widespread heatwave of the year.

It has already been a remarkable summer in the United Kingdom with multiple records broken.

July has been the sunniest month on record for the UK, as well as the driest July on record for England and Wales.

There have so far been 33 days this year when temperatures have exceeded 30C in the UK. Next week, it is likely the record of 34 days, set in 1995, will be broken.

For the first time ever, a temperature of 35C has also been recorded somewhere in the UK on the three consecutive months of May, June and July.

It is possible August will join that list by the end of next week as some forecast models suggest 35C in central and south-east England.

News.title: Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged 'lover' when he was general secretary
News.content:
Gianni Infantino's alleged lover was given a severance payment over the affair by Uefa while he was its general secretary, according to a Daily Telegraph investigation, external.

A spokesman for the now Fifa president was reported to have told the paper Infantino "strongly denies these categorically untrue allegations".

Uefa, for whom Infantino was general secretary from 2009 to 2016, issued a statement confirming "a departure payment was made to the individual in question".

The allegations come as Infantino fights for his future as Fifa president following his aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

BBC Sport has contacted Fifa and Infantino for comment.

The Telegraph reported that Uefa paid a six-figure sum to the woman, who had an alleged relationship with Infantino, who is married, during his time at European football's governing body.

"Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory," a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph.

"No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino's behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved."

Uefa confirmed a payment was made to the woman in question and that it covered the fees for her to complete an MBA course at a local business school.

It said all payments were in line with regulations at the time, but those regulations have since been tightened and "reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation".

News.title: Watch: Moment opposition MP throws eggs at Kosovo's acting PM
News.content:
An opposition MP, Time Kadrijaj, threw eggs at Kosovo's acting Prime Minister Albin Kurti during a plenary session on Saturday.

The Alliance party MP hurled at least four eggs in Kurti's direction before lawmakers and police officers intervened.

Chaos unfolded after Kurti told Parliament he needed more time to hold talks with other parties before proposing a candidate for speaker following the June snap election.

News.title: I went for a full body MOT and the results came as a shock
News.content:
Annabel Mason-Thompson went for a Neko Health scan in September last year, knowing she had a suspicious-looking mark on her back - but it wasn't flagged by the technology.

"I felt a bit let down if I'm honest," the 50-year-old says. "Their AI scanner failed to pick up any of my four cancerous lesions.

"It was only when I went into the doctor's room after the scan and I pointed out my red mark did they take a look at it."

Further examination confirmed the mark was suspicious, so Neko Health contacted Annabel to say she would need treatment and wrote a letter to her private dermatologist to say the "lesion requires evaluation with a view to possible excision".

Her dermatologist found three more cancerous marks which needed urgent treatment.

"Luckily," she says, "they were all slow-growing basal cell carcinomas. I had to have two cut out and two taken off via cryotherapy."

Neko Health says "member safety and clinical excellence are at the heart of everything" it does. The company said its clinical team did identify a "lesion of concern" and it was reviewed by two of its dermatologists before a referral was made for potential treatment.

"We know that no one system is foolproof," Nilsonne says, "which is why we have multiple lenses - it is crucial that the technology and human expertise work together."

His company's latest data shows that of the 4,362 scans carried out on clients who visited Neko Health's Stockholm headquarters last year, 1.2% discovered life-threatening conditions such as melanoma and leukaemia. A further 4% spotted significant health conditions that required further treatment, and 1.2% flagged conditions that could be reversed such as pre-diabetic blood sugar levels.

While the figures are not representative of the population and only account for those who can afford to pay for this kind of preventive healthcare, Nilsonne says this is an indicator of how medicine should look in the future.

But GPs disagree. Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs (RCGP), says they haven't seen "convincing evidence" private broad screening tests "improve health outcomes".

She says the results from these private scans can also place an additional strain on the NHS as clients come back for further tests and potential treatment, even "where the findings prove to be clinically insignificant".

News.title: He's been frozen on Everest for 30 years, now 'Green Boots' may finally be coming home
News.content:
For 30 years, a dead body known as "Green Boots" has been lying in the snow, nestled under an overhanging rock, not far from Mount Everest's summit.

The lime mountaineering boots worn by an Indian climber who died in 1996 have been a grim trail marker for many climbers on their way up the world's highest peak ever since.

Now India is looking for a specialist high-altitude recovery team to undertake a complex and risky mission to retrieve what they say is Dorje Morup's body â arguably the most famous of the hundreds whose bodies have been left frozen on the mountain.

Warning: This story contains a picture of a dead body.

They hope they are on the cusp of returning his remains to friends and family who never gave up hope he'd come home.

"On some days, before I went to sleep, I would think that there'd be a knock on the door tonight and that when I opened, he would be there," Morup's wife told the BBC.

"When he comes home, I will ask him: 'Where were you all these years?'"

News.title: Digital cameras and wired earphones are back and 'a bit more real'
News.content:
Luckily I'm out with my photography-loving best friend, who helps adjust the settings on the camera and gets snapping while I'm otherwise engaged on the dancefloor.

The mere sight of us pulling out the camera and squinting through its tiny viewfinder draws attention â "I've not seen one of these in years", a man remarks.

He's right â digital cameras had their heyday in the late 1990s and early 2000s, just before smartphones took off.

There are currently 42 million active film camera users globally, more than a third of these aged 18â30 and largely influenced by social media trends, according to a market research report, external last year.

So why, when we're surrounded by more advanced tech here in 2026, are they seemingly making a resurgence?

For Lily Redman, a 26-year-old content creator from South Wales, digital cameras "capture a quality that my phone just can't replicate".

She's been taking one on nights out and to concerts and feels the flash on her phone "is grainy and too high definition" compared to the "more smooth" finished product on a digital camera.

"I think people are looking for a bit of grit or something that feels a bit more real," she says.

That may also explain why low exposure photos taken on iPhones and Androids â where people dodge ready-made filters to artificially crank down the exposure setting and produce a darker image â are also popular on socials right now.

With digital cameras offering an element of surprise when you plug in the memory card reader to your computer at home, digital cameras capture a moment in time.

"If I look back at photos my mum took when I was two, they look so old but when I look at photos I took five years ago, they look like they were taken yesterday," says Redman.

"Phone photos have warped our perception of time."

News.title: Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
News.content:
Thirteen days after Hannah Stephenson stayed a night in a Travelodge hotel, she is still itching with red lumps over her body - a nightmare she would not wish on her "worst enemy".

The 31-year-old from Bassingbourn had been out with friends in Cambridge and decided to book a one-night stay at the hotel on Newmarket Road on 26 July to save money instead of getting a taxi home.

The next morning, she woke up to a "horrible realisation", feeling itchy with red lumps over her body and blood spots smeared on the bedding â the tell-tale signs of bed bugs, she said.

A Travelodge spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson's experience and how distressing an incident like this can be."

Stephenson said a lovely evening with friends had turned into a horrible morning.

"It was just a lovely wholesome time of Cambridge sightseeing and pubs, and now it is tarnished by these bedbug bites," she said.

"It wasn't until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened."

News.title: Bristol Airport disruption a 'shambles' as flights restart
News.content:
Widespread disruption continues at Bristol Airport after a runway defect saw all flights suspended.

Hundreds of passengers were stranded after the airport's runway was closed from 18:00 BST on Friday until 08:00 on Saturday. While the runway has since reopened, the airport's website says the majority of flights are delayed or cancelled.

A spokesperson for the airport apologised for any inconvenience caused and advised passengers to check the status of their flight with their airline.

Dave Blackwell, travelling home from the Greek island of Rhodes, said it had been "a shambles" since his flight back to Bristol was diverted to Newcastle.

"We were in Rhodes Airport for three hours with no information. Now we have all been told our flight is going to Newcastle and then a five or six-hour bus ride - why Newcastle? How appalling," he said.

News.title: Strictly dancers Ola and James Jordan separate after 23 years of marriage
News.content:
Former Strictly Come Dancing stars James and Ola Jordan have confirmed they have separated after more than 20 years of marriage.

The former professional dancers were regulars on the show for several series after first featuring in 2006.

The couple's manager Vickie White confirmed the split, which was first reported by the Sun newspaper, external.

She said in a statement: "It is with great sadness that I can confirm that James and Ola began a trial separation some time ago.

"Their shared priority remains co-parenting their daughter, Ella, and they are committed to putting her wellbeing first.

"They would greatly appreciate your understanding as they navigate this difficult time."

Ola Jordan won the Open Polish Championship in 1999 when she was 17 years old and became James' dance partner shortly afterwards in March 2000.

She moved to England a month later and the pair got married in October 2003.

James appeared on Strictly from 2006 to 2013 while Ola appeared on the show until 2015.

Ola's celebrity partners included wildlife presenter Steve Backshall and Welsh sprinter Iwan Thomas, while James danced with former international gymnast and broadcaster Gabby Logan, as well as The One Show presenter Alex Jones.

News.title: Man guilty of fatal shooting of teen outside club
News.content:
A man has been found guilty of fatally shooting an 18-year-old outside a Wembley nightclub.

Tyrece Balcha was found with gunshot wounds outside the Crystal Club in Atlantic Crescent at about 05:30 GMT on 21 September 2025. He was taken to hospital, where he died four days later.

A jury at the Old Bailey found Ashley Wallace, 40, of Shenley Road, Southwark, guilty of murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

At the same trial, two men were found not guilty of murder. A woman was cleared of possession of a firearm, possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and perverting the course of justice. The jury did not reach a verdict on a fourth man.

CCTV footage showed that Balcha had been involved in an altercation inside the club before being followed outside and shot.

Wallace fled the scene in a vehicle and was arrested on 25 September after police traced the car to south-east London.

A revolver carrying Wallace's DNA was found inside the vehicle, and investigators established that the bullet recovered from the murder scene had been fired from the gun.

News.title: Siân Phillips to step back from acting aged 93 after memory issues
News.content:
One of Wales' most celebrated actresses, Dame SiÃ¢n Phillips, is stepping back from full-scale stage acting after experiencing memory issues during rehearsals.

The 93-year-old made the decision after struggling to remember her lines while preparing for a recent production, according to The Times.

However, Phillips said she would continue performing in smaller projects, including a production with Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Her career has spanned more than 80 years across stage, television and film.

Phillips told The Times she decided to stop taking on major stage productions after struggling to remember her lines during rehearsals for Atonement at Chichester Festival Theatre earlier this year.

According to the newspaper, she said she would continue performing in her show It's All Greek and is also due to appear in Samuel Beckett's Rockaby for Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Born in Betws, near Ammanford, Carmarthenshire, in 1933, Phillips grew up speaking Welsh before learning English by listening to the radio.

She began performing as a child, appearing on Welsh-language radio from the age of 11, before studying at the University of Wales and later winning a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.

She performed in radio productions such as The Archers and an adaptation of John le Carre's Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy, opposite Sir Alec Guinness.

Before her acting career took off, she worked for BBC Wales as a bilingual announcer and newsreader.

Phillips went on to become one of Britain's most acclaimed actresses, appearing in productions including Doctor Who, Calendar Girls, Dune, and I, Claudius.

She won a Bafta for her portrayal of Livia in the BBC's I, Claudius and received a Tony Award nomination for playing the title role in Marlene.

She was appointed a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2000 for services to drama, and then a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) in 2016.

News.title: Passengers 'stranded' at locked train station
News.content:
Translink has apologised after rail passengers were left stranded on a platform when a late-night train arrived into a station that was already shut for the night.

A group of about 30 customers were stuck on the platform at Newry Train Station for more than 45 minutes in the early hours of Saturday.

One of the passengers, Anne Greer, told BBC News NI it raised safety questions for the public transport company as the customers had no safe way to exit the station.

Translink said the firm was "looking into the incident" but added its train crew "remained with the passengers to ensure their safety while the issue was resolved".

The train was among a number of extra late-night services which are running to and from Belfast during the Fleadh Cheoil na hÃireann (Music Festival of Ireland).

It was scheduled to leave Belfast at 23:59 BST on Friday and it arrived in Newry at about 01:20 BST on Saturday.

"To our surprise the entire station was closed, so we couldn't exit," Greer said.

"So we're all trapped on the platforms for over 40 minutes."

She said the train crew "helped as much as they could, but there was nothing they could do".

"They were completely gobsmacked as to why they've arrived into a completely closed and locked train station."

Greer said she and other passengers tried to contact Translink but they could only find phone numbers for call centres which had also already closed for the day.

News.title: Man fundraises for stranger's dream trip
News.content:
A man has run almost 200 miles (321km) to pay for a stranger who has incurable cancer to go on a dream trip.

Giles Richards, from Yeovil in Somerset, completed 192 miles (310km) for Kayleigh Ewan to travel to Australia.

Earlier this year, the 36-year-old was diagnosed with metastatic cancer, which spread to her spine and liver. Doctors have told her the disease is incurable. Richards heard about Ewan through his partner and decided he wanted to help.

Ewan said she was really grateful to Richards, adding: "There's lots of places on my bucket list, but Australia is something I'd need time and money to plan and time is something I might not have."

News.title: Man charged after four killed in lamp-post crash
News.content:
A man has appeared in court charged in connection with a crash that killed four people.

James Diggle, 27, of Alundale Road in West Derby, Liverpool, faces four counts of aiding and abetting causing death by dangerous driving.

The charge follows the deaths of four men, Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26, who were killed when the black Seat Cupra Formentor they were travelling in hit a lamp-post on Liverpool Road in Huyton, just before 02:00 BST on 24 July.

Diggle did not enter a plea and was remanded into custody and will appear at Liverpool Crown Court on 7 September.

News.title: Alarming charts that reveal a planet in peril – as experts warn record-breaking heatwaves are just the start
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Britain’s record-breaking summer of heatwaves and life-threatening extreme temperatures could prove to be the coolest of our lifetime unless we double down on efforts to tackle the climate crisis, experts have warned.

Back-to-back hot spells, which saw the mercury peak at 37.7C (99.9F) in June, have so far led to nearly 3,000 deaths, half of England and the whole of Wales are in drought and a failure to heed decades of warnings to build climate resilience into our supply chains has left the UK facing food shortages.

The news overseas is even more alarming, with unprecedented wildfires burning thousands of square kilometres of land around holiday resorts in Spain and France, claiming 16 lives, while record-low water levels threaten Europe’s industrial heartlands on the Rhine and exposing lost Nazi warships on the Danube.

open image in gallery People walk on a path between the sun-scorched grass, turned yellow-brown by a lack of rain, in London’s Greenwich Park ( AFP/Getty )

And the picture is only set to intensify in the coming months as a record-breaking El Nino – a periodic warming of the Pacific Ocean – wreaks havoc with global weather systems, resulting in extreme rainfall in some parts of the world and devastating drought expected in others.

Experts warn that recent temperatures are no anomaly, with worse to come unless we ramp up efforts to phase out fossil fuels and invest more heavily in renewable energy sources.

“Unfortunately, this will be the least extreme climate we will experience in our lifetimes, certainly until we reach net zero emissions,” warned Hayley Fowler, professor of climate change impacts at Newcastle University. “We need to pressure politicians to do more and faster: to both rapidly reduce emissions and rapidly adapt our infrastructure to cope with more extreme weather.”

Prof Fowler’s comments come as recent analysis from Carbon Brief suggests that the combination of climate change and the super El Nino means that 2026 is set to be the warmest or second-warmest year on record – continuing a pattern of global temperatures increasing year after year.

“What we’re seeing now is exactly what climate scientists have been expecting for decades,” added Dr Friederike Otto from Imperial College London. “But the future is not predetermined: every tonne of carbon dioxide we avoid emitting reduces future warming and limits the severity of impacts.”

Gareth Redmond-King, international lead at the Energy & Climate Intelligence Unit think tank, echoed the concerns, saying: “This extremely hot and dangerous summer risks being one of the coolest for the rest of our lives if we keep burning coal, oil, and gas and destroying nature.

“But we should by no means feel that hope is lost, because we have a scientific pathway forward in the form of net zero that we need to be pursuing as urgently as possible if we want to bring our climate back into balance.”

Green Party leader Zack Polanski criticised the government for not doing enough to address the current climate, and urged the new prime minister to do more.

“This is the biggest threat to our country since the Second World War, but Andy Burnham is silent on it,” he said. “Worse than that, he’s considering restarting drilling in the North Sea – literally pouring fuel on the fire. Where is the action to meet the scale of the emergency?”

Fleur Anderson, Labour MP for Putney and chair of the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) on climate change, added: “We need to remember this period when the hot weather goes away. It is important now to join up government thinking between different departments to address all the different areas of our lives that are affected by climate change.”

Her comments come as the latest Met Office data shows that rainfall in July was the lowest it has ever been in records stretching back more than 250 years.

Ms Anderson also criticised the weakening climate consensus among mainstream political parties – with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch pledging to repeal the UK’s Climate Change Act – saying it was “extraordinary in the middle of these heatwaves for the parties to be differing on this”. She added: “I am so disappointed by the fact that the climate deniers seem to be winning the argument on the right in the face of not only scientific evidence, but also what is actually happening to our country.”

‘A new normal’ – that could get even worse

The Met Office has warned that the climate extremes of this summer are becoming “the new normal” for the UK – and the scientific evidence shows that things could get much worse unless global emissions continue to increase annually.

A report published by 160 scientists last year warned that even levels of global warming below 2C above the pre-industrial average could see climate systems that humans depend on for their survival – including the Amazon Rainforest, the Arctic permafrost, and the critical Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) – collapse. Scientists currently believe the world is at around 1.3C of warming.

open image in gallery A combine harvester crosses parched fields in Suffolk ( AFP/Getty )

In the UK, a report on climate preparedness published this summer by the climate APPG warned that the country is woefully underprepared for coming climate impacts. Some 6.3 million homes and businesses are at risk of flooding, and the cost of annual coastal flood damage is projected to increase two to three times by the 2080s, the report found.

By 2050, 92 per cent of existing homes could be suffering from overheating, while climate change and ecosystem collapse could mean the UK will struggle to maintain its food supply as early as 2030. Farmers have already warned that drought and heatwaves are likely to result in shortages, and they may have to stop growing certain vegetables.

Some 46 per cent of roads and 54 per cent of railways will also be at risk of flooding by 2050, the report finds, while direct impact costs from heatwaves over the next 50 years are set to be £64bn.

The cost of heatwaves has been particularly apparent in the wake of record-breaking fires in France and Spain this year. The cost of these fires, as well as those in other parts of Europe, is currently estimated at more than €3bn (£2.6bn).

Members of the APPG are calling on the government to move responsibility for climate resilience from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) directly to the Cabinet Office. “We have always planned historically for the cold in this country, but now we need to be worrying about the summer and overheating. We have to think differently about how we act to overcome these problems,” said Ms Anderson.

Speaking of wildfires that have also hit the UK this year, minister for climate transition Katie White said: “British firefighters are telling us they’ve never seen anything like this. With wildfires across Britain and Europe, we know we’re not waiting for climate change, we’re living through it.

“We must build our resilience, but critically, also cut the dirty emissions driving this.”

open image in gallery Burnt properties in the wake of record-breaking French wildfires ( AFP/Getty )

50 million people facing acute hunger

Over the next year, the world is set to experience a climate phenomenon known as El Nino, which is when unusually warm sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean lead to droughts or increased rainfall in different parts of the world.

This year’s “super” El Nino is set to be more severe due to a particularly high forecast temperature rise, as well as the climate crisis further exacerbating weather patterns. Analysis of El Nino forecasts from Carbon Brief suggests that the next is set to be by far the strongest on record.

In the UK, it risks heightening food shortages, as millions of small-scale farmers around the world who supply the UK with tropical fruits, cocoa, coffee and tea will struggle due to the disrupted weather patterns.

The consequences overseas are set to be catastrophic, with warnings that up to 50 million people could be pushed into acute hunger before the end of next year, the World Food Programme reported this week. It comes on top of geopolitical shocks, such as the war in Iran and aid cuts from wealthy countries, which are already piling immense pressure on the poorest parts of the world.

The past 10 years have already seen the number of people facing a food crisis double, according to the United Nations, with data also showing that foreign aid has fallen to a 10-year low.

As warnings about the climate crisis intensify, how Britons are feeling about the impacts is becoming clearer. A survey published by the think tank IPPR this year found that 81 per cent felt unprepared for the worst impacts of the climate crisis.

But experts stress that there remains every hope that the worst impacts can still be avoided and the world’s climate can be stabilised if we continue – as the vast majority of the world outside the US is doing – to roll out renewables and pursue a goal of net zero emissions.

“There is still time for us to avoid the worst impacts of climate change, and every fraction of a degree of avoided warming matters,” said Professor Elizabeth Robinson, head of the Grantham Climate Institute at the London School of Economics. “But this requires governments not just to stick to their commitments to reducing emissions, but to close the gap between commitments and policies that they are delivering.”

Dr Otto added: “This is a problem that is solvable. We know how to replace fossil fuels with renewables, we know how to lower demand, we know how to redesign cities and landscapes to be much better adapted to increasing floods, extreme heat and drought.

“Climate change is one of the defining challenges of our time, but it is also one where clear, informed decisions and sustained action can shape a much better future for all.”

The UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero has been approached for comment.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives and Liverpool agree Barcelona defender deal
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez while PSG’s Bradley Barcola is also on their list.

But Bruno Guimaraes has finally officially completed his £75m move from Newcastle United with the deal for the 28-year-old midfielder representing a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal’s title defence.

Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – though an initial offer of £38m has been rejected.

Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola’s side. The European champions may be willing to let them go, especially following Maghnes Akliouche signing from Monaco, while the Reds also look to have secured much-needed defender help with ex-Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo set for a loan deal, with an option to buy, at Anfield.

Elsewhere, Manchester United have added to their ranks by bringing in a teenage midfielder and they are exploring their options at left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.

Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below:

Manchester United face their highest-profile pre-season friendly of the summer as the tour of Scandinavia continues with a clash against double reigning Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain.

The Swedish city of Gothenburg plays host to the heavyweight clash, as Michael Carrick’s side look to build on a friendly campaign that has seen them win their previous two matches – including a 2-1 comeback win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm last time out.

PSG are an intimidating foe, although their star-studded squad will likely still be missing a number of players who played for France during their run to the semi-finals at the World Cup last month and they lost their previous friendly 3-0 to Mallorca. However, they will still provide a fascinating test as Carrick gears up for his first full season at the helm.

Lindsey Buckingham has revealed that he and former Fleetwood Mac bandmate Stevie Nicks have rekindled their friendship after years of a complicated relationship marked by professional and personal turmoil.

The pair — who famously dated from 1972 to 1976, breaking up during a turbulent recording session for the chart-topping 1977 album Rumours — have repeatedly gone through major periods of silence and estrangement, most recently after Buckingham, 76, was fired from the band.

The singer and guitarist was dismissed from the “Go Your Own Way” group in 2018, allegedly after Nicks, 78, gave him an ultimatum due to creative tension over a planned tour. Buckingham sued Fleetwood Mac for millions, eventually settling in December 2018. Nicks later denied having anything to do with his firing.

The two virtually went no contact in the following years, save for briefly speaking at Fleetwood Mac singer and keyboardist Christine McVie’s funeral in 2022.

Now, Buckingham said, “Stevie and I are talking all the time.”

open image in gallery Lindsey Buckingham was fired from Fleetwood Mac in 2018, setting off another lengthy period of silence between him and Stevie Nicks ( Getty )

open image in gallery Former Fleetwood Mac bandmates Stevie Nicks (left) and Lindsey Buckingham (right) have a complicated history marked by personal and professional turmoil ( Getty )

Speaking Thursday to E! News at Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood event, the Grammy-winning artist teased that “Fleetwood Mac has been working on a documentary.”

“I think the process of making that has been a very circular healing process for all of us,” Buckingham said.

Nicks and Buckingham’s surprise reconciliation began sometime last year with the re-release of their 1973 collaborative album, Buckingham Nicks.

The re-release fueled speculation of an impending reunion, though the two have remained coy about future joint musical endeavors.

“Next year should be a pretty interesting year,” Buckingham cryptically told E! News, “because I think quite a few things will reveal themselves.”

open image in gallery Buckingham said he and Nicks 'talk all the time now' ( AFP/Getty )

Weeks after the 2025 release of the remastered version of Buckingham Nicks, Nicks appeared on the music podcast Song Exploder to discuss the concept of the album’s hit track “Frozen Love.”

The song is about “two people that were in love, that had a lot of differences and saw the world slightly differently, but had this relationship that seemed to be like a gift,” Nicks said.

“I like to think of it as Wuthering Heights or Great Expectations — a modern day love affair, tragedies,” she added. “Because nobody really loves happy songs. Certainly I didn’t, and neither really did Lindsey.

“Our relationship was up and down and up and down and up and down and difficult, but at the same time, fantastic,” Nicks continued. “And what we were doing was so fantastic, that it was worth putting up with the trials and tribulations of a relationship that’s difficult.”

Content warning: This article contains an image of a dead body

The remains of an Indian climber frozen on Mount Everest for 30 years could finally be brought home to his wife, who says she will ask: “Where were you all these years?”.

An expert rescue team from India is preparing to embark on a risky mission to recover what they believe are the remains of Dorje Morup, a 48-year-old who died in a blizzard during his team’s descent from the summit of the world’s tallest mountain in May 1996.

It was only this year that he was identified as ‘Green Boots’, owning to the distinctive lime-coloured Koflach footwear worn by the late climber whose body has been preserved in the ice at some 8,500 metres for the last three decades.

Morup’s wife, Konchak Yangskit told the BBC that in all this time she and the family had never given up hope that her husband would one day return home.

“When he comes home, I will ask him: 'Where were you all these years?',” she said.

open image in gallery Authorities hope to send out a rescue mission to recover the body by September (Base camp pictured in 2024) ( AFP/Getty )

Now aged around 75, she told the broadcaster it had been difficult to believe what had happened as she never had confirmation.

“Even though we organised cremation prayers at home, my heart refused to believe he had died,” she said. “I didn't see his dead body, so it was difficult for me to believe it.”

Morup was part of a six-member expedition that was caught in a deadly storm near the summit in 1996 while trying to become the first Indian team to climb from the more challenging Chinese side.

It has long been believed that the remains of the climber known as Green Boots belonged to Tsewang Paljor, another climber killed on the expedition.

But testimony from survivors and the location of the last known radio contact with the climbers have led the authorities to believe that the body actually belongs to Morup.

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police in June made a fresh appeal for a specialist high-altitude recovery agency to bring down the body from the Tibetan side of the mountain so they could confirm the hypothesis with DNA testing.

open image in gallery Authorities believe the remains of the climber known as ‘Green Boots’ may belong to Dorje Morup, who died on a climb 30 years ago ( Wikimedia/@Maxwelljo40 )

If the body is confirmed to belong to Morup, the remains will be given back to his family, the BBC reports. Morup’s son, Punchok Dorjai, said the family would want to hold a funeral for him in Ladakh's capital, Leh.

Ms Yangskit told the broadcaster that the night before he left, her husband had promised to come back a hero and to make his country proud.

“He asked me to take care of the kids and come to the airport to greet him on his return,” she said.

The remains of ‘Green Boots’ lie inside Everest’s ‘death zone’ above 8,000m, where harsh conditions make recovery missions extremely dangerous.

At that altitude, temperatures can drop to -40C and air pressure is so low that the body struggles to take in oxygen.

On the Chinese side of the mountain, where the ‘Green Boots’ body is, there are fewer supports and steeper slopes, complicating efforts, Sherpa sources told BBC News Nepali.

open image in gallery Bright yellow tents in Mount Everest Base Camp in Nepal, in the Himalayas ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

The operation is expected to be further complicated by the need to coordinate with Chinese authorities to transport the body across the Tibet-Nepal border, fly it to Kathmandu, and arrange repatriation to India.

The Indo Tibetan Border Police wants the body to be returned by September, the BBC reports, and is now looking for mountain rescue Sherpa groups to volunteer their services.
