One Night Only director Will Gluck has revealed that he decided to scale back the amount of nudity in the romcom because he believes audiences are too uncomfortable with sex on screen.

The movie, starring Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner, is set in a bizarre world in which the U.S. has outlawed premarital sex for 364 days a year — leaving single people just 12 hours annually to hook up.

It has been widely compared to the horror franchise The Purge, in which violent crimes are legalised for one day per year.

In a new interview for Variety, Gluck, whose credits include Easy A and Anyone But You, said he studied empirical data about how Gen Z and Gen Alpha don’t want to see sex on screen, which informed how much intimacy was shown in the final cut of the movie.

“I cut out so much,” he said. “There was so much nudity in this movie that we shot on the streets.”

open image in gallery ‘One Night Only’ is set in a bizarre world in which the U.S. has outlawed premarital sex for 364 days a year — leaving single people just 12 hours annually to hook up ( Universal Pictures )

He decided to cut back on intimate scenes based on the audience’s reaction at test screenings for the movie.

“As we started to show it to audiences, we felt it takes you out of the movie. You’re engaged in the characters and what’s going on, and then you pan over and there’s two naked people having sex, and you watch the audience … it’s a physical thing,” he explained.

“So we just kept editing it out until we got a balance, and those comments went away.”

Gluck suggested that because people are constantly exposed to nudity and intimate scenes on their phones, it’s become “more of a private, intimate thing that people don’t want to see when they’re in a shared experience.”

“Whenever people now see nudity or very adult situations in a big theater, they get uncomfortable,” he reckoned.

open image in gallery Director Will Gluck said he ‘cut out so much’ nudity and intimate scenes from the final cut of the movie ( Universal Pictures )

The director added that he used an intimacy coordinator for romance scenes, and also cast real-life couples already familiar with each other to act in them.

“It was never like we met an extra and were like, ‘you guys are kissing.’ It was fun because there were married couples, people who broke up during the movie and people who became couples so they could do that,” he said.

Reviews for the movie have been polarized, with some critics describing the message of the film as being “strangely conservative” and even “fascist”.

In The Guardian, critic Benjamin Lee wrote that the film’s premise ought to be “the set-up for a grim Handmaid’s Tale-adjacent horror of a totalitarian state insisting extreme control over the body, but instead it’s used as the backdrop for a sunny meet-cute, screams of protest drowned out by a zippy Top 40 soundtrack”.

“If it sounds like far too much for a breezy summer romp to take on, then that’s because it most definitely is, an overstuffed yet undercooked soufflé that can’t quite, ahem, rise to the occasion…”

Others have been kinder to the film, with several outlets singling out the chemistry between the two leads for particular praise.

Variety’s Guy Lodge praised them as “two attractive, pleasingly grown-up leads whom you wouldn’t mind seeing get together; it’s set in New York City at its most invitingly balmy.”

South West Water (SWW) customers have slammed the water provider for introducing a hosepipe ban, demanding that their bills are cut during the ban after enduring years of sewage spills.

The ban came into force on Saturday, for all of its customers in Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset and Somerset and the Isles of Scilly.

In a post on Facebook, SWW said: “The decision follows one of the driest periods in recent years, with rainfall across the South West remaining well below seasonal averages over many months, and leading to the Environment Agency declaring half of England, including the South West, in drought.”

SWW has said people cannot use their hosepipes to water the garden, clean the car, patio or driveway, fill a paddling pool, swimming pool or hot tub, or clean walls, paths or windows.

Residents have responded with anger and a number said they would not be complying with the ban due to the price they pay for water.

Describing SWW as “incompetent”, Chris Rundle responded to an announcement about the ban on Facebook, writing: “So I take it South West Water will be cutting the bills to customers because they fail to supply the water they require.

“After all we pay South West Water for sewage treatment and all you do is dump that in the sea.

“Stop wasting the money we pay for water and sewage which is already the highest in the country on fat cat share holders and start spending it on infrastructure.”

open image in gallery St Mawes Castle in Cornwall. The country has been hit by hot weather all summer, leading to droughts in some areas ( PA )

In March, the BBC reported that data released by the Environment Agency showed that SWW was responsible for 46,164 spills in 2025, lasting 407,006 hours.

This was lower than 2024 but still the highest of any water firm in England, according to the BBC.

The same month, SWW pleaded guilty to a catalogue of pollution-related charges spanning six years across Devon and Cornwall.

At SWW’s sewage works near Bodmin, there were 336 illegal spills in the seven years to March 2020. Sewage discharged into the River Camel, which is a special area of conservation, and is a key habitat for Atlantic salmon, bullhead and otters, the Environment Agency said.

On 231 occasions between January 2016 and July 2021, untreated sewage was discharged on to Harlyn beach, a location popular with locals and tourists.

And in June, South West Water was handed a record fine of almost £2m for supplying water unfit for human consumption after a parasitic outbreak in Devon.

The company pleaded guilty to an offence under s70(1) of the Water Industry Act 1991 over the contamination of water by cryptosporidium, a parasite which causes sickness and diarrhoea.

Exeter Magistrates’ Court heard there were 537 probable or confirmed cases of cryptosporidiosis, with at least 10 people admitted to hospital.

Responding to Mr Rundle’s comment, SWW said there would be no reduction in bills during the ban, adding: “We treat 97 per cent of everything that enters our wastewater network.

open image in gallery Millions of people across England are under hosepipe bans ( Alamy/PA )

“Storm overflows discharge during hydraulic overload to prevent the flooding of homes, businesses and the streets.

“We have invested over £13 billion and are in a period of record investment, £3.2 billion from 2025-2030. We have seen a prolonged period of hot and dry weather, with record temperatures and rainfall well below seasonal averages over many months.

“Along with continuous high demand for water this has caused increasing pressure on reservoirs and available water resources.”

Sid Bulloch criticised water companies, including SWW, for a lack of construction of new reservoirs and the historic sale of them.

“We had one of the wettest winters on record with rain of biblical proportions”, he wrote. “And here we are with a hosepipe ban”.

Linda Grant made a similar point, writing: “Build more reservoirs and collect the rain fall that we had earlier in the year.”

Responding to Mr Bulloch, SWW said: “The reservoirs you mention being sold were service reservoirs, those that hold treated water for distribution to the local area. They were defunct and already replaced within the network.

“Holding reservoirs are those that capture raw water. These are incredibly costly in time, money and environmental impact.

“The primary reason more aren't built is the ecological cost. They cause large areas of habitat to be lost, heavily impacting wildlife and plants. They can also require the relocation of people living too close, due to the risk to property.”

Last April, SWW customers' average bills rose by 28 per cent, costing customers an additional 41 pence per day.

Lauren Chapman asked: “How much are our bills going to be reduced? As obviously if we aren’t allowed to use the water, I assume we won’t be paying for it.”

SWW responded by saying: “Water is continuing to be provided for essential use” as it reiterated it would not reduce charges.

SWW has been approached for comment.

News.title: Nigel Farage ‘horrified’ Ann Widdecombe murder detectives probing firebombing on his home
News.content:
The Way Back. Read our Privacy notice

Nigel Farage is “horrified” that counterterror police probing the alleged murder of Ann Widdecombe have reopened a year-old investigation into a “firebomb” attack at his house.

Officers said the incident, which The Telegraph described as a “lit incendiary device” being posted through the Reform UK leader’s letterbox, happened at an address in Greater London and was reported in April 2025.

The Metropolitan Police and Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London said they investigated an “attempted burglary”, but no arrests were made at the time and the case was closed pending any new lines of inquiry.

Mr Farage, who was not home at the time of the attack and found the damage when he returned home, earlier described the alleged attack as an “outright arson attempt”.

“Luckily it had burned itself out on the porch,” he told The Telegraph in April this year.

Reopening its probe, CTP London said it had identified a line of inquiry “which may have been relevant” but was “not identified and pursued by them at the time”.

The police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), is now investigating the “conduct” of a CTP London staff member, following an allegation that the employee “failed to identify and pursue a line of inquiry” related to the attempted burglary.

The Independent understands that Mr Farage is “horrified” that the attack on his home in 2025 is being reinvestigated by detectives investigating Ms Widdecombe’s murder.

A source said: “There has been a very serious policing error which is why [CTP] have referred themselves to IOPC, which is unprecedented.”

Richard Tice, deputy leader of Reform, said police forces have not been taking threats against his party’s figures seriously.

Mr Tice told The Telegraph: “Only recently have the authorities woken up to the abuse and intimidation I and other Reform MPs have had, despite plenty of real examples that we have provided.

“I was perhaps very lucky with one particular incident I faced last year. For too long, the threats we have faced have not been taken seriously.

“The fact that the police have referred themselves to the IOPC speaks for itself. They recognise that they’ve messed up.”

According to the newspaper, Mr Tice pressed his panic button at his house last Christmas after being approached by an aggressive man outside parliament. Officers then made an arrest.

Reform UK spokesperson and former Tory minister Widdecombe died on 8 July after she was hit over the head with a hammer 21 times at her home in Haytor on Dartmoor, Devon, a court heard.

Counterterror police investigating the death of former MP Ann Widdecombe have reopened a year-old probe into an alleged firebomb attack at Nigel Farage’s home ( PA )

Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged with her murder on 20 July. He has not yet entered a plea and has been remanded in custody until his next court appearance.

Reform UK MPs were given round-the-clock security protection, paid for by the party, after Widdecombe’s death over fears of similar attacks.

Mr Farage has previously raised concerns about MPs’ security, including his own, and said after her death: “And I do fear that for anybody in public life, or especially the political space, things have become even more dangerous to them.”

Confirming the reopened probe following the attack on Mr Farage’s home, senior national co-ordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, Vicki Evans, said: “As part of the ongoing investigation led by Counter Terrorism Policing South East into the murder of Ann Widdecombe, officers have reopened an investigation into an incident reported to police last year.

She added: “Given the nature of this matter and the significant public interest in the investigation into Ann Widdecombe’s death, it was of critical importance for us to provide this update.”

CTP London said it made a “mandatory conduct referral” to the police watchdog on Friday.

An IOPC spokesperson said on Friday: “We can confirm that the IOPC has decided to independently investigate the conduct of a Counter Terrorism Policing London staff member following a referral received earlier today.

“The conduct relates to an allegation the individual failed to identify and pursue a line of enquiry relating to an attempted burglary reported in April 2025.

“Counter Terrorism Policing London has been notified of our decision, and no further information is available at this early stage.”

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Sports.title: Football Wag had to move out of home after ONE NIGHT as she reveals what life in transfer window is really like
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL Wag Jessica Beaumont has revealed the brutal reality of life in the transfer window – including moving out of her dream home after just ONE night.

Jessica and footballer partner Owen Dale had only just bought their first house together when he was sent on loan more than 200 miles away to Portsmouth.



She was recovering from giving birth to their son Xavier at the time, and the move meant their brand-new home near her family was effectively abandoned.

Talking to BBC Sport, she explained: “Owen was on the phone to the manager and his agent while I was in labour. They waited for me to give birth and then he went out on loan pretty much as soon as I was out of hospital.”





The couple spent just one night in their new home before deciding the 10-hour round trip for Dale to see his newborn son was impossible.

“We spent one night in there, we hadn’t even unpacked.”

Jessica was forced to quit her job and put her law career on hold, while Dale chose their new Portsmouth home after viewing properties without her.

She continued: “I had Owen on the phone basically saying, ‘I’ve done a couple of house viewings. I’ve chosen this one. This is where we’re going to be living’ and showing me on FaceTime.”



“In that moment I did feel really out of control.”

Jessica met Dale when he was playing for Crewe and admits she never expected football to dictate where they lived, saying: “I didn’t get together with him because he was a footballer so I never considered the footballer life – that he might just have to move at the last minute.”

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“Since living together, we’ve moved five times in five years. You have to be prepared for anything in the transfer window. But it’s also a really fortunate position to be in at a young age.”

Dale, now 27 and a free agent after spending last season at Plymouth, has made much of his career in League One, with moves often coming late in transfer windows.



Jessica now works from home in social media and shares her experiences on TikTok, but insists Dale’s career has to come first.

She said: “My career can be picked up at any time, whereas his career is right now and you’ve really got to take every opportunity.”

“As much as people say it’s a glamorous lifestyle you do make sacrifices so your partner can have their dream and get themselves as far as they can in football.

“People also put League One players in the same bracket as Premier League players.”

“In the Premier League they’re often set up for life, we can’t live in that way because we have to prepare for life after football.”



With four-year-old Xavier and two-month-old Etta now in the equation, stability is becoming another major concern.

Yet Jessica tries to turn every move into an adventure for the children, rather than something to fear.

She said: “We’ve said to Xavier that we might be moving soon and when we do we’re going to get his bike back out of storage.



“That way he knows that moving is a possibility and hopefully he’s not thinking about what he’s going to lose but what he’s going to gain.

“The main thing for me personally – and what I’ve learned first hand – is the importance of keeping your own identity outside of football.

“If you can get a hobby, a routine or even a work-from-home job, that can help – things that can move with you.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Despite all the upheaval, she insisted: “We’ve lived in places that we never would have lived in. And that’s exciting for a relationship.

“You know, with some relationships you can get bored. In football, you don’t get bored!”

Sports.title: Port Vale fans fight EACH OTHER in ugly scenes during Carabao Cup mauling at Wolves
Sports.content:
FANS fought in the away end as Wolves hosted Port Vale in the Carabao Cup.

Cops were forced to intervene as punches were thrown during the Molineux tie.



The mass altercation appeared to be sparked by two fans fighting, with others subsequently joining in.

As police broke the scraps up the scene appeared to de-escalate.



Port Vale have released a statement vowing to get to the bottom of the incident.

Wolves comfortably won the tie 3-0 to get new boss Cesar Peixoto’s tenure off to a perfect start.

Andre made it 2-0 in the 34th minute, with Fer Lopez adding a third before half-time.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After the game, Vale manager Jon Brady told the BBC: “We had three big chances and then they score after that and it hits you hard.

Vale will begin their League Two campaign with a trip to Oldham next Saturday.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Danny Welbeck shows age with dire AC Milan performance as Joao Pedro runs rings around veteran
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO may be getting his message across to his new Chelsea stars in their dominant win over AC Milan.

The Blues have endured a hapless pre-season with defeats to London rivals Tottenham as well as Juventus as they gear up for their Premier League opener on August 24 at Fulham.



This time, though, Chelsea showed some really promising signs despite their bloated squad.

Pedro Neto also played his first few minutes during pre-season after his comeback from the World Cup with Portugal, while Mykhailo Mudryk continued his return.



But it was Joao Pedro who scored a double for the London giants, before Moises Caicedo made it three with a thunderbolt.

The only downside was a laboured effort from veteran signing Danny Welbeck.

But who stood out and who wasn’t quite up to par?

SunSport’s Lloyd Canfield rates every single Chelsea player below…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 6

Wasn’t forced into a single save by AC Milan, but his passing was good and should’ve probably had an assist had Joao Pedro not been wasteful early on in the game.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS



PEDRO NETO – 7

Forced a good save from Lorenzo Torriani with a shot from the right side of the box that was heading for the bottom left corner, and seemed to thrive as a wing-back.

It could be a new role for the Portuguese winger that could see him given a new lease of life at Stamford Bridge, should Manchester City not get their paws on him this summer.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 8

Rafael Leao formerly named Reece James as the toughest right-back he has faced, and he might now add Josh Acheampong to that list.

The young Blues’ centre-back had arguably the toughest task out of any of their defenders, but stood up brilliantly to the tricky Portuguese winger and played the ball nicely out from the back too.

The best of Chelsea‘s back three today.



WESLEY FOFANA – 7

Made more defensive contributions than any other Chelsea defender, and was strong in the air and across the ground.

Many fans want him sold, but performances like this prove why he can be a really valuable asset to Xabi Alonso‘s side, particularly in a back three system.

JORREL HATO – 6

Was the least involved of Chelsea’s back three, but this is a system that will suit him better than most.

His passing was good, often progressing the ball nicely onto Marco Palestra in front of him, he just wasn’t as busy as the other two due to where AC Milan were (hardly) threatening.



MARCO PALESTRA – 7

Chelsea’s biggest threat in the first half, thriving in the left-wing back position with heaps of athleticism and pace.

Reminiscent of Marcos Alonso in many ways in this Xabi Alonso system, and was really unfortunate not to have an assist or two in the first half alone, had it not been for the Blues’ wasteful forwards.

ROMEO LAVIA – 7

Bagged an assist for Moises Caicedo’s screamer from a corner, masterminded by Austin MacPhee – this was a game that showed the level of player that Romeo Lavia can be.

All action, some brilliant passing, and an ability to keep possession and beat the press like no other.



Completed his first ever full game for the Blues since joining in August 2023.

MOISES CAICEDO – 9

This is a Rolls Royce midfielder – he can do it all.

Excellent in breaking up play against one of the best to ever do it in Luka Modric, his set-piece delivery was pinpoint to set up Joao Pedro’s opener, before he stole the show from the Brazilian with one of the finest volleys ever scored by a Chelsea player.

His trivela volley to add Chelsea’s third was something even Paul Scholes and Zinedine Zidane would look at and admire.

COLE PALMER – 6

Played an interesting role as a right-sided number 10 in this 3-4-2-1 Xabi Alonso lineup, which is where many expect him to shine alongside Morgan Rogers when the former Villa man arrives in blue.



Looked sharp with a few clever touches, but lacked a little in terms of his end product, which he will be hoping is up to scratch by the time the opening day against Fulham comes around.

JOAO PEDRO – 9

Had a big chance after 12 minutes that went to waste following a great pass from Robert Sanchez, and it looked like it might not be his day when he blazed another effort into row Z before eventually finding his range.

Opened the scoring with a perfectly placed header before half-time, and then emerged for the second half with overflowing confidence, tapping home a second just moments after the whistle went.



His versatility to thrive as one of the No10s, just playing off of Danny Welbeck, adds another string to his bow for this season.

DANNY WELBECK – 4

Lashed the side netting with a left-footed effort early on, but was wasteful in all honesty in this game and that was about all he did.

Not overly involved in things for the Blues going forward, with most of the players around him more impactful than he was.

SUBS:

GEOVANY QUENDA (PEDRO NETO, 58) – 7

Hit the post with a rocket of a strike on his weaker foot after coming on.



He looks a really exciting player for the Blues, similarly to Estevao Willian at this point last season, and looks fearless in taking on his man and playing with personality.

Stamford Bridge is going to love him.

NICOLAS JACKSON (DANNY WELBECK, 58) – 6

Came on and was better than Danny Welbeck, linking up nicely with Cole Palmer and making things happen up top, but again lacked that clinical edge that has always been the undoing of his Chelsea career.

AARON ANSELMINO (JORREL HATO, 79)

His touch seemed a little off the pace compared to Jorrel Hato, but he didn’t have much time to settle into the game in his defence.

REGGIE WATSON (MOISES CAICEDO, 85) – N/A

Almost scored just moments after coming on, but was denied by Lorenzo Torriani in the Milan goal.

Sports.title: Chelsea flop Jamie Gittens ‘lined up for shock Roma transfer’ just one year after winger’s £52million move
Sports.content:
CHELSEA flop Jamie Gittens could be heading for a shock Roma exit just one year after his big-money move to Stamford Bridge.

The winger has reportedly emerged as a target for Roma as boss Gian Piero Gasperini continues his search for a creative attacker.



According to reports in Italy, Roma have drawn up a shortlist of attacking options as Gasperini looks to add a left-sided playmaker capable of drifting inside, creating overloads, and pressing from the front.

The Italian giants are understood to be keen to get the deal done quickly.



However, financial restrictions mean Roma must tread carefully, with the club operating a wage ceiling of around £3million net per year, barring exceptional cases.

Antonio Nusa had previously been one of Gasperini’s preferred targets.

But that move has cooled with RB Leipzig valuing the Norwegian at around £50m, a price Roma are unwilling to meet.

That has seen Lyon winger Malick Fofana and Gittens rise up the shortlist.

Fofana is valued at around £40m, although Roma are hoping they can negotiate a lower fee.

And sporting director Tony D’Amico is also keeping a close eye on Gittens.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube Calling all Chelsea fans - we have a brand new YouTube channel! The Sun’s Chelsea YouTube channel will be your go-to destination for the latest news, transfer updates, match previews, post-match analysis, exclusive interviews, fan reactions, and breaking stories from Stamford Bridge. Subscribe to The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube now

The England U21 international only arrived at Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer in a deal worth around £52m.

But his time in West London has failed to go entirely to plan, and Roma could now offer him a route out.

A permanent deal would be difficult for the Serie A club to finance, but a loan could be explored if Chelsea are prepared to sanction one.

Gasperini is desperate to add the right creative spark to his squad and is understood to want his new signing through the door as soon as possible.



Gittens is far from the only Chelsea player whose future remains uncertain.

The Blues could still wave goodbye to up to 15 players before the summer transfer window closes, with as many as 10 potentially leaving on loan.

Chelsea have already done much of their incoming business, meaning the focus is now firmly on trimming Xabi Alonso‘s squad.

Several players who have found themselves on the fringes in recent seasons need permanent homes, while a number of highly-rated academy stars require regular senior football to continue their development.

With Chelsea expected to play just once a week this season, Alonso will have more time to work with his squad.



But keeping a bloated group of players happy could prove a major challenge.

Here are the Chelsea stars who could still leave before the window shuts:

Axel Disasi

Disasi impressed during his loan spell at West Ham towards the end of last season and could now be heading for another Premier League move.

Crystal Palace have been linked with the defender as they look for a replacement for Maxence Lacroix, while several Serie A clubs are also understood to be monitoring him.

Tosin Adarabioyo

Tosin was one of Chelsea’s most experienced players last season after arriving on a free transfer from Fulham.



But he could now find himself surplus to requirements.

Alonso is reportedly looking for four or five centre-backs, and Tosin’s position in the pecking order is far from secure.

Benoit Badiashile

Napoli currently appears to be the most likely destination for Badiashile.



A loan deal containing an option to buy has reportedly been discussed as Chelsea look to move the French defender on.

Trevoh Chalobah

Chalobah is closing in on a move to Cesc Fabregas‘ Como.

The defender could even find himself facing Arsenal in his new club’s first game next Wednesday.

Wesley Fofana

Fofana could yet remain at Stamford Bridge, particularly with Chelsea needing to trim their defensive options.

Barcelona and Roma have both been linked with the Frenchman, but he could be given one final opportunity to resurrect his Blues career.



Malo Gusto

Paris Saint-Germain have reportedly shown an interest in the versatile Frenchman.

Chelsea are believed to want around £75m for Gusto, while the arrival of Marco Palestra could further cast doubt over his future.

Romeo Lavia

Lavia is still waiting to complete a full 90 minutes for Chelsea.

Monaco are reportedly interested in the Belgian midfielder, whose enormous potential has repeatedly been undermined by his injury problems.

Alonso needs players he can rely on, making Lavia’s fitness record a major concern.



Enzo Fernandez

Fernandez was linked with a move to Real Madrid this summer, only for the Spanish giants to publicly distance themselves from the possibility.

The Argentine now finds himself in something of a transfer limbo.

Chelsea are reportedly demanding around £120m for their midfielder, but there are currently no serious suitors willing to meet that valuation.



Pedro Neto

There is no desperation from Chelsea to sell one of their standout wingers from last season.

However, Manchester City are understood to be interested in the Portugal international.

Chelsea would reportedly consider a sale if their £70m valuation is met.

Liam Delap

Delap is one of four out-and-out strikers on Chelsea’s potential departure list.

Nottingham Forest, Everton, Leeds and Newcastle have all been linked with the forward, although none are currently close to agreeing a deal.



Nicolas Jackson

Chelsea want around £65m for Jackson.

The Senegal international has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs as well as teams across Europe, leaving the door open for a late-window exit.

Marc Guiu

Guiu was at the centre of one of the strangest transfer sagas of last summer when Chelsea brought him back from his loan spell at Sunderland.

But the club now have younger and more highly-rated options up front, making a permanent departure a logical next step for the striker.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And with Chelsea facing a major squad reshuffle before the window closes, Gittens could be one of the most intriguing names to watch.



The winger only arrived for a huge fee last summer — but Roma’s interest suggests his Stamford Bridge future may already be in serious doubt.

Ronald Araujo is set to join Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona, where one of his lows came in a Champions League quarter-final loss against Luis Enrique's Paris Saint-Germain

‌

When it came time to address his squad, the Spaniard explained: "Let this gentleman (a magnet on a board) be Araujo, who is a high-level player, no doubt about it. But he is the player with the most problems. Every time the ball gets to Araujo - whether it's a support, a pass and so on - when the ball comes in motion, cover the passing line and go."

‌



Enrique's game plan looked to be out of the window when Raphinha gave Barcelona the lead on 12 minutes, extending their advantage. But then came the turning point, as Araujo played a misplaced pass after being pressed by Bradley Barcola exactly in the way Enrique had instructed him to.

Scampering back as Barcola raced away, Araujo clumsily fouled the French winger and got himself sent off, paving the way for PSG's comeback. Enrique's team ran out 4-1 winners on the night and progressed to the last four.

Will Ronald Araujo prove his doubters wrong? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The incident has haunted Araujo's career at Barcelona ever since, and he was also culpable for a crucial goal in their Champions League semi-final defeat to Inter Milan in 2025 when Hansi Flick's men were seconds away from going through. The Champions League has been a particular source of frustration for Araujo, who was also sent off against Chelsea last season.

That red card prompted him to take a mental health break which Barcelona granted him, telling Mundo Deportivo: "I'd been dealing with anxiety for a year and a half that turned into depression, and I was playing like that. That doesn't help, because on the field you don't really feel like yourself."

‌



Barcelona faced PSG in the Champions League again last season, and when Enrique's comments were put to Flick, he replied: "What happened in the past is no longer valid; now is different. I have full confidence in all my players. He's incredible and has proven it in recent games. I'm very happy with him."

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola was fouled by Ronald Araujo and it changed the tie (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

Araujo will hope that his move to Anfield serves as a fresh start. Blessed with pace, strong and boasting a towering 6ft 3in frame which makes him a threat in both boxes, Andoni Iraola likes what he sees from the Uruguay international, who didn't feature at the World Cup due to a calf injury.

Article continues below

His ability to play at right-back should also come in handy for Liverpool, who need cover in the position due to Conor Bradley's injury. Last month, centre-back Joe Gomez suffered an injury, making it a bigger priority to recruit a defender.

Sports.title: Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move
Sports.content:
Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move

Manchester United have been forced to turn to other targets in their attempts to sign a left-back this summer after Newcastle made it clear that Lewis Hall isn't for sale

View 5 Images Lewis Hall won't be joining Manchester United it seems (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Manchester United have made little ground in their efforts to sign a left-back this summer, with top target Lewis Hall appearing to be out of reach.

‌



Newcastle have made it clear to United that after selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, they are in no mood to offload Hall, too. It would take a bid way beyond United's means to test that stance meaning that, with 24 days of the transfer window left, United must look elsewhere.

‌



Michael Carrick is keen to add competition for places at left-back, where Luke Shaw remains the first choice. Harry Amass has featured in pre-season but could be sold or loaned out, while Noussair Mazraoui and Diego Dalot are more comfortable on the right side of defence, and Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward under Carrick's management.

‌



United have already landed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos to address their most pressing need in central midfield but could find left-back a more difficult prospect. Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the other contenders.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry READ MORE :

Antonee Robinson

Robinson had been a regular name in transfer reports, but fell off the radar somewhat last season due to a dip in form. But his 2024-25 campaign, in which he returned 10 assists in the Premier League, hasn't faded from the memory of scouts and sporting directors yet.

‌



The 28-year-old, who played for the United States at the World Cup in the summer, has eye-catching pace and loves to go forward - something that sets him apart from the more conservative (and much slower) Shaw. He has two years left on his Fulham contract, so could be affordable.

View 5 Images Antonee Robinson is an option for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

El Hadji Malick Diouf

Diouf was relegated with West Ham last season and is far from the finished article, but at 21 years old could be a player for the future. He contributed five assists in 32 Premier League matches for the Hammers last season and is a regular for Senegal.

‌



West Ham don't want to sell and, having shipped out Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for big fees already, are under little pressure to do so. Signed from Slavia Prague for £19million last summer, he still has four years left on his contract and West Ham have already rejected one bid from Brentford for his services, with a second offer expected.

View 5 Images El Hadji Malick Diouf had a good first season at West Ham (Image: Julian Finney)

Jorge Salinas

Another one for the future, rather than a serious contender for Shaw's place in the starting XI. The 19-year-old Racing Santander player is reportedly on United's radar.

‌



He is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, making him very affordable. However, United could face competition from Barcelona, who often hoover up the best talent in Spain and are looking for a replacement for Joao Cancelo, who is set to make the move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

View 5 Images Jorge Salinas is on Manchester United's radar

David Raum

The RB Leipzig captain is an energetic, durable and experienced player who is capable of displacing Shaw from the United team. He is much more mobile than Show, who is about to start his 13th season with the Red Devils.

‌



Raum has a strong left foot, is not shy of crossing, and could link up nicely with Benjamin Sesko, who is a real aerial threat and knows the German from his time at Leipzig. The 28-year-old is settled at Leipzig, who have just sold Yan Diomande to Real Madrid for £120m, so are in no rush to cash in.

However, the Germany international recently revealed he is yet to hold talks about extending his contract, which has less than a year left to run. "It's up to the club to decide when they approach me, what they offer, how much appreciation they show, what their plans are for me, and where they want to go in the coming years," he said.

View 5 Images David Raum has entered the final year of his RB Leipzig contract (Image: Ralf Ibing - firo sportphoto/Getty Images)

‌



"Of course, I have to listen to that and make my own decision. I'm 28 now, and naturally I also have dreams and goals. You always have to see how that fits together with the club's plans, ideas and objectives for the next few years."

He added: "The club generally doesn't like to let a player run down his contract. I don't know what they have planned with me. At the moment, it doesn't look like they want to sell me or get rid of me. I feel a lot of appreciation here."

Depending on your interpretation, that is either a player trying to force the club to the negotiating table for a new deal, or a player issuing a come-get-me plea.

Sports.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
Sports.content:
Betfred Super League side Huddersfield Giants have announced they are to leave the town and move to Dewsbury for the 2027 season onwards.

The Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground.

The investment will deliver a transformational upgrade of the venue, including the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators, creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants director of rugby Andy Kelly reflects on what he's described as the 'most challenging' period of time in charge of the club

The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of the fan concourses, significant upgrades to existing and new hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, both male and female player dressing rooms, and press facilities elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

An agreement has been reached following extensive and amicable negotiations with Betfred Championship team, Dewsbury Rams, and a strong partnership between the two clubs has been forged. The Flair will continue to host the Rams in the newly-upgraded and dual-branded facility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants prop Tom Burgess joins Jenna, Jon and Sam Tomkins on The Bench

This comes following a period of uncertainty for the Giants after seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

Owner of the club, Ken Davy OBE, has explored several alternative sites, including The Shay Stadium in Halifax.

Speaking of the decision, Davy said: "It's no secret that as a club, we have fought to find a home in Huddersfield. We had to move from Fartown, from Leeds Road, and now from the Accu Stadium. But the Huddersfield Giants will not retreat. We will not compromise or quietly shuffle into the shadows.

"While we remain the Huddersfield Giants, I am proud to announce that our stage for the 2027 season and beyond is Dewsbury.

"The Flair Stadium is the perfect location for us, it will have the right capacity and facilities for the Giants and its fans to thrive while we continue the search for our permanent home. Our one giant future starts now.

"My overriding aim is to create a purpose-built stadium within Huddersfield for the Giants to call home. My commitment on that has not wavered. However, that was not feasible for the 2027 season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League

Ralph Rimmer OBE, executive chairman of the Huddersfield Giants, added: "The Giants' future is bright, and we are excited to lead the club into this new era.

"For fans, the matchday experience will be our focus. A smaller, more intimate ground means the crowd is closer to the action, letting the atmosphere grow and support the team out on the pitch.

"The Flair Stadium offers everything that supporters need from parking and accessibility to corporate hospitality and function rooms.

"We can't wait to welcome you for the 2027 season and beyond to be a part of the Giant future we have in store."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Nicholls pays tribute as Big Buck's dies aged 23
Sports.content:
Big Buck’s, one of the greatest staying hurdlers of all time, has died at the age of 23.

Owned by the late Andy Stewart, he was part of a golden age for trainer Paul Nicholls as he counted Kauto Star, Denman, Master Minded and Neptune Collonges among his stablemates.

Big Buck's had always been viewed by connections as a potential top-class chaser, however, a fall at the final fence in the 2008 Hennessy Gold Cup saw him revert back to hurdles and he never looked back.

He won what is now the Stayers' Hurdle a record four times, the Liverpool Hurdle four times and three times he came home in front in the Long Walk Hurdle.

Big Buck's, who struck up a great relationship with Ruby Walsh, was a fan favourite as he would often hit a flat spot in his races before powering to victory.

Nicholls told the Press Association: "Ability-wise he was probably as good as anything I've ever trained, it's just a shame he couldn't jump a chase fence.

"He was a wonderful horse for a wonderful owner who deserved to own a great horse like that. Andy enjoyed the whole journey and shared it with everybody.

"The horse had a brilliant life and had a great time with us and then a great time with Mike and Lucy Felton in retirement, but sadly time caught up with him.

"I was very lucky to have him at the same time as Kauto Star, Neptune Collonges, Master Minded and Denman. He was definitely as good as any of them."

Image: Big Buck's and Ruby Walsh formed a formidable partnership

One of the last surviving members of that halcyon period for the Ditcheat handler, Big Buck's would go on to pass Sir Ken and win a then record 18 straight National Hunt races when reverting to hurdles, an achievement only eclipsed by Altior since.

However, for Nicholls there will always be the question of how high he could have climbed if remaining over the larger obstacles.

"He won the Graded race at Aintree over fences, jumped 18 fences and jumped them 18 different ways and still won," said Nicholls.

"It made me think he was a certainty in the Hennessy and he was unlucky that day, but he just wasn't a natural jumper of a fence.

"If Kauto Star hadn't been about at that time then we probably would persevered over fences and he had the ability to win a Gold Cup. If he had won the Hennessy that day it would have definitely given us a headache and it would have been interesting where he would have ended up.

"But over hurdles he was invincible. Andy said I was bonkers, but going back over hurdles was the best thing we ever did. History tells you how good he was and Cheltenham, Aintree, Newbury, Ascot - if there was a big staying hurdle race, he won them all - all those Grade Ones on the trot, what a horse."

Big Bucks would become a standing dish on Thursdays at the Cheltenham Festival, with his famous flat spot often sparking nervous gasps from supporters before hitting top gear and surging up the Cheltenham hill under Walsh.

When asked to nominate just one race in Big Bucks' decorated career littered with so many great triumphs it was his fourth-straight success in the day three feature, when seeing off arguably the deepest field he met, edging out Irish raider Voler La Vedette, that Nicholls remembers most fondly.

"His fourth World Hurdle was the one that sticks out as being very special," said Nicholls.

"But we had so many great days with such a brilliant horse and we were all very lucky to be associated with him."

Sports.title: Australia survive late Japan rally as new coach Kiss makes winning start
Sports.content:
Australia held on for a tight 35-32 victory over Japan, despite a first-half red card for Miles Amatosero, as they made a winning start in head coach Les Kiss' first match in charge.

The Wallabies were forced to dig deep, battling the heat as well as being a man down, holding off a strong comeback from Japan to emerge victorious.

"That was tough, wasn't it? Not just the conditions," said Kiss. "They're a good team. They ​play fast and hard at home in their backyard.

"Probably offered a few too many opportunities for them. We'll have a look at it. But overall, that's a Test win. Well done, boys."

Image: Les Kiss was previously head coach of Queensland Reds

Kiss took over from Joe Schmidt as head coach last month after Australia finished the first phase of the Nations Championship with one win in three - a victory over Italy following on from losses to Ireland and France .

For Australia's two-Test series against Japan, Kiss included only one uncapped player, centre Isaac Henry, but recalled big, versatile Reds forward Lukhan Salakaia-Loto and left out veteran James Slipper.

The Wallabies were forced to scramble after Amatosero was red-carded in the 32nd minute for a dangerous clean-out on Warner Dearns. Initially shown a yellow card, it was upgraded to red just before the break, which the teams entered locked at 14-14.

Tries from Max Jorgensen and Fraser McReight early in the second half helped Australia build a nine-point lead but Japan steadily ate into that advantage with a pair of penalties from Takuro Matsunaga.

The quality of Australia's bench proved the difference as it allowed the visitors to keep up the pressure on Japan, and Taniela Tupou crashed over to give them a 10-point lead with 10 minutes remaining.

Japan captain Dearns set up a grandstand finish when he found a way over, reducing the lead to three, but Australia held on.

Image: Former Australia and England head coach Eddie Jones is in his second stint in charge of Japan

Eddie Jones, the former Australia and England head coach, is in his second stint in charge of Japan.

"We let ourselves down with a few fundamental ​errors in the last 20 minutes when we had an opportunity to probably put Australia away, so pretty disappointed, mate," said Jones.

"But yeah, I'm really proud of how hard the players ‌are playing and there's a lot of development ​in this team."

Sports.title: Joao Pedro nets double as Chelsea bounce back to beat Milan
Sports.content:
Chelsea bounced back from back-to-back pre-season defeats with their best performance under Xabi Alonso so far as Joao Pedro's double helped them to a convincing 3-0 win over AC Milan in Jakarta.

The Blues' previous hybrid between 4-2-3-1 and Alonso's patented 3-4-3 was ditched in favour of the latter and paid off against the Serie A heavyweights, with Marco Palestra shining at left wing-back and the impact of new set-piece coach Austin McPhee already evident.

Chelsea scored 10 goals from corners across the whole Premier League season in 2025/26 but managed two in 90 minutes here, with Joao Pedro peeling off Milan goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani to glance Moises Caicedo's delivery home unmarked, moments before the break.

He doubled his and Chelsea's lead within a minute of the restart by pouncing at the back post to turn home Pedro Neto's in-swinging cross, before Caicedo turned provider to scorer by latching onto a volley from another corner from the edge of the box three minutes later.

Chelsea could have had more with substitutes Geovany Quenda and Nicolas Jackson both lively and denied by the woodwork, but they could settle for a morale-boosting victory and more than an hour in the legs for most of a strong starting line-up in Indonesia.

Sports.title: Rockets clinch qualification for women's knockouts in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets booked a place in the knockouts of The Hundred women's competition with a thumping nine-wicket win over already-eliminated MI London.

Nat Sciver-Brunt (67no off 36 balls) and Beth Mooney (54no off 44) struck sublime half-centuries as Rockets eased to their 122-run target with 18 balls to spare to claim a fifth-straight win.

Earlier, Australian left-arm spinner Sam Bates claimed 3-13 to move joint-top of the wicket-taking charts as MI London struggled to 121-5.

The Rockets then strolled to their target, despite Sophia Dunkley being dismissed for a three-ball duck. Sciver-Brunt and Mooney's subsequent 118-run stand is the second-highest partnership in the history of the women's competition.

MI London had made a steady enough start after being asked to bat, reaching 28-0, but the innings fell away after Bates took the key wicket of Hayley Matthews (10), trapped lbw.

Hollie Armitage (4) fell cheaply to Charley Phillips, before Bates struck twice off consecutive deliveries - dismissing Kira Chathli (31 from 27) lbw before Nicola Carey fell to a smart stumping by Mooney - as the hosts slumped to 49-4, with only an MI London review denying her the wicket of Alice Monaghan and a hat-trick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Trent Rockets' Sam Bates was denied a hat-trick after MI London's Alice Monaghan reviewed the umpire's original decision of out lbw on Bates' hat-trick ball which proved to be agonisingly missing the wickets

Monaghan (27no off 21) and Melie Kerr (17 off 14) rebuilt, before Chinelle Henry (27no off 21) struck a flurry of boundaries late on, but their total looked well below-bar on a good deck against a rampant Rockets outfit. And so it proved.

What is happening in The Hundred on Sunday?

It's another four-match day, with two games apiece at Headingley and Lord's.

SunRisers Leeds first host Welsh Fire (women's game 11am, men's 2.30pm), the two teams jostling for position in the latter stages of both the women's and men's tournaments.

London Spirit then take on Birmingham Phoenix (women's game 2.30pm, men's 6pm), both battling for pride as they've already been eliminated from the women's and men's competitions.

"I'm so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. I'm your warrior, I'll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together."

Newcastle had been keen to ensure the Brazil international, who had two years left on his contract plus a club-held option for a third, stayed at St James' Park, but his departure means they have now sold more than £240m worth of talent this summer.

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona in a £69.3m deal and Spurs signed Sandro Tonali for £100m, while head coach Eddie Howe also left in what has been a turbulent few months at the club.

A Newcastle statement said: "The agreed fee represents one of the top-10 highest transfer fees ever received for a player aged 28 or over, and a record fee for a player of his age and position combined."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes a closer look at how Guimaraes stacks up against Arsenal's current midfield

Guimaraes told Newcastle bosses earlier this summer that he wanted to join Arsenal if a suitable offer arrived. Their opening bid was rejected before the deal was agreed.

He joined the Magpies in 2022 from Lyon for £40m and made 195 appearances for the club, scoring 31 goals and winning the Carabao Cup.

'One of the toughest decisions of my life'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Guimaraes' best Premier League goals for Newcastle

On his Newcastle departure, Guimaraes said: "This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together.

"I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my team-mates, Eddie (Howe) and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

"I thank PIF, our chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David (Hopkinson) and Ross (Wilson) for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.

"This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family. I had a very positive conversation with Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands.

"To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club's journey. Thank you for everything."

'A statement signing for Arsenal'

Sky Sports' Oliver Yew:

Guimaraes is one of the best midfielders in the Premier League, if not the world, and from a position of strength, Arsenal have taken him from Newcastle.

Midfield is already an area of the pitch where Arsenal are strong but Guimaraes' arrival is certainly an upgrade on Christian Norgaard, who has joined Everton. Myles Lewis-Skelly was playing incredibly well at the end of last season and started the Champions League final. Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino are World Cup winners and after some rest will be ready to go. There is Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze for the No 10 position alongside the two potential starters in Declan Rice and Guimaraes.

I'm so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. I'm your warrior, I'll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.

The Brazilian gives Arteta even more options and it also allows for the possibility for Rice to get a breather in certain games after his exploits last season.

It is a world-class midfield and if Arsenal were not favourites for the title already, they are now.

Question marks were being raised over the fee Newcastle wanted for a player who will be 29 in November but the deal has been done nowhere near the reported £100m fee that was wanted. At the start of the transfer window, you would have probably said this is a fair fee, but with the last few weeks we have had in the window, with big money spent on midfielders Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, anything under £100m looks good value.

Guimaraes is a little older but this is Arsenal's strategy, they want to win now. They have signed some younger players but last summer's deal to sign Viktor Gyokeres was to win now. He will not need any time to settle in. He is one of the most consistent Premier League midfielders.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd thinks Guimaraes is an upgrade for Arsenal's midfield and will play alongside or fill in for Declan Rice

Arsenal will not necessarily make money on him in the future but his arrival should get them closer to winning a first Champions League and he may help them retain the Premier League title.

If they can add a left winger and some star quality in that position, which looks like the last piece of the puzzle, it could be bad news for their title rivals.

'Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Keith Downie explains the three reasons why Newcastle have allowed Guimaraes to leave the club for Premier League champions Arsenal

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie:

Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes and if he had said he wanted to stay, Newcastle would have refused any offer from Arsenal or any other club.

Attempts to persuade Guimaraes otherwise were made and positive conversations were held, but he was insistent he wanted to leave because he felt this was his last big opportunity to win titles.

The deal could only go ahead if two things happened: Guimaraes said he wanted to leave (which he has respectfully) and Newcastle sold on their terms, similar to Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

Newcastle insisted it was their valuation or no deal. They would only sell Guimaraes at a fee that would become one of the highest paid for a player aged 28 or over.

In addition, a deal would only be sanctioned if the situation was handled properly - for example, Guimaraes attending Newcastle's training camp in Spain, which he reported to on Monday.

Newcastle feel Guimaraes has complied with their demands immaculately. They did not want a repeat of the Alexander Isak situation, where he refused to train before joining Liverpool last summer.

Agents were in between the clubs from the outset but Newcastle refused all pushes, which had began with mentions of a deal worth £40-£45m in June.

Newcastle were left frustrated because they felt Arsenal elongated the transfer by refusing to contact them for weeks.

Newcastle insist there have been no fall outs and good relations remain between player and club.
