Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Sports.content:
Uefa has confirmed a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Gianni Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary, allegations Fifa has dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino. In a statement, Uefa confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, which it said was “in line” with regulations at the time.

However, Fifa has responded to the reports. “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph. “No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

The report comes as pressure mounts on Infantino following his plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino worked at Uefa for 16 years and was its general secretary from 2009 before being elected as Fifa president in February 2016.

A Uefa spokesperson said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.”

The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. “Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino has found himself at the centre of a storm for two weeks following his controversial plan to sell stakes to private investors in a company to run the World Cup. The plan was rejected by Uefa and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino was backed by Fifa’s management board following a meeting in Morocco and issued an apology over the process.

Uefa’s threat for its 55 member countries to boycott Fifa competitions until the plan was scrapped remains, with the European confederation saying on Thursday that Wednesday’s announcement “changes nothing”.

Sports.title: West Ham v Portsmouth, Burnley v Notts County: Carabao Cup first round – live
Sports.content:
GOAL! Preston North End 0-1 Huddersfield Town (Balker 38). Radinio Balker takes advantage against the ten men, heading a cross from the right into the bottom left. This is a replay of the 1938 FA Cup final, incidentally. Here’s how we described the winner of that match in the Joy of Six.

1. George Mutch (PRESTON 1-0 Huddersfield Town, 1938)

The 1938 FA Cup final between Preston North End and Huddersfield Town was the first to be televised live by the BBC. In the commentary box, describing the first half of this historic and prestigious event, was George Allison, manager of Arsenal, who were busy elsewhere taking on Liverpool as they battled with Wolverhampton Wanderers in the race for the title. (Imagine Sir Alex Ferguson eschewing Manchester United’s game at Blackburn in order to take the mic for ESPN. The past really is a different country.) Arsenal would win the league the following week, but Allison’s luck wasn’t in this particular day: the first half of the final, his showpiece broadcast, was a defensive non-event.

The second half was barely any better, save for a couple of speculative shots from Huddersfield’s Pat Beasley and Preston’s Bill Shankly. The game went into extra time. Describing the action, such as it was, since half-time was Lieutenant-Commander Thomas Woodrooffe, a former naval officer who had become one of BBC radio’s top broadcasters. Woodrooffe was appalled at the dreary nature of events, and with the match entering the 120th minute, he announced to the viewing nation (which, in 1938, totalled about 17 toffs in the Alexandra Palace area of London) that “if there is a goal now, I’ll eat my hat”.

Sure enough, and right on cue, Preston’s inside-right, George Mutch, picked up the ball and went on one last desperate sortie into the Huddersfield area. Alf Young, the Huddersfield captain, went over to cover. He stuck out a boot, with calamitous results. “Flat to earth went Mutch as though sudden death had overtaken him,” reported the Manchester Guardian. “The Huddersfield team stood thunderstruck in all the sad variety of woe, all save the wretched Young, who threw up appealing arms before the referee. Preston put breath back into Mutch and, after some anxious conclave, nominated and unanimously elected him to exact the tribute for the affront that had been done to him.”

Mutch nearly missed the penalty – it would be another exact half-century before that grim fate befell a player in the cup final – but the ball flew between Bob Hesford’s arms, caught the underside of the bar, and rolled along the netting before dropping into the goal. There was just time for Huddersfield to kick off before the final whistle blew. So, not exactly a contender to rival Ricky Villa, Roberto di Matteo or Ray Parlour, but one of the most dramatic finishes to a cup final, and one with a surreal denouement. Woodrooffe – who was already infamous for his majestic drunken Fleet’s Lit Up meanderings at a naval show a year earlier – bravely kept the promise made in the moments before Mutch sprawled over Young’s leg, and tucked into a bowler hat live on BBC television. It was made of cake and marzipan.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães completes £75m Arsenal move: ‘I needed a new challenge’
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães says he “needed a new challenge in my life” after joining Arsenal from Newcastle for £75m and has targeted winning trophies. Guimarães is understood to have signed a four-year contract that contains a further one-year option after Newcastle reluctantly agreed to sell their captain.

The 29-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first trophy since 1955 when they won the Carabao Cup last year, had made it clear that he wanted to join the Premier League champions after meeting the club’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, this week.

Arsenal have previously shown an interest in signing Guimarães on two occasions – in 2020 when he was playing for Athletico Paranaense in Brazil and then 18 months later when he was at Lyon and went on to move to the north-east. But the Brazil midfielder said he wanted to join Arsenal after his first meeting with Mikel Arerta and the sporting director, Andrea Berta.

“I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life,” he told Arsenal’s website. “After playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it.

“I’m so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

The arrival of Guimarães significantly boosts the midfield options available to Arteta, who now has a formidable squad that contains Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

“We are further strengthening the heart of our team,” said Berta. “As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity and has provided goals and assists for his team every year. Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimarães revealed he has already received a message from Rice welcoming him to Arsenal that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”. “I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, is one of the best in Europe,” said Guimarães. “Everyone is an amazing player. I’m so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well,”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães said leaving Tyneside was ‘one of the toughest decisions of my life’. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Guimarães also released a statement to Newcastle. He said: “I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie [Howe] and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together. I thank PIF, our chair, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David [Hopkinson, the Newcastle CEO] and Ross [Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director] for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.”

On Friday, Wilson said they had no option but to allow Guimarães to leave. “What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave,” he said.

“That doesn’t mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen.”

Sports.title: Jorge Messi, father and agent of Argentina great, dies aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi’s father and agent, Jorge, has died aged 68 at a medical clinic in the ⁠Argentinian city of ⁠Rosario after ​a long illness, the family have announced. Jorge Messi spent his final months ⁠alternating between a medical centre in Rosario and his home, accompanied by his wife, Celia, and his ⁠children Rodrigo, Matías and María Sol.

Lionel Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the World ‌Cup before rejoining his club, Inter Miami, for whom he ‌returned to action a week ago. Inter Miami are due to play Monterrey on Saturday at home in the 2026 Leagues Cup, but the MLS club have yet to announce whether he will feature.

Newell’s Old Boys announced the death in a social media post that said he had undergone treatment in recent months for an unspecified illness. The post described him as “the pillar and the person who, with vision, rigour and affection, supported the career of the best player of all time, alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini”. The South American Football Confederation, Conmebol, also offered its condolences in a statement, “with respect and affection for Lionel”.

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi poses with his brother Rodrigo, sister María Sol, father Jorge, mother Celia, nephew Tomás and brother Matías in Rosario, Argentina, in 2003. Photograph: El Grafico/Getty Images

At the World Cup, Lionel Messi said after Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Algeria – when he broke down in ​tears while celebrating ​his first goal in the team’s opening match – that he was going through a difficult personal situation. Later, he explained his tears ​were due ‌to “something unrelated to ​football” after ​going through “a few difficult, complicated days”.

There was speculation that the player’s emotional reaction to Argentina’s last-16 victory over Egypt was due in part to his father’s deteriorating condition. A few days later, the family issued a statement regarding Jorge Messi’s “health situation”, informing the public that he was undergoing medical treatment.

Jorge Messi closely accompanied his son throughout his career, beginning with his early years at Barcelona. He acted as a crucial pillar of support and, for several years, served as his representative. “I always ‌needed my dad’s approval, ever since I was a kid. After every match, I’d ask him ​what he thought of how I played,” said Lionel Messi.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona’s Ronald Araújo on loan as Jacquet cover
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed to sign Ronald Araújo on a season-long loan from Barcelona after Andoni Iraola was faced with lack of defensive options for the start of the new season.

Concerns over Jérémy Jacquet – the France Under -21 defender who arrived last season for more than £50m – and injuries to Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni have left Liverpool short of options at the back after the departure of Ibrahima Konaté on a free transfer to Real Madrid.

Araújo, who was part of the Barça side that won La Liga last season, will add much-needed cover in the short-term. The Uruguay defender is expected to complete his medical on Sunday.

The deal for the 27-year-old is believed to contain an option to buy at the end of the season. Araújo has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona, but only made 11 league starts last season.

Liverpool have shown an interest in Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa, but were put off by the £60m valuation of the England defender. Arsenal have had an initial approach for Konsa rejected.

Jacquet, who signed from Rennes in February, has not made a competitive appearance after picking up a serious shoulder injury last season and did not feature during Liverpool’s three-match tour of the United States. Iraola said last week that he has been feeling “some discomfort, so we don’t want to rush him”.

The Liverpool manager added: “He comes from a lot of months without playing. And obviously I would like to try with him with Virgil [van Dijk] when he recovers, because with the injury of Joe we’ve been without senior centre-backs. But we have to be careful with Jeremy.”

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.

“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso deploys a back three for the first time as Blues boss and why adding a set-piece coach has proved a masterstroke: Chelsea 3-0 AC Milan
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso can take plenty of encouragement from deploying a back three for the first time at Chelsea - conclusively beating AC Milan 3-0.

The display was a far cry from Chelsea’s leaky defensive performances in pre-season so far, as they kept their first clean sheet since Alonso took charge.

Chelsea were dominant throughout, helped by having consistent personnel on the pitch - making only two changes before 80 minutes, whereas AC Milan made wholesale substitutions at half-time.

But it was the defensive structure Alonso utilised so effectively at Bayer Leverkusen that enabled a comfortable performance.

Summer signing Marco Palestra was deployed at left wing-back, with Pedro Neto on the opposite side. In possession, though, they may as well have been wingers.

When Chelsea attacked, Neto ran beyond Palmer - who started on the right of Danny Welbeck - offering a penetrating threat to stretch play. Palestra acted the same way on the opposite side as his perpetual movement shone.

Not only did the set-up allow Chelsea to threaten all over the pitch with significant offensive threats occupying both wide and narrow areas, but the front three demonstrated their fluidity.

Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Welbeck often rotated. At times, there were two up top with one behind. The main formation, though, was a 3-4-2-1.

Welbeck led the line with Palmer and Pedro either side of him. But that was not a strict rule, as the attackers were given the freedom to roam.

A link-up between Pedro and Neto earned Chelsea their second less than a minute after half-time. Neto found Pedro’s run with a dinked cross into the box from the right.

Neto had very few defensive responsibilities as the right wing-back, allowing him to focus on being a nuisance.

That right side could prove deadly during the season, with full-backs forced to deal with the menacing Palmer inside while also keeping tabs on the threat Neto poses out wide.

Pedro, meanwhile, flourished in the system. Encouraged to float around, the technical Brazilian demonstrated his versatility as a number 10 who can also play out wide and up front.

Joao Pedro has been on fire during pre-season, scoring five times, and Xabi Alonso’s back three seemed to bring out the best in him

Four shots, two goals, a big chance missed and the most touches in the AC Milan box - Pedro, thanks to the set-up, was extremely active and took his pre-season tally to five goals.

Josh Acheampong was also a beneficiary of the system, exuding confidence both on and off the ball. The centre-back recovered brilliantly to make a last-ditch challenge on Rafael Leao in the first half, strong in the tackle - putting his mistake behind him.

With the likes of Reece James, Maxence Lacroix, Enzo Fernandez, Malo Gusto and Morgan Rogers to report for the remainder of pre-season next week, Alonso has every right to be excited about this Chelsea side.

At 70 per cent strength, Chelsea looked cohesive and controlled, with four games now under their belt and an encouraging understanding of what is required in a back three.

As even more quality is added to the group next week, the back three looks an appealing option to open their Premier League campaign against Fulham.

MacPhee's immediate impact

New set-piece coach Austin MacPhee has already started to earn his money.

Chelsea paid a release clause just shy of £1million to get him out of his contract at Aston Villa and bring him to Stamford Bridge. Minuscule in the context of player spend, but significant for a member of the backroom staff.

Yet he could prove to be Chelsea’s most important signing of the summer.

Chelsea had an appalling record from set-pieces last season, with a negative goal difference from them - conceding 17 and scoring 14. It is no wonder Alonso was so keen to add one of the world's best dead-ball coaches to his coaching staff.

Having joined Chelsea just this week - flying to Asia to unite with his new side on their pre-season tour - MacPhee made a blazing impact, with Chelsea scoring twice from corners against AC Milan.

Chelsea scored twice from set-pieces against AC Milan, with Moises Caicedo finding the back of the net from outside of the area

The first was pretty basic. Moises Caicedo’s pinpoint cross found Pedro’s intelligent movement. Pedro, unmarked, glanced his header into the far corner. It was a goal you will see many times this season.

The second, however, was certainly a move crafted on the training ground as MacPhee's expertise emerged.

Romeo Lavia floated a cross to the edge of the area where Caicedo was waiting. The midfielder coolly came onto the ball and ingeniously guided it into the bottom corner with the outside of his boot. He made a tough finish appear straightforward - it was anything but.

A move executed with individual brilliance, but one crafted by Chelsea’s new master in the dugout. If this is just a glimpse of MacPhee’s capabilities, Chelsea certainly have plenty to look forward to.

Lavia provides timely reminder of his quality

Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes for Chelsea since joining from Southampton for £53m in 2023, taking another step towards building up his fitness.

The 22-year-old midfielder has endured injury after injury since arriving in West London, but made significant progress on Saturday, having played 25 minutes against Juventus just three days earlier.

There have never been any questions about his ability. Lavia has the talent to become one of the Premier League’s best midfielders - the biggest question is whether his body will allow him to fulfil that potential.

Romeo Lavia played 90 minutes for the first time in a Chelsea shirt

That is his challenge: staying fit. He has two more opportunities to build up substantial minutes before Chelsea’s season opener, and a steady pre-season would give him the ideal platform to build on in the campaign ahead.

Lavia was lively alongside Caicedo in midfield, providing an assist from a corner, rarely giving the ball away and making eight recoveries.

Completing a game will boost his confidence and provide a platform for greater stability.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest close in on £36m transfer, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest close in on £36m transfer, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Loan star Ronald Araujo to check in at Liverpool

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of completing is loan with option to buy from Barcelona.

The fee on the option to buy for the 27-year-old defender is £47million.

Araujo is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new teammates tomorrow.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre-back and right-back.

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of a loan with option to buy

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a number of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona teammates today prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Full story

Forest on cusp of £36m Diomande move

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36million deal for Sporting Lisbon centre back Ousmane Diomande.

The proposed transfer looked to be off last week but a series of conversations have ironed out differences and the 22-year-old Ivory Coast international is due to travel over this evening ahead of undergoing a medical.

Forest have a five year contract in place for the defender.

Forest centre back Nikola Milenkovic is an option being considered by Juventus while Murillo also has interest from other clubs.

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36m deal for Sporting centre back Ousmane Diomande

Barca set to table new Rodri bid

Barcelona are preparing a new bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their initial £38m offer plus bonuses was dismissed.

City want £68m for the 30-year-old Spain captain.

Barca are looking to find moves for a number of players including Marc Casado, Roony Bardghji, Hector Fort, Alvaro Cortes, Tommy Marques, Ferran Torres, who is bound for Paris St Germain and Ronald Araujo who is off to Liverpool.

Hammers re-enter Solomon talks

West Ham have revived talks with Tottenham over a deal for winger Manor Solomon.

Talks initially broke down over bonuses due if West Ham were promoted which the Championship side thought were unreasonable but the clubs are working towards a £10m agreement.

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14m.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Geronimo Rulli medical at Man City

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is due to undergo a medical at Manchester City on Monday after the clubs agreed a £1.75m deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45m.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16m

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16m plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Paige Spiranac makes rare comment on her dating life... and reveals the two golfers she had 'the biggest crush' on
Sports.content:
Paige Spiranac makes rare comment on her dating life... and reveals the two golfers she had 'the biggest crush' on

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Golf influencer and glamour girl Paige Spiranac opened up about her dating habits in a rare look into her off-screen life.

Spiranac posted a YouTube video entitled 'Confession time' where she answered questions commonly asked by her fans while filming on a golf course in Florida.

The former college golfer, who has a combined 5.7million followers on Instagram and TikTok, revealed that she had a crush on a pair of major champions while she was playing in the junior ranks.

In the video, she name-dropped Justin Thomas and Xander Schauffele as the two golfers who caught her eye.

'I don't really have a type,' Spiranac said. 'But my type is someone who can hit a golf ball really well.'

Later in the video, Spiranac revealed that her list of past beaus is not as long or as dotted with celebrities as some might assume.

Golf glamour girl Paige Spiranac revealed the two PGA Tour pros she had 'the biggest crush' on

She said she fancied Justin Thomas (L) and Xander Schauffele (R) in her junior golf days

Spiranac married an athletic trainer in 2018, but confirmed she was unmarried in 2022

'No, I actually haven't dated anyone famous before,' Spiranac admitted. 'I haven't dated that many people in general. I was homeschooled from fourth grade all the way until college. It was a very sheltered life.'

Spiranac tied the knot with athletic trainer Steven Tinoco in 2018. However, in 2022, the influencer revealed that she wasn't married anymore. It's not clear when the two split.

Before her life on-camera took off, Spiranac played golf at the University of Arizona and San Diego State.

She spurned the chance to turn professional and instead focused on her internet career – becoming one of the most popular social media figures in the sport.

In the video, she added that she wished to keep some parts of her life private and out of the eyes of her millions of followers.

'I have so many supportive people who follow me. I think a lot of people would be really excited if I got married, or if I decided to have children, and that's not the reason why I don't talk about it,' Spiranac said.

'I've just always wanted to keep a section of me to myself.'

Sports.title: Jorge Messi dead at 68: Tributes pour in for father of Lionel after months of health woes
Sports.content:
Jorge Messi dead at 68: Tributes pour in for father of Lionel after months of health woes

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lionel Messi's father Jorge has died at the age of 68, two months on from the family revealing he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

The news was first reported by local media in Argentina, and has since been confirmed by Messi's first team, Newell's Old Boys, in a statement.

Jorge reportedly died in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, at around 10pm local time on Friday August 7.

In the statement, Newell's Old Boys, wrote in Spanish: 'Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.

'Recognized leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andrés Messi. Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

'His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory. Thank you for teaching him to love these colors.

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, has died at the age of 68

Messi cried on the pitch at the World Cup amid his father's long battle with health problems

'The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matías, and María Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment. Farewell forever, leproso.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to Inter Miami and the Messi family for a further statement, and no cause of death has yet been revealed.

In a post on X, CONMEBOL - the governing body of football in South America - added: 'CONMEBOL deeply regrets the passing of Jorge Messi, father of Argentine footballer Lionel Messi. We accompany Lionel, his family, friends, and loved ones with respect and affection in this moment of profound grief. May he rest in peace.'

Football legend Messi was extremely close to his father, who also operated as his agent and de facto business manager throughout his career, overseeing his son's multi-million dollar empire off the pitch.

In recent months, though, the patriarch of the family had been dealing with an as-yet-unconfirmed medical issue that had seen him taken to hospital in his home country.

His illness first came to light when Lionel, 39, cried on the pitch at the World Cup in a rare public display of emotion.

After scoring a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opening group game in Kansas City, Messi was questioned by journalists and said: 'No, honestly it's something completely unrelated to sports. It's been a few difficult days, complicated.'

Just hours later, journalist Eduardo Feinmann explained the reason for the tears in an interview on Radio Mitre, one of the country's most listened-to stations.

'This has to do with his father. His father is not in good health,' he said. 'For quite some time now, several months, since last year.

'And this week there were some situations that slightly worsened his health, and Messi is going through this internal struggle. In other words, like any human being.'

It has since been reported that Jorge suffered a 'medical episode' at his home in January of this year, and he was hospitalized as a result.

Messi's childhood sweetheart Antonela Roccuzzo has supported him throughout his career

Messi stands in front of his family (including father Jorge (third left) in Rosario in October 2003

Jorge arrives at son Lionel's wedding in 2017 with his wife Celia (L) and daughter Maria (R)

In the aftermath, he was said to have undergone cardiovascular and neurological tests, but no official diagnosis was shared by the family, who sought to keep Jorge's health out of the media.

Jorge's health became headline news again in June, when a broadcaster in Argentina falsely claimed he had died - before later issuing an emotional apology and stepping down from her job.

Lionel is the third of four children of Jorge and his wife Celia Cuccittini, and the pair remained together until his death.

They married in 1978 and split their time between Rosario and Miami, where their footballing superstar son currently plays for David Beckham's Inter Miami in MLS.

Before becoming Lionel's agent, Jorge worked for a steel manufacturer in Villa Constitucion, meeting his wife as a young man in Rosario - where the family then grew up.

Messi has two older brothers, Rodrigo and Matias, and a younger sister, Maria Sol.

Jorge has been at Messi's side throughout his historic career, which began in Argentina with Newell's Old Boys, before he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy in 2000.

He became the greatest of all-time in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain - orchestrated by Jorge - in 2021.

After two seasons in the French capital, he moved to MLS and Inter Miami, where he remains to this day at the age of 39.

Jorge remained with his wife, and Lionel's mother, Celia Cuccittini, until his death on Friday

Jorge was Lionel's business manager and was alongside him for the tax fraud case in 2016

Messi gives his father a hug in Fort Lauderdale in November 2025, as his mother watches on

While Lionel's career has been magical on the pitch, it has not been without controversy off it, with Jorge famously by his son's side throughout his tax fraud case in 2016.

The pair sat together in front of the court, with Jorge in his role as his son's business manager, with the prosecution alleging that Messi failed to properly pay tax on income from his image rights between 2007 and 2009.

Ultimately, both father and son were convicted of three tax offenses, initially each receiving suspended 21-month prison sentences.

Jorge's sentence was subsequently reduced to 15 months upon review in 2017 by Spain's Supreme Court, with the pair also hit with substantial fines.

Sports.title: Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup clash with Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations
Sports.content:
Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup clash with Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Sullivan has defiantly attended West Ham's first game of the season at the London Stadium, despite being advised to stay away from home matches after being accused of multiple counts of sexual misconduct.

The club's co-owner and largest shareholder, 77, resigned as co-chair in June ahead of the airing of a BBC Panorama and Times investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour, which he strongly denies.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday that Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into missing West Ham's Carabao Cup clash against Portsmouth on Saturday by 'keyboard warriors', after operators of the London Stadium advised against him attending over fears of potential fan unrest.

West Ham's fan advisory board warned that his presence would cause 'offence and upset', while many inside the club were left staggered upon learning that Sullivan planned to defy the advice and attend.

Sources close to the co-owner told Daily Mail Sport that Sullivan is concerned about the state of the team heading into their first season in the Championship in 14 years and also over the lack of transfer activity in the summer window.

As a result, Sullivan felt he needed to watch the first game of the season, according to sources.

David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium for West Ham's game with Portsmouth

Sullivan was accused in June of preying on a string of women, some in their teens, during his time as a newspaper chief stretching back to the 1980s as seven women came forward to give detailed accounts of predatory behaviour they had experienced, including pressuring them for sex or oral sex by suggesting it would help their careers. Sullivan described the allegations as ‘factually incorrect and entirely false’.

Sources close to Sullivan also claimed he’s received numerous messages from fans urging him to attend despite his presence at matches last season sparking continued protests from spectators against his ownership, including marches, boycotts, sit-ins, black balloons and thousands of fans brandishing red cards.

The Panorama investigation revealed that Sullivan had been banned from contact with West Ham women’s and youth teams for the past three years.

Prior to Sullivan's attendance today, London Stadium’s operator asked to be made aware of any planned visits from the co-owner so it could implement its own safety measures.

West Ham are said to have told the operator that they do not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Sullivan attending the stadium.

Until recently, it appeared as though Sullivan’s grip on West Ham was loosening when it was announced in June that Vanessa Gold, daughter of former co-owner David, had agreed to sell part of their stake in the club to fellow shareholder Daniel Kretinsky. The move that would have seen the Czech billionaire overtake Sullivan as leading shareholder.

Sullivan, with Karren Brady in 1993, resigned as West Ham's co-chair in June ahead of the airing of an investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour

Last week, however, a new announcement confirmed that Gold had accepted a new offer from a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley for her shares. Staveley agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake for £150million, which values the club at around £600million, and would still leave Sullivan as the leading stakeholder.

Staveley, though, has reportedly also made an offer to Sullivan, who is believed to be open to selling his stake in the club but values it at much more.

Sports.title: Phil Parkes dead aged 79: Wolves legend passes away as tributes pour in for record-breaking 'gentle giant' goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Phil Parkes dead aged 79: Wolves legend passes away as tributes pour in for record-breaking 'gentle giant' goalkeeper

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wolves legend Phil Parkes has died at the age of 79, the club confirmed on Saturday.

The former goalkeeper, who chalked up 382 appearances for Wolves during his remarkable 18-year spell at the club, suffered a fall at his home in 2025 and remained under medical supervision until his death, a club statement revealed.

'Legendary Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes sadly passed away this morning at the age of 79,' the statement, posted to the club's website on Saturday, read.

'The Hall of Fame inductee, affectionately nicknamed 'Lofty' due to his 6'4' frame, spent 18 years at Wolves and is known as one of the greatest ever goalkeepers to represent the club.'

Parkes joined the Midlands club as a schoolboy in 1960 and made his senior debut six years later, saving a penalty in a 3-2 victory over Preston North End.

A highlight of his career was helping Wolves reach the UEFA Cup final in 1972, which they lost on aggregate to Tottenham.

Wolves legend Phil Parkes, who played 382 games for the club, has died at the age of 79

Parkes still holds the record for most consecutive league games played at Wolves (127 games)

Parkes still holds the record for most consecutive league games played at Wolves, tallying a remarkable 127 games in a row during the early 1970s.

Following his retirement in 1983, which came five years after his departure from Wolves, he went on to serve on the committee of Wolves' former players association.

His old team-mate John Richards told BBC Radio WM on Saturday: 'It's a sad day, I've had so many calls this morning from former players and friends of Phil just passing on their best wishes and thoughts and prayers to the family.

'You've got to bear in mind Phil has been part of the Wolves family for the best part of 70 years. He's going to be a big loss.

'He was one of the people who would have your back. He looked frightening but he was the opposite. He was a big gentle giant until one of his friends was in trouble and then he was there to protect everybody.

'He was known as Lofty or the big man and he lived up to it in a lot of ways. He had a big heart as well.'

Asked in 2024 how he'd like his Wolves career to be remembered, he said: 'I hope my Wolves career is remembered with joy. I loved playing for this football club, I had a great time, so I just hope all the supporters enjoyed it too.'

Sports.title: South Korea FA says sorry for providing 'sexual services' to foreign referees on multiple occasions
Sports.content:
South Korea's national football association apologised on Saturday after a media report alleged it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees when they were in the country for international matches more than a decade ago.

South Korean broadcaster JTBC reported on Thursday that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had provided such services to foreign referees on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012, including when they were in the country for qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

'We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of,' the KFA said in a statement.

In its news report, JTBC cited a 2016 sports ministry investigation that found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees on seven occasions between March 2011 and March 2012, including trips to massage parlours where the fees had included the costs of sexual services.

The KFA did not immediately respond to an email seeking further comment and details.

'The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,' the KFA said in its statement.

South Korea's early exit at the World Cup group stages caused consternation at home

The allegations add to scrutiny of the association over a separate issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo.

Seoul police raided the KFA's offices on Thursday as part of an investigation related to Hong's appointment, police told Reuters.

Hong returned as national team coach in 2024 after a previous spell in charge from 2013 to 2014. His appointment drew scrutiny after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign candidates and selected Hong following a brief meeting.

The controversy resurfaced after South Korea's disappointing World Cup campaign ended in a group-stage exit.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal transfer twist, Newcastle eye Bruno replacement, Liverpool Araujo detail
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news, updates and rumours from the Premier League and further afield, including deals for Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United

Hello and welcome to the Mirror's live transfer blog on Saturday, August 8.

Arsenal could end up paying through the nose for Cristian Romero this summer, given Tottenham Hotspur will not want to sell their club captain to their North London Rivals. The Argentine centre-half has been touted as potential cover, with William Saliba sidelined for an extended period through a back injury.

However, the Gunners are not the only party interested at present. Inter Milan, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are all thought to me monitoring Romero's situation, and could hold a major advantage in terms of a lesser fee compared to Andrea Berta's outfit.

While Romero is said to be receptive to a move to the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal will likely pay more for his services than other clubs, as a result of their bitter rivalry with Spurs.

Up in the North East, Newcastle United are on the market for a replacement for an outgoing Bruno Guimaraes - who has been announced as Arsenal's latest summer signing following a £75million deal.

Pierre-Emile Hojberg could be exactly what the Magpies are looking for, given the 31-year-old's experience in the English top flight with Spurs and Southampton. It is also understood that Marseille are looking for just £13m to allow the central midfielder to leave ahead of September's deadline.

Liverpool, meanwhile, have secured Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan from Barcelona, as Andoni Iraola looks to bolster his back-line following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid on a free.

It is understood that the Reds also have an option to buy the 27-year-old next summer for £47m, should he impress at Anfield in the coming months.

With all of that being said, stay with us throughout the day for all the latest transfer updates...

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's father, 68, dies as tragic news confirmed in club statement
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's father, 68, dies as tragic news confirmed in club statement

Jorge Messi, a businessman and agent for his superstar footballer son, Lionel, had been ill for a significant period of time and passed away on Friday in his home city of Rosario, Argentina

View 2 Images Jorge Messi has died aged 68 (Image: X)

Lionel Messi's father has died at the age of 68 following a long battle with illness. Jorge Messi passed away in hospital on Friday in his home city of Rosario, Argentina.

‌



His family said during the World Cup in June that Jorge had been dealing with a 'health-related situation'. Lionel's former club, Newell's Old Boys, have now confirmed his passing.

‌



A statement published on Saturday read: "Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario. Recognised leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andres Messi.

‌



"Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini. His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Jorge Messi was his son's agent (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



"Thank you for teaching him to love these colours. The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matias, and Maria Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment."

Speculation about Jorge's health and wellbeing was rife throughout the World Cup, as Argentina reached the final before losing to Spain in extra-time. It was even falsely reported that he had died after his son was seen crying during Argentina's 3-0 win against Algeria in the group stage.

"Why was I crying? It had absolutely nothing to do with football," Lionel said post-match. "I have had a few difficult days."

‌



A subsequent statement read: "The Messi family wishes to inform you that Jorge Messi is currently dealing with health problems. He is currently under medical supervision and is recovering well.

"Given the reports, rumours and speculation that have been circulating in recent hours, the family wishes to express its deep concern about the lack of sensitivity, respect and discretion with which some people have treated a strictly private family matter."

Jorge played an instrumental role in his son's career, serving as his agent from the beginning. He travelled to Barcelona with a 13-year-old Lionel and the rest - such as eight Ballon d'Or awards, four Champions League wins and 13 domestic league titles - is history. He is survived by his wife, Celia Maria, sons Lionel, Rodrigo and Matias, and daughter Maria Sol.

Article continues below

Argentine club Rosario Central also paid tribute by posting on social media: "El Club Atletico Rosario Central deeply regrets the passing of Jorge Messi. We accompany with respect and affection Lionel, his family, and all his loved ones in this painful moment. May he rest in peace."

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Lewis Hall update as Newcastle make training camp decision
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Lewis Hall update as Newcastle make training camp decision

Newcastle United have a decision on Lewis Hall's pre-season involvement amid ongoing Man Utd transfer speculation

View 2 Images Manchester United have been linked with a summer transfer swoop for Lewis Hall. (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall has been sent home from their warm-weather pre-season training camp in La Manga nursing a minor injury. The 21-year-old, who is a transfer target for Manchester United this summer, has returned to Tyneside, with the rest of his teammates set to take on Valencia this evening.

‌



The Magpies having already knocked back an initial approach from Michael Carrick's side and remain resolute that Hall will not be offloaded this summer. Newcastle have already lost Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon during the current window.

‌



Eddie Howe's exit from the club has only fuelled further conjecture surrounding Hall's future, though the club have stressed Hall won't be sold.

‌



The left-back is a key part of both the club and Matthias Jaissle's plans for this season, as the new German head coach plans his St. James' Park rebuild.

Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chronicle Live reports that Hall and fellow defender Fabian Schar have been granted time away following the warm-weather camp in La Manga to recuperate from their respective injuries.

‌



The England international has been carrying out a separate training programme from his Newcastle teammates in Spain, concentrating on upper-body work.

Hall will play no part for new head coach Jaissle in his first match at the helm against Valencia this evening.

View 2 Images Man Utd are interested in signing Lewis Hall this summer. (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

‌



Man United are believed to be eager to bring in a new full-back this summer, with Carrick holding Hall in high regard.

Recent reports suggest the defender would welcome a move to Old Trafford if a fee could be agreed, though Newcastle have taken a firm stance following a turbulent summer of departures.

The Reds have also been connected with a potential swoop for Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas.

‌



Nevertheless, the La Liga outfit have made it plain the 19 year old will only be offloaded if his £13.7million release clause is triggered.

Barcelona have also been associated with a move for the defender, having had an offer turned down earlier this summer.

Luke Shaw remains United's first-choice at left-back, with Carrick choosing to deploy Patrick Dorgu in a more attacking role and the club are eager to bolster that area of the defence.

Sports.title: Stevenage 'set standard' as Alex Revell lauds Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe
Sports.content:
Stevenage 'set standard' as Alex Revell lauds Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe

Stevenage progressed to the second round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2016 with Friday's 2-1 victory over Wycombe at Adams Park, leaving manager Alex Revell full of praise for his side

View 2 Images Stevenage manager Alex Revell was pleased with his side's performance in Friday's Carabao Cup defeat of Wycombe

Stevenage manager Alex Revell said Friday's Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe is "the standard" for his side this season as they progressed to the second round for the first time since 2016.

‌



The Boro secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over their hosts at Adams Park thanks to a 95th-minute winner from summer signing Josh Magennis, ensuring they would get their 2026-27 campaign off to the perfect start as they look to build on last season's play-off finish in League One.

‌



On the same night, Wolves defeated League Two outfit Port Vale 3-0 and Middlesbrough beat Wrexham 1-0 in an all-Championship affair, while a further 29 Carabao Cup first-round fixtures are set to take place today.

‌



Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend READ MORE :

Stevenage, who finished five places and 12 points ahead of Wycombe (11th) in the third tier last season, were certainly made to work for their victory, however, as the Chairboys responded well to going behind in the 27th minute.

Both sides could have arguably put the game to bed during the first half, and it looked as though the tie would be heading to a penalty shootout following a relatively lackluster second half, but veteran forward Magennis popped up in the dying seconds to steal the win for his new side.

Following the game, Revell said he was "really pleased" with Stevenage's overall performance, having demanded a certain standard from his players heading into the new campaign.

‌



"For us, we wanted to set a standard, and we have certain demands to maintain what we achieved last year and try to be better," Revell told The Mirror. "There's no better feeling than winning. For us, it was a really good challenge and really nice to start the season with a win."

What made things even better for Revell, a former Stevenage player himself, is that the winner came from not just one of his new signings, but one of his substitutions, as Magennis came off the bench to head home the winner.

"You look a genius, don't you?" he laughed. "Really pleased for Josh, he's worked really hard. When you get good delivery and timing, and somebody wants to score a goal, it’s a great ending to the game for us.

‌



"We just have to get our head down and keep doing what we've been doing throughout pre-season, working as hard as we can to keep improving. Tonight, there were signs of that as well, and we'll look to keep that winning mentality going."

View 2 Images Wycombe manager Michael Duff was left rueing his side's missed opportunities to win the game

As for Wycombe, they will look to quickly bounce back with a victory in their opening League One game of the season away to Blackpool next week, though manager Michael Duff couldn't help but rue the missed opportunity for his side on home soil.

Article continues below

"The players said it themselves at halftime, we need to be better in both boxes," Duff told The Mirror. "We missed a load of chances and given them a really, really cheap goal.

"Ultimately, they didn't execute what we wanted in terms of being better in both boxes; that's why we've ended up losing the game."

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel hit with new Man Utd training ground ban as he's forced to break rank
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel hit with new Man Utd training ground ban as he's forced to break rank

Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel is continuing his rise at the club but also must adhere to a Premier League rule during training

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel recently made his unofficial Manchester United debut during pre-season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel has been unable to don the club’s new training kit sponsor due to gambling regulations. United recently announced a £20million per year deal with Betway, which sees the gambling company sponsoring the squad’s training gear.

‌



The agreement was possible due to a loophole in the new Premier League rule set to take effect in the 2026/27 season, which bans gambling companies from serving as front-of-shirt sponsors. The rule change was initially agreed upon back in April 2023, but the ban does not prevent gambling companies from appearing on shirt sleeves and training kits, as well as in stadiums.

‌



When announcing the Betway deal, United’s chief business officer Marc Armstrong said: "The scale of our exciting new partnership reflects our growth strategy, the enduring global strength and appeal of Manchester United, and our ability to attract leading brands that want to engage with our vast worldwide fanbase."

‌



However, Premier League rules prevent rising star Gabriel from wearing the new training kit sponsor. The 15-year-old, alongside any other under-18 player in the Premier League, is not allowed to wear kit which promotes gambling companies.

It is not the first rule that Gabriel has had to navigate as the teenager continues his ascent at United. The young forward is also forced to change separately from Michael Carrick’s squad due to safeguarding regulations.

‌



However, that has not stopped Gabriel from already making his mark this summer. He was given his unofficial first team debut as a late substitute against Atletico Madrid at the start of the month.

Gabriel is eligible to play in the Premier League this season, as he will turn 16 during the campaign, though he will be unable to sign a professional contract until he is 17. The youngster impressed his United teammates after making his debut against Atletico.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
