World.title: The federalism that promotes productivity (2), By Dipo Baruwa
World.content:
Ultimately, federalism succeeds not merely because power is decentralised, but because authority, incentives and capability are deliberately aligned to make productivity the basis of political success. When states compete to build institutions, attract investment, develop people and expand their productive frontiers, rivalry becomes developmental. It is through that alignment, not constitutional perfection, that productive capabilities are built, locational comparative advantages emerge and sustainable development becomes possible.

Productive Federalism

Productive federalism is not a race to duplicate identical industrial parks, airports, universities or government-owned enterprises. While such investments are not inherently negative, the use of scarce resources requires a more strategic rather than reactive process through which states identify their economic opportunities, coordinate public and private investment around them, develop the required capabilities, and progressively construct locational advantages. The aim is not competition for appearances but for measurable outcomes.

How many sustainable businesses have been created? How many firms have expanded or reinvested? Has agricultural output per hectare improved? Have logistics costs declined? Are technical institutions producing the skills demanded by local industries? Has the state attracted complementary firms around an emerging sector? Has internally generated revenue expanded because productive activity has increased, rather than merely because taxes and levies have multiplied? This requires capable institutions that can identify external opportunities, connect them to local capabilities and ensure that the benefits become embedded within the domestic economy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

This distinction is important because Nigeria has sometimes confused productive rivalry with politically motivated aggrandisement. States compete to announce the largest airport, the most imposing government building, the newest university or the most ambitious industrial project, even where the economic foundations required to sustain those initiatives are absent. The result is rivalry in expenditure, rather than in capability.

A productive federation would reward governments not for the scale of their announcements but for the durability of the economic systems they create. Public investment would be judged by whether it reduces production costs, improves access to markets, expands knowledge, raises labour productivity and attracts further private investment. Political success would be increasingly connected to economic outcomes, rather than to the ability to distribute patronage or commission conspicuous projects. Unfortunately, the latter is the lived reality of the Nigerian polity.

What is Behind the Cry of Local Government Autonomy?

This also has implications for the relationship between states and local governments. The same authority–incentive–capability framework that applies between the federal and the state governments must also apply within the states themselves. Nigeria cannot build a genuinely productive federation, while local governments remain institutionally marginal to development.

Many services closest to communities, including basic infrastructure maintenance, local markets, primary healthcare support, community libraries, sanitation, local economic information and aspects of agricultural extension, require functioning local government institutions. Yet state governments have progressively absorbed functions and revenues without always providing a more effective replacement. Authority has become concentrated, accountability has become blurred, and local governments have been left with limited incentives or capability to shape development within their jurisdictions.

States should be able to compare themselves transparently on investment attraction, education quality, healthcare delivery, agricultural productivity, infrastructure maintenance, business survival, internally generated revenue and employment creation. Successful reforms undertaken by one state should be documented and adapted by others. Governors should face not only electoral comparison within their states but developmental comparison across the federation.

The question is, therefore, not simply whether local governments should receive allocations directly. It is whether authority, revenue, responsibility and accountability can be aligned at the level in which particular public services and developmental functions can be performed most effectively. Direct funding without capability and accountability may simply reproduce the same distributive weakness at a lower level. But denying local institutions meaningful authority also removes an important layer of experimentation, information gathering and development implementation – basic ingredients for building the federation’s institutional capability to generate, synthesise, and utilise local economic information for national development.

Productive federalism, therefore, requires clarity about who is responsible for what, the resources available for performing those responsibilities, and the outcomes by which performance will be assessed. Where authority is assigned without financial or administrative capability, failure becomes inevitable. Where revenue is provided without responsibility and accountability, distribution becomes an end in itself.

This is also where institutions such as the Nigeria Governors’ Forum should assume a more developmental role. The Forum should not function principally as a platform for political bargaining with the Federal Government or for coordinating common positions on revenue allocation. It could become an institution for productive peer review among states.

States should be able to compare themselves transparently on investment attraction, education quality, healthcare delivery, agricultural productivity, infrastructure maintenance, business survival, internally generated revenue and employment creation. Successful reforms undertaken by one state should be documented and adapted by others. Governors should face not only electoral comparison within their states but developmental comparison across the federation.

Kenya’s experience with county-level devolution offers a useful, though imperfect, illustration. Counties have increasingly been compared on healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and service delivery. Rwanda, although not a federation, has used performance contracts to connect subnational administration with measurable outcomes. The lesson for Nigeria is not to copy either country, but to recognise that decentralised authority becomes developmental only when performance is visible, comparable and consequential.

The Federal Government also has an indispensable role. Productive federalism does not imply a weak or indifferent centre. It requires a centre that concentrates on functions that benefit from national coordination: macroeconomic stability, national infrastructure, interstate commerce, competition policy, national standards, external trade relations, security coordination, research and the provision of public goods that individual states cannot efficiently supply alone.

The debate before Nigeria is therefore not simply whether to restructure the federation, but what kind of federalism the country wishes to practise. A federation organised predominantly around distribution will continue to produce political competition for existing wealth. A federation organised around productive capability will encourage competition to create new wealth.

The centre should also generate and distribute economic information, coordinate national and subnational institutions, remove barriers to interstate production and trade, and ensure that equalisation supports minimum standards without extinguishing incentives for subnational initiative.

Redistribution remains necessary. Nigeria’s states possess different resource endowments, populations, revenue capacities and historical advantages. A federation cannot ignore these differences. However, redistribution should provide a foundation from which less-advantaged states can build capabilities; it should not become a permanent substitute for productive effort. Equalisation should enable participation in development, not institutionalise dependence on allocation.

The debate before Nigeria is therefore not simply whether to restructure the federation, but what kind of federalism the country wishes to practise. A federation organised predominantly around distribution will continue to produce political competition for existing wealth. A federation organised around productive capability will encourage competition to create new wealth.

Conclusion

The argument throughout this series has been simple. Many of the constitutional and institutional ingredients for productive federalism already exist within Nigeria’s governance framework. What remains deficient is not merely constitutional design, but the governance architecture needed to align authority, incentives and institutional capability.

As Nigeria approaches another general election cycle, this debate should not be ethnicised or reduced to slogans about “true federalism.” Nor should it become a contest between those who support redistribution and those who advocate production. Every viable federation requires both. The real task is to design a system in which equitable redistribution strengthens rather than weakens the incentive to produce.

Ultimately, federalism succeeds not merely because power is decentralised, but because authority, incentives and capability are deliberately aligned to make productivity the basis of political success. When states compete to build institutions, attract investment, develop people and expand their productive frontiers, rivalry becomes developmental. It is through that alignment, not constitutional perfection, that productive capabilities are built, locational comparative advantages emerge and sustainable development becomes possible.

Dipo Baruwa is a business climate development analyst.

World.title: NYSC, khaki and the fight against drug abuse, By Fatih Lawal‑Garu
World.content:
Many young Nigerians see NYSC as a one‑year ritual — khaki, clearance, CDS, and monthly allowances. But my experience taught me something deeper. National service is not about the uniform. It is about the impact made while wearing it… It is about recognising problems around us and choosing to act. It is about using our skills, creativity and passion to improve communities. It is about leaving behind footprints that outlive the service year.

A week before the United Nations International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, I walked into the PRNigeria Centre expecting nothing more than another ordinary newsroom assignment. I had no idea that a simple instruction — “Put on your khaki; we’re heading out” — would pull me into an experience that would redefine my understanding of national service and the responsibility that comes with wearing the NYSC uniform.

The PRNigeria Centre is not a typical newsroom. It is a place where ideas breathe, where books are born, and where young people are challenged to think beyond headlines. Corps members do not just file reports; they write books, lead campaigns and contribute to national conversations. I had seen this culture firsthand through publications like Youth Service for National Stability, Diplomacy and Digital Innovation, and anti‑drug, anti‑smuggling campaigns. These works, authored by corps members, made me quietly determined to leave my own mark before my service year ends.

But I did not expect that opportunity to arrive so suddenly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Our destination was the NDLEA FCT Command, where Deputy Commander Aliyu Omama joined us before we proceeded to Parliament Secondary School and Government Secondary School, Apo. The mission was simple: educate students about the dangers of drug abuse under a campaign titled “Promoting Drug‑Free Schools: A Corper Initiative.”

The initiative was led by Abdulhameed Yushau Shuaib, a fellow Mass Communication graduate from Bayero University, Kano, serving at NITDA. Listening to him speak, I realised this was not just another awareness programme. It was a heartfelt intervention driven by a young Nigerian who refused to watch his peers fall victim to addiction, peer pressure and the deceptive glamour of drug use on social media.

What struck me most was his conviction. He was not complaining about the problem — he was confronting it.

Deputy Commander Omama delivered a message that was both sobering and necessary. He explained how drug abuse fuels domestic violence, armed robbery, kidnapping, banditry and other crimes that plague our society. He listed commonly abused substances — cannabis, cocaine, methamphetamine — using both scientific names and street slang the students recognised instantly.

Yet he did not present addiction as a dead end. He spoke about rehabilitation, recovery and reintegration, reminding the students that help exists, but prevention is always better than cure. His final message was simple: never experiment with drugs.

Representing NITDA’s Director General, Mrs Deborah Dada urged the students to reject drugs and embrace digital skills. She reminded them that technology offers limitless opportunities, which are far more rewarding than any temporary high. Her praise for Abdulhameed’s initiative underscored a powerful truth: national service is not about where you are posted, but what you choose to do with your posting.

Their engagement surprised me. They asked thoughtful questions, exchanged contacts, and expressed genuine interest in future programmes. I left the schools convinced that something meaningful had begun.

But the campaign was only halfway done.

Then came a competition that became a movement. An essay and quiz competition was announced across FCT schools. The response was overwhelming: 87 essays submitted. Editors reviewed each one carefully, screening out plagiarism and AI‑generated content to reward originality and genuine understanding.

On 26 June — the UN Day Against Drug Abuse — the grand finale took place at the PRNigeria Centre.

Ozor Kamsy of Federal Government Boys College, Wuye won the essay competition, followed by Arafat Ismail and Nafisat Abbas. Their presentations showed depth, clarity and a maturity far beyond their age.

The quiz competition was equally intense. Questions covered causes, consequences, prevention, rehabilitation and global efforts against drug abuse. As I watched, I realised how much I still had to learn.

Jamal Oyawoye of Badr Integrated School emerged winner, with Nicodemus Gideon and Salma Musa taking second and third place.

This is a campaign with a future. Partner organisations pledged to sustain the initiative. The Programme Coordinator of Youth Against Disaster Initiatives (YADI), Umar Farouk Bala, announced plans to expand future editions to include disaster preparedness, digital citizenship and public safety. NYSC representative, Mrs Rukayya Abu, praised the organisers and described Abdulhameed’s project as a shining example of meaningful national service.

Her words captured the essence of everything I had witnessed. The True Meaning of National Service.

Many young Nigerians see NYSC as a one‑year ritual — khaki, clearance, CDS, and monthly allowances. But my experience taught me something deeper. National service is not about the uniform. It is about the impact made while wearing it.

It is about recognising problems around us and choosing to act. It is about using our skills, creativity and passion to improve communities. It is about leaving behind footprints that outlive the service year.

That single instruction to wear my khaki took me beyond the newsroom and into a movement. It showed me the power of youth-led advocacy and reminded me that the true measure of NYSC is not the duration of service, but the difference made during it.

I arrived expecting a routine assignment. I left with a renewed understanding of responsibility, purpose and the transformative power of national service.

Fatih Lawal‑Garu is a Corps member serving in Abuja. Email: [email protected]

World.title: “Aren’t We All PR People?”: Setting a new benchmark for communicators, By Yushau A. Shuaib
World.content:
For emerging communicators, this book will serve as a mentor. For educators, it will be a teaching companion. For practitioners, it will be a reminder of the discipline’s core values. And for the profession at large, it will be a contribution that strengthens the intellectual and practical foundation of PR in Nigeria.

Ahmed Balarabe Sa’id’s new book, Aren’t We All PR People?, is one of those rare works that immediately announce themselves as more than textbooks. It is a field guide, a mentor in print, and a career compass for anyone stepping into the demanding but rewarding world of Public Relations. After carefully reviewing the book, I am genuinely tempted — without any flattery — to call it the definitive PR career guide for emerging communicators. It is a standout resource that sets a new benchmark for the field.

Balarabe, a Mass Communication graduate of Bayero University Kano (BUK) more than two decades ago, is not merely a communication scholar, he is a true PR professional in every sense of the word — far beyond regulatory certification. Calling him a practitioner feels almost inadequate because he breathes, speaks, writes, and conducts himself with the instinctive discipline of someone who genuinely lives and promotes Public Relations through his relationships, engagements, and professional ethos.

What makes this book remarkable is not only its breadth but its narrative style. Balarabe writes with a clarity that demystifies PR practice and a warmth that draws readers into the profession’s human side. His storytelling approach, just like my recently released memoir, MNI Versus MNIPR in NIPSS, creates curiosity, making even foundational principles feel fresh and urgent. For budding communicators who often encounter PR as abstract theory, this book offers something different: a vivid, practical, and relatable journey into the craft.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Several chapters carry uniquely crafted titles that immediately spark curiosity and offer clear glimpses into their thematic direction. Chapter One, “From Ancient Rhetoric to Digital Dialogue,” sets the tone by tracing the evolution of communication from classical persuasion to today’s fast paced digital exchanges. Other standout chapters — “A Constellation of Concepts,” “Professionalising the Practice,” “That Good PR Practitioner,” “A Universe of Opportunities,” “Some of Your Mentors,” “Ethical Traps and Hidden Dangers,” “You and AI,” and “PR Shots” — present their subjects with clarity and creative framing. PR Shots, in particular, is an engaging compilation of short, sharp professional posts originally shared on social media, now curated into a chapter that reads like a pocket guide for daily practice. The final chapter, which foregrounds the emerging role of Public Relations in Nigeria’s national project, provides a thoughtful and forward looking conclusion — positioning PR not just as a profession but as a strategic pillar in nation building.

The book succeeds on multiple fronts. First, it bridges the gap between theory and practice. Many PR texts lean heavily on academic frameworks, leaving young practitioners unsure how to apply them in real world situations. Balarabe flips that script. He grounds every concept in lived experience — crisis moments, ethical dilemmas, communication landmines, and the subtle art of managing reputation. The result is a book that teaches not only what PR is but how PR is done.

Second, the book is structured to guide readers through the profession with increasing depth. From foundational ethics to the anatomy of a good practitioner, from crisis communication to the evolving role of AI, each chapter builds on the last with intentional clarity. The inclusion of real personalities — role models whose careers illuminate different pathways in the field — adds a human dimension that young readers will find both inspiring and instructive.

Third, Balarabe demonstrates a rare courage in addressing contemporary issues. His challenge to the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) on the absence of AI regulation is bold and necessary. His exploration of digital crises, misinformation, and emerging technologies shows a practitioner who understands that PR is evolving rapidly — and that the next generation must be prepared for a landscape far more complex than what existed a decade ago.

The book also shines in its treatment of ethics. Balarabe does not present ethics as a checklist but as the backbone of professional credibility. His insistence that ethical grounding must precede technical skill is a message young communicators urgently need. In a world in which speed often competes with accuracy, and visibility competes with integrity, this emphasis is both timely and timeless.

One of the book’s strongest features is its use of narrative to teach principles. Balarabe’s stories — of practitioners, crises, institutions, and turning points — are not decorative. They are instructional. They show how PR works in real life, how reputations are built and broken, and how communicators must think, act, and adapt. This narrative approach makes the book accessible without sacrificing depth.

The book is also refreshingly honest. It does not romanticise the profession. It acknowledges the pressures, the politics, the ethical crossroads, and the emotional labour involved in communication work. Yet, it balances this realism with optimism, reminding readers that PR remains one of the most impactful careers for those who master its principles.

For emerging communicators, this book will serve as a mentor. For educators, it will be a teaching companion. For practitioners, it will be a reminder of the discipline’s core values. And for the profession at large, it will be a contribution that strengthens the intellectual and practical foundation of PR in Nigeria.

In my sincere assessment, this book is more than a guide. It is a benchmark. A resource that will inspire, instruct, and challenge. A book that emerging communicators will return to repeatedly as they navigate their careers.

And truly, Aren’t We All PR People is a book our profession has been waiting for.

Yushau A. Shuaib, an award-winning PR practitioner, is the author of MNI Versus MNIPR in NIPSS- Tackling Institutional Bullying. Email: [email protected]

World.title: AES criticises Tinubu’s comment on regional security
World.content:
The Alliance of Sahel States (AES) has criticised President Bola Tinubu for his comment, attributing Nigeria’s growing security crisis in part to insecurity in neighbouring states.

The AES — made of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso — considered Mr Tinubu’s remark “simplistic,” “hasty”, and trivialised the states’ efforts to address terrorist operations in the Sahel.

Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Karamoko Traore, disclosed the AES’s stance on Thursday during a meeting with the Chargé d’Affaires of the Nigerian embassy in Burkina Faso.

President Tinubu made his comment last week while discussing the military operation that led to the rescue of pupils and teachers kidnapped in Oyo State. He linked the growing insecurity in the country and the resurgence of kidnapping to the security situation of its neighbours in the Sahel.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Some of them (the terrorists) are not Nigerian. You see, the problem of insecurity in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger only exacerbates our difficulties,” he said.

The three, in response to this, summoned the Nigerian Chargé d’Affaires for a meeting in Ouagadougou.

At the meeting, Mr Traore stated that Mr Tinubu’s “surprising” remark downplayed the sacrifice of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso in the fight to curb armed groups.

He also claimed the comment minimised the role played by the Nigerien army in the fight against Boko Haram.

He pointed out that Niamey was already facing the Boko Haram threat even before the emergence of large-scale terrorist insecurity in the other countries of the Alliance.

“Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, and Nigeria are facing the same enemy.

“We would have preferred a more accurate presentation of the security situation, rather than placing the blame for a complex situation on neighbouring countries, at the risk of fuelling misunderstandings and frustrations between peoples bound by history, geography, and fraternity,” the minister said.

Nigeria’s relations with Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso have been fraught since the 2023 military coup in Niger and the subsequent deterioration of relations between the AES and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the three countries officially exited ECOWAS in early 2025. This was after a year-long effort by the bloc to convince them to reconsider leaving.

The juntas in all three nations had accused ECOWAS of failing to support them in their fight against terrorism and of imposing sanctions that they claim harmed their populations.

Due to the strained relations, security cooperation also suffered, particularly along Nigeria’s borders with the three Sahelian countries.

The fragmentation of regional security arrangements has made intelligence sharing, joint operations, and cross-border coordination more difficult.

However, the Nigerian government has been pushing for cooperation with the AES to counter cross-border criminal networks operating in the region.

Last week, Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, called for joint regional action between the AES and ECOWAS to combat insurgency in West Africa.

Mr Musa stated that confronting West Africa’s complex security landscape requires an inclusive, coordinated front.

World.title: 2027: Kogi East APC Stakeholders Back Tinubu, Ododo, Demand Power Rotation
World.content:
• Say East will no longer be appendage to any political bloc

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kogi East Senatorial District have declared their total support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, while demanding a fresh and equitable framework for political power rotation in Kogi State.

The stakeholders, who spoke through a communiqué issued at the end of their Strategic Leadership Conference in Abuja and made available to THISDAY on Saturday, said Kogi East would no longer accept a political arrangement that relegated the senatorial district to the status of an appendage of another political bloc.

They also called for direct negotiations with political stakeholders from Kogi Central and Kogi West on what they described as “distinct, transparent and equitable” terms to establish a predictable framework for power transition and inclusive development in the state.

The stakeholders said their immediate priority was to ensure victory for the APC in the January/February 2027 general election, particularly the re-election of Tinubu and the victory of all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats.

They further pledged to mobilise support for Governor Ododo’s re-election for a second term in the November 2027 governorship election.

According to them, the political objective was not merely to win elections but to reposition Kogi East within the mainstream of state and national politics and secure what they described as the “deserved share of development” for the district.

The communiqué noted that Kogi East had recorded the highest bloc vote for President Tinubu among the three senatorial districts of Kogi State in the 2023 presidential election, stressing that the district was prepared to increase its contribution to the APC in 2027.

He said: “We look forward to increasing our electoral contributions to the APC and to strengthening our collaboration with our fellow compatriots from Kogi Central and Kogi West Senatorial Districts to return power to Kogi East.

“However, we are resolved to mobilise total support for the incumbent governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, and his re-election for his second term come

2027.”

The declaration came against the backdrop of what the stakeholders described as more than a decade of political fractures, disaffection and missed opportunities in Kogi State following the 2015 governorship election and the death of the late former governor, Prince Abubakar Audu.

They said attempts to achieve political realignment in 2019 and 2023 were not sustained, leaving ordinary citizens of Kogi East to bear the consequences of prolonged political disagreements.

The stakeholders insisted that the time had come to heal the wounds, rebuild trust among the three senatorial districts and establish a new political understanding based on equity, inclusion and mutual respect.

They said: “We refuse to allow old wounds to permanently damage the deep historical linkages between the people of the various sections of Kogi State.

“Our only path to reawaken the political strength of Kogi East is to encourage healthy collaboration with the other sections of the state and negotiate truthfully for all that our people deserve.

“We reject any attempt to make Kogi East an appendage of any group in the state.”

The stakeholders invoked the political legacy of Prince Audu, saying his philosophy was anchored on statewide unity, inclusion, dialogue and equitable distribution of development.

They recalled that during Audu’s administration, major projects were conceived and executed across the three senatorial districts, including the establishment of the state university in Anyigba and the Obajana Cement Project, as well as roads and other civic infrastructure.

They argued that the late governor’s political philosophy should be revived as the foundation for a new era of cooperation in Kogi State.

“That is the true political philosophy we must revive today: vision, selflessness, courage, fraternity, equity and shared purpose,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders also demanded an immediate shift towards a predictable political transition arrangement, arguing that sustainable development could not be achieved where political succession remained a source of tension.

According to them, “We assemble here today to lay a solid foundation for Kogi East to be part of a realistic, predictable and harmonious political transition in Kogi State.

“We call for an immediate shift towards building consensus, renegotiating power transfer and rotation, and establishing an inclusive, development-driven agenda that guarantees equitable access to the instruments of power.”

The group also sought national recognition for Audu, describing him as a statesman whose contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development should not be confined to his final years in politics.

It urged the Kogi State Government to present Audu’s contributions to the Federal Government for a “highly merited and long-overdue national honour”.

The stakeholders cited the 10th anniversary commemorative events held in Lokoja in October 2025, which brought together national political leaders, traditional rulers and former governors, as evidence of the late governor’s enduring national stature.

They also noted the naming of a major boulevard in Lokoja after Audu by Governor Ododo and the unveiling of the Prince Abubakar Audu Leadership Foundation by the representative of President Tinubu at the anniversary events.

The stakeholders called for the foundation to operate as a nationwide, non-partisan platform for preserving Audu’s memory and promoting his leadership philosophy.

They argued that restricting his legacy to one election cycle or the final period of his political career would amount to historical injustice.

“Prince Audu belonged to multiple eras of Nigeria’s democratic development, from his early public service to his trailblazing leadership as the first and second civilian executive governor.

He must be remembered as a statesman,” they said.

In their resolutions, the stakeholders pledged to unify APC grassroots structures across the nine local government areas of Kogi East behind Tinubu and all APC legislative candidates in the 2027 elections.

They also committed themselves to dialogue with political leaders in Kogi Central and Kogi West, stressing that such engagement must be conducted on mutually acceptable and equitable terms.

The stakeholders further resolved to align with the state government to promote peace, inclusivity and accelerated development across Kogi East.

They called on party leaders, youth leaders, elders and other members of the late Audu’s political family to put past grievances aside and work towards a united political front.

“Our goal is to reintegrate Kogi East into the mainstream of politics in Kogi State and the nation on terms that will assure us of our deserved share of development,” they declared.

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Abia Leadership Academy, Strategic Institution For Training Future Leaders, Says Gov
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, says the Abia State Leadership Academy was established as a strategic institution where ethics, values, and practical leadership skills would be instilled in Abia youths.

He said the essence was to catch them young, adding “we are committed to getting it right with the younger generation. Otherwise, our wider development efforts will be in jeopardy.”

Governor Otti, represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, spoke while declaring open the 2026 Youth Leadership Bootcamp of the Abia State Leadership Academy. The batch has 1, 000 participants selected from 7, 000 applicants. The training holds every long vacation at Government College, Umuahia, since the Otti administration came to power.

The governor reaffirmed his commitment to developing young Abians as future leaders of the state and nation and charged the participants to learn with humility and participate actively in the programme.

“This year’s programme is particularly significant, with 1,000 participants selected from more than 7,000 applicants. That response tells us our young people are hungry for genuine transformation—and they trust this administration to deliver it.

“For 2026, we’ve partnered with the Enterprise Development Centre of Pan-Atlantic University—a global-standard institution with ties to the World Bank, Goldman Sachs, and MasterCard.

“To our young participants, your selection is only the beginning. I urge you to learn with humility, participate actively, build meaningful relationships and, most importantly, use what you learn to positively influence your schools, communities and State,” the Governor said.

Earlier, the facilitator of the programme and Chairman of Abia State Civil Service Commission, Pastor Mrs. Eno Jerry –Eze, represented by Rev. Mrs. Ifeoma Agu, said that the programme was an opportunity to for the youths to imbibe the ideals of civic responsibility and urged the participants to be determined to use the lessons of the bootcamp to better their lives as well as bring about the change they crave for.

Mrs. Jerry-Eze thanked the governor for placing the youths in the leadership map in Nigeria and for leaving a legacy that assures that the leadership he has introduced would be sustained.

Delivering a lecture on the theme of the training: ‘The Demands of Stewardship’, the Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, noted that the governor was investing in the lives of the teenagers and young leaders of the state through the academy.

Pastor Ajagba, while describing the initiative as a strategic investment in the future of the state and a lasting legacy that will shape the character, mindset and leadership capacity of generations yet unborn, disclosed that by intentionally preparing young people for responsible leadership, Governor Otti was laying a firm foundation for sustainable development and ensuring that the ideals of integrity, innovation and public service remain deeply rooted in Abia’s future.

He added that it was an honour for all those invited to share their perspectives in the noble vision of raising a generation of principled, disciplined and transformational leaders through the academy and applauded the exemplary life of vision, focus, sacrifice, discipline, competence, integrity of Governor Otti and assuring of the unwavering commitment of the Governor to good governance and purposeful leadership.

Also speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the development partner – the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC), Pan-Athlantic University, Dr. Uche Egbuna, said the future of every society depends on the quality of leaders it intentionally develops, adding that leadership was about responsibility, integrity and service.

Dr. Egbuna stated that the boot camp was built on four key pillars: leadership and service, enterprise, impact and innovation, and encouraged participants to strive for meaningful impact by becoming problem-solvers and change-makers.

He described the partnership with the Abia State Leadership Academy as a shared commitment to developing ethical leaders, resilient entrepreneurs and innovative young people who will contribute to economic growth and social transformation.

President of Abia State Leadership Academy, Prof. Kenneth Kalu, disclosed that 7052 persons applied for the programme and about 1000 were qualified after the rigorous processes of selection.

Prof. Kalu enjoined the participants to remember that they were expected “to think, reflect and become” future leaders, emphasising that what was more important was not that they participated in the programme but what they become from the programme.

Responding on behalf of the participants, Chukwuemerie Obiorah and Treasure Ogbonna thanked the governor for the opportunity given them to become transformational leaders, assuring that they would not disappoint but make good use of the bootcamp to better citizens in the society.

The opening ceremony of the bootcamp being coordinated by the Programme Manager, Abia State Leadership Academy and Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Public Communication, Mr. Dodoh Okafor, was graced by Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Emmanuel Meribeole; Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Prof. Uche Emeh Uche; Principal Secretary and Chief Strategist Officer of the state, Mr. Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, among other government officials.

World.title: Just In: DSS Arrests Three More Suspects Over Kidnap of Nasarawa Varsity Professor
World.content:
Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) have arrested three more suspects linked to the kidnapping of the Dean of Agriculture at Nasarawa State University, Professor Samuel Avengbe Okunsebor.

The suspects were arrested on Friday night at a local brothel along the Mararraban Akunza axis of the Lafia–Makurdi highway.

A security source disclosed that the three suspects were members of the kidnapping gang responsible for the abduction of the university don.

Professor Okunsebor was kidnapped by gunmen in the early hours of Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at Mile Uku, a border community between Lafia and Nasarawa-Eggon Local Government Areas of Nasarawa State.

He was rescued two days later by DSS operatives. Two suspects, including a woman, were also arrested in connection with the incident at the time.

According to a security source, the newly arrested suspects were identified as 25-year-old Yakubu Abubakar, also known as Black or Starboy, a member of the Doemak tribe in Plateau State; 37-year-old Usman Abubakar Mairiga; and 27-year-old Sale Babauro Abubakar.

The source said Mairiga is Hausa, while Sale Babauro Abubakar is Fulani.

The three suspects are currently being held at the DSS State Command for further investigation.

The source added that their continued detention followed a warrant obtained from a magistrate’s court.

The latest arrests bring to five the number of suspects reportedly apprehended in connection with the kidnapping of Professor Okunsebor. Investigations into the incident are ongoing.

World.title: Bianca, Great Asset To Humanity, Says Gov Otti
World.content:
Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, has said that Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, is a huge asset not only to the Igbo nation but also to Nigeria, and humanity.

This was contained in a birthday message the governor sent to Nigerian former Ambassador to Spain, where he also enjoined her to continue to uphold the virtues and character that have distinguished her and made her an admirable amazon.

The governor’s birthday felicitations to the minister was endorsed by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma. The former Beauty Queen celebrated her birthday on August 5, 2026.

Governor Otti described Ambassador Ojukwu as an amazon who has distinguished herself in many facets of human endeavour, noting she deserves to be celebrated.

He recalled that the minister supported the struggle for Abia’s redemption, starting from when he first ran for governor on the platform of All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), adding that she is “an honest, just, and courageous Nigerian who has represented womanhood diligently and positively.”

“On a day like this, I feel excited to celebrate my sister and friend, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, on the occasion of her birthday. She is a woman of strong will and courage. An amazon from the East who has distinguished herself in many facets and continues to prove that, with courage and character, nothing is too big for any human being to accomplish,” the governor stated.

He noted that her appointment as Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, “her commitment and accomplishments were already outstanding and commendable.”

The governor assured Ambassador Ojukwu that he would continue to support and stand by her at all times as she strives courageously to write more success stories in her eventful life and wished her a happy birthday, while praying that she would live long in good health to celebrate many more beautiful years ahead.

World.title: Adeleke Commends Monarch Residents  On Osun-Osogbo Festival
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The world-famous Osun-Osogbo Festival was held yesterday with more than 500,000 participants from all over the world.

Osun-Osogbo Festival is celebrated in August every year at the Grove. The festival attracts thousands of Osun worshippers, spectators and tourists from across the globe.

The Osun-Osogbo Festival is a two-week celebration of culture, spirituality, and heritage held annually in Osogbo, South West Nigeria.

Speaking on this year festival, Osun State Governor, Senator Ademola Adeleke, commended Oba Jimoh Olanipekun Oyetunji, Larooye II, Ataoja of Osogbo, and all sons and daughters of Osogbo at home and in the diaspora on the celebration of the Osun-Osogbo Festival.

The governor described the annual festival as a priceless cultural and spiritual heritage that reflects the enduring bond between the people of Osogbo and the sacred River Osun, celebrating centuries of history and faith.

He noted that the festival remains one of Africa’s foremost traditional festivals and a proud symbol of Yoruba civilisation.

The governor stated that the sacred procession led by the Arugba, the royal presence of the Ataoja, the traditional rites at the Osun Sacred Grove, the prayers, chants, and cultural displays all represent our culture and preserved heritage across generations while projecting Osun State to the global stage.

Adeleke commended the monarch, Ataoja of Osogbo, the Osun Priestess (Iya Osun), the Arugba, traditional institutions, devotees, cultural custodians, and the entire people of Osogbo for sustaining a festival that has continued to attract visitors, researchers, and tourists from across the world.

“On behalf of the Government and the good people of Osun State, I heartily felicitate with Kabiyesi, His Imperial Majesty, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun Oyetunji, Larooye II, Ataoja of Osogbo, and the entire people of Osogbo on this year’s Osun-Osogbo Festival.

“As we celebrate this sacred tradition, may the blessings of Osun continue to bring peace, prosperity, and progress to our dear state.”

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to preserving Osun’s rich cultural heritage and protecting the Osun Sacred Grove as a globally treasured heritage site.

He added that the administration will continue to support initiatives that promote tourism, cultural diplomacy, and economic opportunities for the people accordingly.

World.title: Opata Defends Tinubu’s ‘All Is Fair in Politics’ Remark
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

A Professor of African Literature at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), Prof. Damian Opata, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s recent remark that “all is fair in politics,” arguing that the expression is neither new nor peculiar to Nigeria’s political history.

He urged Nigerians to consider the remarks within their historical and philosophical context.

Opata, who is also the National Chairman of the South East Movement for Tinubu 2027, said the expression derives from the popular saying, “All is fair in love and war,” which he traced to John Lyly’s Euphues: The Anatomy of Wit.

According to a statement issued on Thursday, he said he had no objection to the memorandum presented by the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria and read by its President, Bishop Matthew Ndagoso.

He said the bishops demanded free and fair elections, improved security and good governance for the common good, while also requesting the return of schools to their original proprietors and the extension of constitutional guarantees of freedom of religion. He noted that President Tinubu responded by highlighting improvements in the education and security sectors, explaining that the issue of returning schools rested with state governors and reaffirming that freedom of religion is guaranteed by the Constitution.

He added that the bishops applauded the President’s response by clapping at four achievements of his administration.

Opata said President Tinubu’s assertion that “all is fair in politics” reflected “his brutal courage in speaking and acting on truth and reality,” although he acknowledged that critics were justified in arguing that, as President, such an expression could send the wrong signal because he embodies the nation’s conscience and ethical standards.

He further argued that the bishops’ address should not have focused solely on the President and the All Progressives Congress, maintaining that all political parties share responsibility for ensuring free and fair elections.

According to him, the President’s remark is reducible to the Machiavellian principle that “the end justifies the means,” a doctrine rooted in political pragmatism that has found expression in institutions such as universities, churches, the police, the civil service and the business sector.

Commenting on reactions that followed the meeting, including an interview granted by Cardinal John Onaiyekan, Opata urged the media and the public to exercise restraint, saying attention should remain on the substantive issues rather than peripheral matters.

He concluded by calling on the ruling party, opposition parties and Nigerians to avoid conduct that reflects either “the end justifies the means” or “all is fair in politics” as the country prepares for the 2027 general election, expressing the hope that doing so would help guarantee free and fair polls.

World.title: EU, PLAC Charge Nigerian Youths to Demand Transparency, Accountability
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The European Union Delegation to Nigeria and the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre (PLAC) have asked Nigerian youths to demand transparency and accountability from public institutions.

Speaking at a Model Legislative Assembly Session in Abuja, Programme Manager for Democracy, Rule of Law and Gender at the EU Delegation, Laolu Olawumi, said Nigeria’s democracy can only deepen when young people insist on accountable governance at all levels.

“This internship is not just about producing future politicians. It is about forming citizens who understand governance and how to engage it,” she said.

Olawumi told participants that democracy goes beyond elections to include lawmaking, oversight, citizen participation, and consensus building in a diverse country like Nigeria.

She urged them to use the knowledge gained to explain governance processes to their communities.

“You are now ambassadors of Nigeria and representatives of your communities. A second thing I want you to focus on is continuing to hold institutions accountable,” she added.

Executive Director of PLAC, Clement Nwankwo, said the internship exposed participants to the realities of lawmaking, representation, oversight, legislative research and the day-to-day operations of the National Assembly.

He noted that the programme would equip beneficiaries to interrogate those in leadership and contribute meaningfully to national development.

Also speaking, the Clerk of the National Assembly described the PLAC legislative internship as one of Nigeria’s foremost platforms for grooming young professionals with practical knowledge of legislative practice and democratic institutions.

The programme was organized by PLAC with support from the EU Support to Democratic Governance Programme.

World.title: Teen elated as GoFundMe exceeds R2m: ‘Give and you will receive’
World.content:
Young Wernand has recieved over R2m in a GoFundMe campaign. Images via Instagram

A teen boy known as Wernand, who appeared in a viral BI Phakathi video, has pledged to share the funds raised through a GoFundMe campaign with his family and others living in destitution.

The 14-year-old has received over R2 million in donations from around the world.

GOFUNDME CAMPAIGN SURPASSES R2 MILLION FOR TEEN WERNAND

In recent days, a GoFundMe campaign set up for young Wernand, seen in a BI Phakathi video, has exceeded R2 million.



The campaign has raised $128 200 (over R2 million) from donors around the world.

Wernand touched the hearts of the public after he was spotted gathering scrap metal and old tyres to sell to raise money to help his family. At the time, the 14-year-old lived in a dilapidated house with no walls or roof.

In an updated video, Wernand appeared to be living in a safer home, filled with food and groceries.



The overjoyed teen vowed to continue supporting his mother, baby sister, and all those living in destitution.

He said, “I don’t have the kind of heart to say no. I don’t know how to say no.

“Even if I have a R2 in my pocket….

Wernand added that his grandmother had instilled in him a life lesson to help the less fortunate.



He added, “If you give, you will receive”

WHO IS BI PHAKATHI?

Good Samaritans BI Phakathi and US philanthropist Logan Mayberry are credited for helping young Wernand secure food and a safe home via the GoFundMe account.

While Mayberry is widely known through his Reward The Kind charity endeavour, Phakathi has kept his identity a secret from ordinary South Africans. 

Through his foundation, the Phakathi aims to “help people who need help in these difficult times”.

He says of himself: “The South African motivational speaker, filmmaker, and life coach BI Phakathi lends just a hand, without showing his face.

“BI has maintained his reputation as a mysterious giver to the underserved on the streets. In his videos, he helps the underprivileged and homeless people with resources. Bi believes in maintaining anonymity while adding value to society”.

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns confirm the signing of Bafana Bafana forward
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns have confirmed the signing of Cassius Mailula, with the forward returning to the club after three years away.

The 25-year-old has rejoined the Brazilians after spending the past three years with MLS side Toronto FC.

For weeks, there had been speculation that Mailula could return to Masandawana. With the departure of Peter Shalulile, his return allows the talented striker to finish what he started with the Tshwane giants.



“A familiar face returns to where it all began. Cassius Mailula is back in yellow, ready for a new chapter with The Brazilians. Masandawana, welcome him back in the comments,” Mamelodi Sundowns said on social media.

The Brazilians have been relatively quiet during this transfer window. Following the untimely passing of midfielder Jayden Adams, their pre-season was delayed, meaning they were unable to begin their Betway Premiership campaign last weekend.

Mailula’s arrival gives Sundowns another attacking option and adds more firepower to their frontline. He will compete alongside the likes of Tashreeq Matthews, Iqraam Rayners and Brayan León.

Mamelodi Sundowns re-signs Mailula

Before leaving Sundowns for Toronto FC in July 2023, Mailula enjoyed a breakthrough 2022/23 campaign, scoring 16 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions.

However, he made only a handful of appearances for Toronto before being loaned to Wydad Casablanca, where he played under former Sundowns coach Rulani Mokwena.

His spell in Morocco proved successful, with the forward scoring important goals for the North African giants.



Mailula later had another loan spell in Belgium before eventually returning to Mamelodi Sundowns following the end of his time with Toronto FC.

The Bafana Bafana forward now has an opportunity to revive his career at the club where he first made his name and once again establish himself as one of the country’s most exciting attacking talents.

Will Mailula shine or flop?

World.title: ‘As it was before COVID’: Pensioners push to have payment date reversed
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries have renewed calls for the agency to shift grant payment dates back to the start of each month, with commenters arguing the current system leaves pensioners short-changed for longer than necessary.

In response to a The South African article, Nola Van Loggerenberg raised the payment date issue head-on, comparing the current system unfavourably with pre-pandemic practice.

“At least the pensioners don’t have to wait 33 days next month for SASSA to pay out. The date should be moved back to the first of every month as it was before COVID,” she wrote.



Money doesn’t stretch far enough

Beyond the date itself, beneficiaries say the money doesn’t last once it hits their accounts. Mary Coetzee summed up the financial squeeze many pensioners face in stark terms: “Yes, that money lasts just one day.” Caroline September agreed the strain begins immediately, adding “Not just one day..up..the moment you take it out”, suggesting that for many, the grant is spent before it even reaches their pockets properly.

Caregiver and disability grant frustrations surface

The thread also surfaced deeper concerns about how SASSA assesses grant applications. Daisy Moodley shared her own experience applying for a caregiver-related grant, describing what she felt was an unreasonable expectation from officials. “OMW, they don’t give the caregiver money, apparently they want to see you in a wheelchair, my doc said yesterday. I went to fill the form saying I look so fit, 76, yet I cannot walk without someone holding me, I have a misbalance, got pins and needles in my knee,” she wrote, a comment that drew sympathetic reactions from other users.

Meanwhile, Machiliza Nomthandazoe raised a separate practical concern, asking for guidance on updating banking details on behalf of an elderly relative: “Plz help what do they need at Sassa my granny want to change her banking details.”

Together, the comments paint a picture of beneficiaries juggling delayed payments, insufficient amounts, and confusing administrative processes, all while trying to make ends meet on a fixed monthly income.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.content:
Orlando Pirates team vs Milford FC at the Orlando Amstel Arena. Image: Orlando Pirates media

76′ Kgositsile’s header goes slightly wide with the keeper beaten. The score remains Orlando Pirates 1-1 Durban City!

71′ Kgositsile’s curling shot flies too high and wide.

68′ Maswanganyi strays offside after Mbatha plays a brilliant pass.

62′ Appollis takes a freekick but City keeper Sangare makes a comfortable save.

55′ Yellow card! Maswanganyi is booked after a foul on Sanger.

52′ Goal! Lubumba taps in from the six yard box. Great play from Shandu and Sirino onthe right to create the chance. Orlando Pirates 1-1 Durban City!

50′ Appollis is caught offside after a intricate pass from Sebelebele.

45′ The second half is underway.

HALF TIME

47′ Half Time! The referee sends the two sides to the break. The score remains Orlando Pirates 1-0 Durban City!

45′ Third official adds two minutes from stoppage time.

37′ Moremi shoots from the edge of the box but the shot flies too high.

37′ Goal! Orlando Pirates take the lead. Maswanganyi with a cooly taken penalty that sent Sangare the wrong way.

33′ Penalty kick for Pirates! And a red card for Durban City. Poggenpoel takes down Moremi. Poggenpoel also gets his second yellow and is sent off.

30′ Sibisi is stretched off the pitch, before quickly making his return to the park.

28′ Lubumba breaks on the counter before shooting wide of Chaine’s goal. The score remains Orlando Pirates 0-0 Durban City!

27′ Big miss by Mbuthuma in the box. A wonderful cross by Maswaganyi but Mbuthuma’s contact was not strong enough to direct the ball into the net.

24′ The Buccaneers win a free kick 30 yards from goal. Poggenpoel foul on Dansin.

22′ Both teams struggling to find their rhythm. The score still reads Orlando Pirates 0-0 Durban City!

20‘ Mbatha takes a shot from distance. Sangare tips it over for a corner.

17‘ Yellow card! City’s Poggenpoel gets booked for a late challenge on Mbatha.

14′ Maswanganyi gets the crowd roaring with a little showboating. .

9′ Pirates win a corner after a run from Moremi. The short setpiece is cut out by Durban City.

5′ Sanger’s hits a volley that goes wide of Pirates‘ goal.

3′ The Buccaneers launch a fast counter attack but Moremi’s cross is too close to keeper City’s keeper Sangare.



1′ – Kick-off! We’re underway at the Orlando Amstel Arena. Orlando Pirates vs Durban City in the MTN8 quarterfinals!

MTN8 QUARTERFINAL: ORLANDO PIRATES VS DURBAN CITY

Orlando Pirates starting line up: Chaine, Sibisi (captain), Seema, Sebelebele, Ndaba, Mbatha, Dansin, Maswanganyi, Appollis, Moremi, Mbuthuma.

Substitutes: Dladla (GK), Kgositsile, Masilela, Zulu, Mokobodi, Mthiyane, Radiopane, Lungu, Hotto.

Durban City starting line up: Asare, Msomi, Mokone, Ncanana, Shandu, Poggenpoel, Sanger, Nodada, Sifumba, Sirino, Lubumba.

Substitutes: Dreyer, Gcaba, Maseko, Mthembu, Mofokeng, Makua, Morris, Green, Domingo.

13:00: The team buses have arrived at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

14:00: Starting line ups to be confirmed

15:00: Match kick off.

The Soweto giants enter the clash with history firmly in their sights as they chase a record-breaking fifth consecutive MTN8 title. Orlando Pirates began their remarkable run in 2022, defeating AmaZulu 1-0 in the final. Monnapule Saleng scored the decisive goal to secure the Buccaneers’ first trophy under former coach Jose Riveiro.

They successfully defended their crown in 2023, overcoming Mamelodi Sundowns on penalties after a goalless final. Goalkeeper Sipho Chaine proved to be the difference, producing three crucial saves in the shootout.

Orlando Pirates continued their dominance in 2024, defeating Stellenbosch FC 3-1 in the final to become the first club in the PSL era to win the MTN8 three seasons in succession.

The Buccaneers extended that remarkable record last season under Abdeslam Ouaddou. They defeated Stellenbosch FC 3-0 after extra time, with Tshepang Moremi scoring twice as Pirates secured their fourth consecutive crown and 14th MTN8 title overall.

DURBAN CITY EYE UPSET

Durban City head to Soweto determined to prevent another chapter being added to Pirates’ remarkable cup history. The Nedbank Cup holders have strengthened their squad under new coach Khalil Ben Youssef. They will believe they have enough quality to challenge the defending champions.

The Citizens also know they can frustrate the Buccaneers. They held Orlando Pirates to a goalless Betway Premiership draw when the sides last met.

Victory on Saturday would take Orlando Pirates one step closer to an unprecedented fifth straight MTN8 crown, while Durban City will be targeting a major quarter-final upset at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs mourn tragic passing of former star Michael Nkambule
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have paid tribute to former star Michael Nkambule, who tragically passed away on Friday.

The 37-year-old former footballer was involved in a car accident approximately two weeks ago. The vehicle he was driving reportedly overturned, leaving him seriously injured.

After spending two weeks in hospital, the former Chiefs midfielder sadly succumbed to his injuries, as reported by Soccer Laduma.



On Saturday, his former club paid tribute to Nkambule, remembering him as a product of the Kaizer Chiefs academy.

“Kaizer Chiefs Football Club and the entire Kaizer Chiefs family deeply regret the passing of Michael Nkambule, a former academy graduate and player for the Kaizer Chiefs first team from 2007 to 2010,” the club said in a statement.

“A product of the Kaizer Chiefs academy, who earned a move to France in 2003 after impressing scouts with his performances for the Kaizer Chiefs U15 team at the Milk Cup tournament in Northern Ireland.”

Ex-Chiefs star Nkambule dies

“Kaizer Chiefs wishes to express its condolences and support to his family, friends, and former teammates. May his soul rest in peace.”

After leaving Chiefs, Nkambule went on to represent Black Leopards and SuperSport United. However, the midfielder’s professional career did not reach the heights expected of him, and he retired before turning 30.

Despite ending his professional career early, Nkambule remained deeply involved in football and regularly featured in legends’ matches.



Which match made you a fan of Nkambule?

World.title: Medication or rent? Pensioners reveal the impossible choices R2400 forces on them
World.content:
Frustration among South African pensioners is boiling over, with beneficiaries taking to Facebook to demand an urgent increase to the Older Persons Grant, insisting the current payout is nowhere near enough to cover the basics.

Commenting under a recent The South African article on SASSA payments, Annamarie Otto laid out the brutal arithmetic pensioners face every month.

“R5000 would help us so much. Some medication costs more than R1000. Then rent…food, and the rest follows. R2420 is not enough. How can we survive???” she wrote.



Her frustration was echoed by Vani Deevichand, who framed the grant shortfall as a matter of basic human dignity for older people.

“Really speaking, old age is literally saying… the last few years of their lives …make them happy and help them live comfortably, after 60 is bunsela years God gives grace …DO THE RIGHT THING, GOVERNMENT…. R5000 IS NOT A LOT…COST OF LIVING IS HIGH,” she said.

Calls for R5000 grow louder

The demand for a R5000 grant wasn’t an isolated complaint – it was a rallying cry repeated across the comment section. Mlungisi Donda put it simply: “We now demand R5000 grant for the older people.”

Nola Van Loggerenberg went further, tying the grant amount to broader dissatisfaction with SASSA’s payment schedule, arguing that pensioners deserve both consistency and a livable amount.

“Sassa old pensioners need a decent increase up to R5000. No one can survive on R2400 a month, everything is expensive in South Africa,” she wrote, adding that “Government should do the right thing and look after these old age pensioners.”

Patience wearing thin

Not everyone believes change is coming any time soon. Casper Janse van Rensberg was blunt about his scepticism, joking, “You will only receive that R5000 once the Donkeys are out and the Horses are back”, a comment that captured the weary cynicism running through the thread.



Whether government responds to the mounting pressure remains to be seen, but one thing is clear: pensioners are no longer prepared to suffer in silence over an amount they say simply isn’t keeping up with the cost of living.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Cameron Waldeck-Cooks appears carefree in video before ‘murder’
World.content:
Cameron Waldeck-Cooks in a video captured before her death. Images via TikTok

Cameron Waldeck-Cooks was seen dancing with a group of pals, just days before her death, in a video posted on TikTok. The St Stithian Grade 11 learner was allegedly killed in a murder-suicide involving former matriculant Ethan Coetzee.

The teens’ bodies were discovered in a Sabi game lodge in Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August.

Police have confirmed that an initial inquest has been upgraded to a murder charge.



CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS LAST DAYS

In a tribute posted by a pal on TikTok, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks joyfully danced alongside a group of friends

The blonde teen appeared happy and carefree, blissfully unaware of what would transpire a few days later.

“Here’s to you, my Cam”, her pal captioned the clip.



In the comments section, another friend added: “To think this was just a week ago”.

Watch the video here.

According to a statement from her family, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks would spend the weekend with another family at a lodge in Sabie on a hiking adventure.



On Monday, 3 August, her body and that of her alleged boyfriend, Ethan Coetzee, were discovered by his father

An independent forensic pathologist’s preliminary findings indicated that Cameron died as a result of strangulation and suffocation. Police have stated that Ethan, who was 19-years old, may have died by suicide.

BRIGHT FUTURE AHEAD

Both Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee’s lives were tragically cut short in the double tragedy,



Cameron, a St. Stithians Girls College Grade 11 student, was working towards the Gold level of The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment, which is part of the Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award.

She was also in the rowing and netball clubs and was described as a “natural leader” and a “big sister”.

Meanwhile, Ethan – who matriculated in 2025 – had been part of the first team rugby club, was a national champion in the equestrian sport of Eventing, and was a respected senior student at Penryn House.

World.title: ‘Chiefs will be eliminated by Arrows’ – Junior Khanye predicts
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs winger Junior Khanye has backed Golden Arrows to knock Amakhosi out of the MTN8 in the quarter-finals.

Chiefs return to the competition after missing out on the previous two editions. They will host Arrows on Sunday afternoon, knowing that victory would take them one step closer to lifting the trophy they last won 12 years ago.

However, Khanye remains unconvinced by Chiefs despite their impressive 3-1 victory over Kruger United in their opening match of the season last weekend.



The outspoken analyst has predicted Chiefs to suffer a narrow defeat against Arrows and exit the competition.

“For me, Chiefs will be eliminated from the tournament,” Khanye said.

“The tournament for them is unfortunately eight teams. I don’t predict a heavy score, but there is also a possibility of extra-time in this game. I think Chiefs will be eliminated if we face reality.



“Arrows will beat Chiefs, but they will narrowly edge them. I predict Arrows to win this game, but it’s going to be a tough match,” he told iDiski TV.

Khanye has also backed defending champions Orlando Pirates to beat Durban City in Saturday’s other MTN8 quarter-final.

The former Chiefs star believes the Buccaneers have enough quality to retain the trophy, which they have won four consecutive times.



Chiefs to lose to Arrows, Pirates to retain trophy, says Khanye

“Pirates are favourites,” Khanye said ahead of the MTN8 clash with City.

“They haven’t changed their team a lot. Even though they lost their star player Relebohile Mofokeng, they beefed up their squad. I know Sundowns are a threat to any team, but there’s something we call momentum. Pirates started the season very well.

“I think, for me, Pirates will defend the MTN8. It’s straightforward,” he said.



Chiefs host Arrows on Sunday while Pirates and Durban City battle it out on Saturday afternoon in Soweto.

Will Amakhosi go through?

World.title: Pitso Mosimane named as new Bafana coach
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pitso Mosimane is set for a return to the Bafana Bafana dugout.

The South African Football Association has approved his appointment as the new national team coach following the departure of Hugo Broos.

The decision was ratified at a Safa National Executive Committee meeting, with members backing Mosimane to take charge of the side that recently made history at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

South Africa reached the knockout rounds round for the first time, highlighted by a memorable victory over South Korea.

While SAFA said a few administrative details still need to be finalised, an official announcement is expected next week.

Mosimane was previously in charge of Bafana in a caretaker capacity in 2007 and from 2010 to 2012.

World.title: RFA flags enforcement gaps in freight sector
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Road Freight Association CEO Gavin Kelly said stronger enforcement is crucial to ease tensions over foreign driver employment in South Africa’s freight sector.

With truck driver associations threatening a freight shutdown, Kelly argued the issue begins with how companies are registered and monitored.

“We are not taking the right steps when we initially register companies. When we register companies, do we ask those companies who are their employees, before we allow the company to be registered?

“We need to ask questions like are you registered with the council that is applicable to your sector of business so that we have inspectors going to all the companies that are active in that sector.

“What happens now is that inspectors to companies they are aware of and that’s the real reason we have been struggling with this. Secondly, the deterrent has to meet this problem. It doesn’t help if you get rid of these foreign nationals and they reappear or the company just employs other foreigners because that destroys the operation of the sector in totality," Kelly said.

World.title: Coalition decisions will be crucial - Mnguni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The race is on for political parties to garner votes ahead of the November local government elections.

But the reality is many municipalities may end up with coalition governments.

Rise Mzansi said fixing Johannesburg starts with principled leadership, transparent coalition agreements and no deals with parties tainted by criminality.

City of Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni said they work based on principles and coalition agreements ought to be signed.

“I do think that people are exceedingly disappointed in how the ANC is governing this city.

The ANC will probably have a huge task to justify why it must be included in a coalition. But those are conversations that become more material when you see the actual results.

“But I think starting with principles, quality of leadership, coalition agreements, and ensuring that residents have a much more transparent path to coalition formation than we have had previously,” Mnguni said.

World.title: Recovering Marchand to skip medleys at European swim champs
World.content:
PARIS - Swimming star Leon Marchand has cut back on the events he will compete in at the European championships starting Monday because of a lingering thigh injury.

The French federation confirmed Saturday that Marchand will not compete in the 200m and 400m individual medley events in Paris.

The Frenchman had already ruled out the 200m breaststroke but remains entered in the 200m butterfly and 400m freestyle that place less strain on the adductor muscles.

He may also participate in one or two relays with the French team.

"The injury is healing well, and recovery is largely complete. However, since competing in the 200m and 400m individual medley carries a non-negligible risk of recurrence, and to safeguard the remainder of the competition, the decision was made not to enter these races," explained team doctor Sebastien Le Garrec.

The four-time Olympic champion injured his adductor during the 200m breaststroke heats at the French championships in June, subsequently withdrawing from the rest of the competition.

He suffered a setback during a training session in Marseille three weeks later.

Earlier this month, he had confirmed his participation in the European championships, though he was doubtful regarding the 400m individual medley.

Ultimately, he decided to withdraw from the shorter distance as well as a precautionary measure.

The withdrawal from his two signature events is a major setback for the 24-year-old, who had made these championships the primary goal of his season.

He had also stated he wanted to break his own world record in the 400m individual medley this season.

"It's something I want to do in the near future, and I imagine doing it in Paris at the European championships would be great," he had said.

World.title: MotoGP leader Martin speeds to British Grand Prix pole
World.content:
LONDON - MotoGP world championship leader Jorge Martin set a new lap record on his way to pole position for both Saturday's sprint race and Sunday's British Grand Prix.

Spanish rider Martin was not only the fastest in Saturday's midday qualifying session in perfect conditions at the Silverstone track, but also broke the all-time lap record with a time of 1min 56.160sec.

It was the second time in two days that the record fell after Martin's Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi blitzed to 1min 56.280sec in practice on Friday despite fracturing a collarbone at the German MotoGP last time out.

Italian Bezzecchi will start fifth on the grid for Saturday's 10-lap sprint race and Sunday's 20-lap Grand Prix.

Behind Martin are compatriot Raul Fernandez, riding another Aprilia for the Trackhouse team, just 0.021sec behind, followed by Japan's Ai Ogura and Italian Fabio Di Giannantonio.

The Marquez brothers, Marc and Alex, round out the top seven.

Marc Marquez revived his title defence by winning in Germany and is only 18 points behind Martin in the standings, and four points adrift of second-placed Ogura.

The top five in the championship race, with Bezzecchi in fourth and Di Giannantonio fifth, are separated by just 24 points.

The sprint race takes place at 1500 GMT.

World.title: Zwakele Mncwango named ActionSA’s eThekwini mayoral candidate
World.content:
KWAMASHU - ActionSA President Herman Mashaba pledges consistency as he urges eThekwini residents to back the party in November’s local government elections.

He told voters they can expect the same governance ActionSA delivers in Tshwane.

He spoke in KwaZulu-Natal as ActionSA unveiled its mayoral candidates.

"We are appealing to people of eThekwini, if they want to see the kind of governance that we are experiencing in the City of Tshwane under Dr. Nasipi Moya, that's what they will get,” Mashaba said.

ActionSA has positioned itself as the alternative to corruption, political patronage and unfulfilled promises.

Tshwane Mayor Nasiphi Moya said ActionSA is ready to govern eThekwini Municipality.

The party has announced its mayoral candidates for eThekwini, KwaDukuza, and Newcastle ahead of the local government elections.

“Today is about declaring that ACTIONSA is ready to govern,” she said.

Mashaba named Zwakele Mncwango as the party’s mayoral candidate in eThekwini.

Mncwango will spearhead ActionSA’s campaign in the metro ahead of November’s elections.

The party joins a crowded field as parties intensify their campaigns for eThekwini.

World.title: POPCRU demands firm response to Reiger Park cop killers
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Police and Prisons Civil Rights Union (POPCRU) has the brutal killing of two members of the South African Police Service’s Anti-Gang Unit in Reiger Park, Ekurhuleni, on Friday.
