World.title: Prague 7 Plans Floating Swimming Pool on the Vltava in Holešovice
World.content:
A floating swimming pool could be built along the Vltava River in Prague’s Holešovice district, near U Vody Park.

Prague 7 City Hall is considering using a section of the waterfront near the Port 7 development for the project.

The municipality hopes the pool could be ready within three years, although the cost has not yet been determined.

The project is still in its early stages. The district is currently looking into whether it could obtain older or unused pontoons and adapt them to create the swimming facility.



One of the main questions is where the pool water would come from. Prague 7 is considering both the Vltava and the municipal water supply.

The aim would be to use this data to determine when swimming in the river is considered safe. Čižinský has suggested introducing a simple traffic-light system similar to those used in cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam, allowing swimmers to see whether conditions are suitable.

According to Čižinský, the Vltava generally has good enough water quality for swimming, although conditions can deteriorate after heavy rainfall.

Recent measurements support this concern. Prague hygiene officials have been monitoring the water at Branická beach since the beginning of this year. The water has generally received a rating of two on the five-level scale used by hygienists.

The Holešovice proposal is not the first plan to introduce a floating swimming facility on the Vltava.

A similar idea was included in an earlier proposal to transform Prague’s riverfront. The project near Vyšehrad envisaged a large floating structure measuring 69 by 7.5 meters, with a swimming pool and a smaller paddling pool. A second connected vessel would have provided facilities for visitors.

The proposal was later put aside. In 2025, Prague property councilor Adam Zábranský of the Pirates said the investment was not among the city’s priorities.

World.title: Construction Disrupts Prague Tourists and Businesses During Peak Summer Season
World.content:
Construction projects across Prague’s historic center are proving a pain for tourists and locals alike who say the clumps of dirt, building supplies and equipment block popular sites and make it difficult to move around one of Europe’s most visited cities.



Heading down Národní to the Charles Bridge or going for a beer near the Vltava river now looks more like a vast construction site where tourists need to look out for more than the cobble-stone streets and baroque spires.

“It’s their first time here too, [they’ve] never seen it and now it’s torn up,” said Sherryl, a tourist visiting from the United States with her friends.

A major source of the disruption are upgrades to the public transport system. The central tram route delivering travelers to the heart of the city near the Národní Divadlo stop has been shuttered for weeks.

The disruption has taken a heavy toll on surrounding businesses like Aggeo, an Italian grocery store along the corridor. Its manager, Irena Kumpová, noted a sharp drop in foot traffic from travelers and regular local customers, who stroll by the National Theater on their way to gaze at the artist David Černý’s famous Kafka head.

“I’d rather stay closed… it’s a catastrophe,” remarked Kumpová.

With tourism growing every year in Prague, the widespread construction is making its mark this summer. So far this year, 1.7 million people have visited Prague, marking the strongest start in 15 years, according to Prague City Tourism and the Czech Statistical Office.

Tram services are suspended through the city center, clogging the streets and forcing many to find another way to work or home. For businesses that rely on heavy foot traffic during the busiest months of the year, that means less earnings.

“I have a table outside, but mainly just to signal to people that we’re open, but no one sits there right now,” said Kumpová.

The reconstruction is part of Prague’s broader effort to modernize its transport network, including long-term investments such as the future tram connection to Wenceslas Square and the expansion of Metro Line D as the city seeks to expand public transport.

Not everybody minds the disruption. The loud machines, dusty air, and obstructed sidewalks offer a certain charm for some who view the construction as part of the sightseeing experience.

“Despite the construction, it’s still beautiful,” said Raluca Costachescu, a traveler from Romania.

Written by: Mae Bryant, Bilyana Spasova, Milica Petrušová, Zuzana Kormančíková, Zhanna Bekiryan

World.title: Live Nation and PPF to Run Three Major Prague Venues
World.content:
Live Nation and PPF Group are forming a joint venture that will operate three of Prague’s major event venues — O2 Arena, O2 Universum and Forum Karlín.

The companies plan to invest in the venues and upgrade their facilities, with Live Nation set to hold a 51 percent stake in the new company.

The agreement will bring together one of the world’s largest live entertainment companies and PPF, the investment group that owns O2 Arena and O2 Universum through its subsidiary Bestsport.



PPF has also operated Forum Karlín, which has been owned by Patria Investment Company since last year.

The companies announced the planned partnership in a joint statement. Financial details of the transaction and the amount of the planned investment have not been disclosed. The deal remains subject to the required regulatory approvals.

Under the agreement, the new operator will be responsible for the day-to-day running of all three venues, including event planning and programming. The venues themselves will remain under their existing ownership structures, and their names will not change.

The partners said they intend to invest substantially in the facilities over the coming years. The aim is to improve conditions for audiences and performers while expanding the number of events held in Prague and strengthening the city’s position on the international concert and entertainment circuit.

PPF said the cooperation with Live Nation is also part of its strategy of developing the long-term value of its assets alongside major international companies.

Live Nation Entertainment operates across several areas of the live entertainment industry, including concert promotion, ticketing and sponsorship. Its businesses include Live Nation Concerts, Ticketmaster and Live Nation Sponsorship.

PPF Group is an international investment company with holdings across Europe, North America and Asia. Its portfolio includes telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, e-commerce, industry and biotechnology.

World.title: Prague to Restore Tram Service Between Holešovice and City Center
World.content:
Residents of Prague 7 will regain a tram connection between Holešovice and the city center from September, with tram line 5 set to operate through the district and continue toward Wenceslas Square.

The change follows months of pressure from Prague 7 officials and local residents, who have called for better tram connections since the cancellation of line 14.

The district had previously requested either the return of line 14 or the introduction of an equivalent service and organized a petition supporting the demand.



The new arrangement will initially be temporary. According to the Prague Integrated Transport (PID) system, two trams will operate on the route at least through December 2026.

Line 5 to replace temporary route

The new service is linked to planned transport changes in Žižkov. Because of a traffic closure there, tram line 34 will be replaced by line 5 in Holešovice.

At Holešovice train station, line 5 will connect with line 6, effectively creating a continuous service between the two routes. Trams will run from the station through the Holešovice area, past the market and across Vltavská Street before continuing toward Wenceslas Square and other parts of central Prague.

For passengers in Holešovice, the move restores a connection that was lost when line 14 was discontinued.

Service could change again next year

The situation between January and June 2027 has not yet been fully settled. According to PID, the final arrangement will depend in part on discussions between the incoming leaderships of Prague 3 and Prague 7.

Maintaining the additional tram service in Holešovice during that period could require limited reductions elsewhere in Prague 3. Another option would be to temporarily return to the existing arrangement using combined tram lines 6 and 34.

PID has warned that permanently combining lines 5 and 6 could also create delays at both ends of the route. Such a change could affect passengers travelling through Prague 2 and Prague 5, even though it would provide the direct connection sought by Prague 7.

World.title: “Ivan, Go Home!” Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
World.content:
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.

The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.

The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.



The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.

The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.

Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.

The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.

The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague’s Wenceslas Square Tramline
World.content:
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.

The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.

The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.

The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.

“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.



The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.

The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.

The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.

The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.

The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.

The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Video: Wild boar storms Budapest metro station, forcing line to shut down
World.content:
A wild boar caused an extraordinary disruption to Budapest’s M2 metro line on Saturday after somehow making its way into the Kossuth Lajos Square station and running down an escalator towards the platforms.

The incident brought metro services to a temporary halt between Deák Ferenc Square and Déli railway station, with the BKK deploying 30 replacement buses while the animal was being dealt with.

The unusual visitor was first spotted shortly after 11 AM, when the station’s traffic controller noticed a wild boar walking down an out-of-service escalator towards the platform level.

Wild boar briefly entered a metro train

According to Budapest public transport operator BKK, the station controller immediately alerted the driver of a metro train arriving at the station. The driver asked passengers on the platform to return to the train for their own safety.

The situation then became even more extraordinary: the wild boar briefly entered one of the metro carriages.

No passengers were injured, however. The animal soon left the train and made its way down a service staircase leading to the tracks, where it hid underneath a waiting metro train. The station was immediately evacuated and metro services were suspended in both directions while emergency crews were called to the scene.

A video of the animal inside the station was also recorded and later published online by Szeretlek Magyarország:

The animal was injured and eventually shot

Fire and rescue crews arrived to capture the animal, but officials soon discovered that the approximately 60-kilogramme wild boar was injured, according to the Budapest Transport Company (BKV). A veterinary officer was called to the scene to assess its condition. After considering the available options, authorities decided that the animal had to be shot.

It remains unclear where the wild boar sustained its injuries or how it managed to reach the Kossuth Lajos Square metro station in the first place. Earlier reports claimed that the animal had been hit by a metro train and subsequently shot by police. BKK later clarified that these reports were inaccurate.

According to the transport operator, the animal survived the encounter with the train and was later removed from the tunnel after the train had been moved and the station’s power supply had been switched off.

Replacement buses deployed across Budapest

The incident temporarily brought traffic on the M2 line to a standstill between Deák Ferenc Square and Déli railway station. The Batthyány Square station was also excluded from the replacement service. BKK deployed 30 buses to provide replacement services while emergency crews dealt with the situation. Services resumed shortly after midday once the operation had been completed.

Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony also reacted to the extraordinary incident on social media.

“Replacement buses had to be deployed on the M2 metro line because of a wild boar. I never thought I would have to write something like this…”

Karácsony added that nobody yet knew how the animal had ended up at the Kossuth Square metro station.

World.title: Fidesz attacks Tisza’s presidential nominee: ‘He will serve only until Péter Magyar replaces him with a comment’
World.content:
The Fidesz parliamentary group leader has launched a sharp attack on András Baka, the former president of Hungary’s Supreme Court, after the Tisza Party nominated him as the country’s next president.

János Bóka said on Saturday that Fidesz considers the election of a new head of state illegitimate, arguing that President Tamás Sulyok’s mandate was terminated by the Tisza Party “arbitrarily and illegitimately”. The Fidesz parliamentary group will therefore boycott both the nomination and election process, Bóka announced in a Facebook post.

“Hungary’s last legitimate president is called Tamás Sulyok,”

he wrote.

János Bóka and Viktor Orbán. Photo: Orbán Viktor/Facebook

Fidesz calls Baka’s nomination an ‘illegal procedure’

Bóka accused Baka, a prominent legal scholar and former Supreme Court president, of taking part in what he described as an unlawful process and helping to build what he called “Péter Magyar’s arbitrary rule”.

The Fidesz politician also referred to Baka’s legal battle with the Hungarian state, although he did not explicitly name the case. He claimed that Baka had previously taken Hungary to an international court over a “significantly smaller grievance” than the one he believes has now been caused by the Tisza Party’s removal of Sulyok.

Bóka was apparently referring to the case brought by Baka before the European Court of Human Rights. In 2016, the Strasbourg court ruled in Baka’s favour, finding that he had been removed prematurely as president of the Supreme Court through legislation specifically designed to affect his position after he had publicly criticised measures threatening judicial independence.

Baka’s case subsequently became a major example in discussions about judicial independence and the rule of law in Hungary.

‘Baka will be a puppet of the Tisza majority’

Bóka ended his statement with a particularly pointed prediction about the future president.

“András Baka will hold his position only until Péter Magyar replaces him with a comment. He will be the puppet of the Tisza majority, and he must be aware of that.”

The Fidesz group leader also said his party had declared political resistance against what it considers arbitrary rule. He pledged that Fidesz would support what he called the “circles of freedom” and work to restore constitutionalism.

The comments came shortly after the Tisza parliamentary group announced that it had selected Baka as its presidential nominee in a secret ballot:

Mi Hazánk also rejects Baka as a candidate

Fidesz was not the only opposition force to criticise the nomination. The Mi Hazánk Movement also declared Baka unsuitable for the presidency. Party leader László Toroczkai argued that statements made by Baka in recent years had made him unfit for the position.

Toroczkai described the nomination as “ironic”, arguing that Baka had previously fought against the kind of personalised and retroactive legislation that, in his view, the Tisza Party is now pursuing.

Mi Hazánk continues to support energy law expert Máté Tóth as its preferred presidential candidate. The party says he could help establish stronger checks and balances during a government that abuses its power.

Baka is expected to become Hungary’s next president

Despite the criticism, Baka’s election is expected to be largely a formality. The Tisza Party has a 141-member parliamentary group, giving it more than the two-thirds majority required to elect the president. Fidesz and KDNP have already announced that they will not participate in the election.

Parliament is scheduled to vote on the new president on Tuesday, 11 August.

If elected, Baka is expected to take office on 19 August, following the constitutional procedure under which the newly elected president assumes office on the eighth day after the announcement of the election result.

World.title: Warning by US intelligence: Putin could test NATO with attack within years
World.content:
US intelligence assessments indicate that Russian President Vladimir Putin could attempt to test NATO’s unity by launching a limited attack against a member state within the next few years, according to sources familiar with the reports.

The assessments reportedly outline several possible scenarios, ranging from a cyberattack to a small-scale military incursion. The objective would be to test how NATO responds and whether the alliance would remain united in the face of an attack on one of its members.

The reports do not establish when such an attack might take place or what form it would take. However, the Baltic states and Poland are reportedly considered among the most likely potential targets.

Russia could test NATO’s Article 5

One of the key concerns is that Moscow could deliberately launch an attack that challenges NATO’s commitment to Article 5 without immediately triggering an all-out military confrontation. Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty establishes the principle of collective defence: an armed attack against one NATO member is considered an attack against all members.

According to the intelligence assessments, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, a limited incursion could therefore be designed to expose disagreements between NATO members over how far the alliance should go in responding.

A cyberattack or other form of hybrid aggression could represent one possible scenario, while another could involve a small-scale incursion into allied territory. The timing remains uncertain. One source cited by CNN said Putin’s potential window for choosing his next course of action could extend from now into the next few years. US and NATO officials reportedly believe the risk could increase if Putin fails to secure a favourable way out of the war in Ukraine.

Baltics and Poland could be particularly vulnerable

While there is no confirmed Russian plan to attack a NATO country, sources familiar with the assessments reportedly consider the Baltic states and Poland among the most likely potential targets. The region has already been at the centre of heightened tensions between Russia and NATO.

Russia has repeatedly been accused of actions affecting NATO territory and airspace in recent years. In September 2025, NATO fighter jets shot down Russian drones that had entered Polish airspace during a Russian attack on Ukraine.

In May this year, a drone carrying explosives struck an apartment building in Romania while Russian forces were attacking a nearby Ukrainian port, injuring two people. These incidents have added to concerns that the conflict could spill over beyond Ukraine through direct or hybrid attacks.

NATO says it is prepared for multiple scenarios

NATO has declined to comment specifically on classified US intelligence assessments. Martin O’Donnell, a senior NATO military spokesperson, said the alliance is constantly preparing for a range of possible scenarios.

He stressed that NATO is monitoring developments and remains prepared to deter threats and defend its members if necessary. The alliance has significantly strengthened its eastern flank since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with additional troops, air defences and military infrastructure deployed across the region.

Explosive-laden drone raises fresh concerns in Germany

The intelligence reports come as European authorities investigate another potentially serious incident. An explosive-laden drone discovered at an airport in Germany this week was assessed by the United States as belonging to a Russian intelligence service, according to a US defence official cited by CNN.

The drone reportedly carried military-grade explosives and was found in a secure area used for cargo flight operations. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described the discovery of an armed drone at an airport as a new type of threat. He later indicated that the device could be linked to foreign powers, although he did not identify a specific country.

Germany’s National Security Council, led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, met on Friday to discuss the incident. The case has added to concerns about Russia’s increasingly sophisticated use of hybrid tactics, including drones, cyber operations, sabotage and other activities below the threshold of conventional warfare.

US weapons stocks add another layer of concern

The latest intelligence assessment also comes at a difficult time for the United States and its allies, as concerns grow over available stocks of key munitions and missile interceptors. The US has supplied significant quantities of weapons to its allies during recent conflicts, while American military resources have also been used in the war against Iran.

According to CNN, nearly 80 per cent of US THAAD missile interceptors and roughly half of its Patriot interceptors have been depleted compared with pre-war levels.

At the same time, civilian casualties from Russian long-range attacks in Ukraine have increased sharply. The United Nations has reported a 60 per cent increase in civilian casualties from such weapons between January and June compared with the same period last year.

A major Russian attack this week involving ballistic and anti-ship missiles killed at least 17 people and wounded dozens more, according to CNN. None of the missiles involved was intercepted by Ukrainian air defences.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Ukraine war remains central to the risk assessment

The intelligence assessment comes as US-led diplomatic efforts to end the war in Ukraine have stalled. Western sanctions have put pressure on the Russian economy, but they have not persuaded Putin to end the invasion.

According to the sources cited by CNN, the Kremlin’s future decisions could partly depend on the outcome of the war. If Putin fails to secure a face-saving settlement, US and NATO officials believe he could consider escalating against the alliance.

That does not mean an attack on NATO is inevitable. Rather, the intelligence assessments highlight a potential scenario in which Russia could deliberately test the alliance’s resolve. For NATO members on the alliance’s eastern flank, however, the warning underscores the continuing importance of deterrence and collective defence as the war in Ukraine enters another potentially dangerous phase.

World.title: BREAKING: Tisza announces its nominee for Hungary’s next president
World.content:
Hungary’s ruling Tisza Party has nominated András Baka, the former president of the country’s Supreme Court, as its candidate for President of the Republic.

The party’s parliamentary group made the decision in a secret vote on Saturday, selecting the 73-year-old legal scholar from three potential candidates.

With Tisza holding a two-thirds majority in Parliament, Baka is widely expected to be elected as Hungary’s next head of state when MPs vote on Tuesday.

Who is András Baka?

Baka is a legal scholar specialising in human rights and minority rights and has extensive experience in both Hungarian and international law.

Born in Budapest in 1952, he graduated from the Faculty of Law at Eötvös Loránd University in 1978. He subsequently spent more than two decades as a researcher at the Institute for Legal Studies of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

Between 1991 and 2008, Baka served two terms as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) in Strasbourg. He also worked as a visiting professor at several universities in the United States and was invited to lecture in France and West Germany.

In 1990–91, Baka served as an independent MP for the Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF), although he never joined the party. He was elected president of Hungary’s Supreme Court by Parliament in 2009.

Removed after criticising judicial reforms of the Orbán government

Baka became particularly well-known in Hungary after he was removed from his position as Supreme Court president in 2011.

His early dismissal came after he publicly criticised reforms introduced by the government of Viktor Orbán that he argued threatened the independence of the judiciary.

The case eventually reached the European Court of Human Rights.

In 2016, the Strasbourg court ruled in Baka v. Hungary that his premature removal had violated his rights. The court found that Baka had been removed through legislation specifically tailored to his situation after he had publicly expressed professional criticism of measures affecting judicial independence.

The case subsequently became a significant example in European discussions about judicial independence and the rule of law in Hungary.

The Council of Europe’s Committee of Ministers later criticised Hungary over its failure to fully implement the judgment.

Tisza praises Baka’s independence

In announcing the nomination, the Tisza parliamentary group highlighted Baka’s professional independence and his commitment to the separation of powers. The party said his decades of legal and judicial experience were particularly valuable at a time when Hungary was preparing to establish a new constitutional framework.

Tisza described Baka as someone who had consistently defended the rule of law and judicial independence throughout his career. The party said he was capable of representing the unity of the Hungarian nation and called him an independent and impartial figure whose professional career had already established his authority.

The nomination is also consistent with Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s earlier description of the qualities he wants in Hungary’s next president. Magyar has said the head of state should safeguard national unity and constitutional principles, carefully weigh opposing views and understand the consequences of presidential decisions.

Baka was one of three candidates

The final decision followed weeks of speculation over who Tisza would nominate. Magyar initially proposed former chess world champion Judit Polgár, but she declined the invitation. The prime minister subsequently met several potential candidates, including historian Ignác Romsics, lawyer Botond Fülöp, who became known publicly as the “Rural Lawyer”, and Baka.

On Friday, Magyar confirmed that three candidates would be put before the Tisza parliamentary group. The names were widely understood to be Baka, Romsics and Fülöp. The parliamentary group ultimately chose Baka in Saturday’s secret ballot.

Parliament expected to approve him on Tuesday

The presidential election is scheduled for Tuesday, 11 August. A candidate needs the support of two-thirds of MPs to be elected in the first round. With Tisza controlling 141 seats, the party has more than enough votes to secure the required majority on its own.

The Fidesz-KDNP opposition has announced that it will boycott the election, arguing that the removal of former President Tamás Sulyok was unconstitutional and that the presidential office was not legally vacant.

The opposition has therefore rejected the legitimacy of the process. The Mi Hazánk party has nominated energy lawyer Máté Tóth, but its six-member parliamentary group does not have enough MPs to put his name on the ballot without support from other parties.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Baka could take office on 19 August

If Parliament elects Baka on Tuesday, the new president can take office on the eighth day after the result of the secret ballot is announced. This means Baka could officially assume the presidency on 19 August, just one day before Hungary’s national holiday on 20 August.

He would therefore be expected to hand out state honours and awards at the traditional 20 August ceremonies almost immediately after taking office.

Under Hungary’s recently amended Fundamental Law, the new president’s mandate will last until the new Constitution enters into force, but for no longer than five years.

Baka’s expected election would therefore mark a significant change in Hungary’s presidency: a former senior judge who was removed from office after challenging government reforms could soon become the country’s head of state, tasked with representing constitutional principles and the unity of the nation.

UPDATE: Baka accepts nomination

Péter Magyar posted on Saturday:

“We personally informed Dr. András Baka of the Tisza faction’s decision and, at the same time, asked him to accept the nomination for the office of President of the Republic. The President accepted the nomination out of a sense of duty to the nation and is ready to work for the unity of the Hungarian nation and for a democratic, European Hungary.”

World.title: Tisza chooses next President, announces emergency funding for airports and changes to education
World.content:
Hungary’s ruling Tisza Party is set to decide on its candidate for the country’s next president, with three names reportedly under consideration ahead of Tuesday’s parliamentary vote.

The Tisza parliamentary group held a key meeting on Saturday morning to discuss the presidential nomination.

“We are holding an important parliamentary group meeting today: we will discuss the person of the President of the Republic,” the Tisza parliamentary group said in a social media post. The party added that Hungary needs a president who represents not a political party or side, but all Hungarians.

Three names reportedly under consideration

Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Friday that the Tisza leadership would put three candidates before the parliamentary group for consideration.

The three names are Botond Fülöp, András Baka and historian Ignác Romsics.

Magyar recently shared a photograph of himself with the three men, prompting speculation that they could be the party’s presidential candidates. He also said that the Tisza Party was looking for someone who had never held a party-political position and who could represent the unity of the nation.

The selection process follows the withdrawal of former Olympic fencer Judit Polgár, who previously declined Magyar’s invitation to become the party’s presidential candidate. The parliamentary group began its meeting at 10 AM on Saturday.

Parliament could elect the new president on Tuesday

The final candidate is expected to be chosen by the Tisza parliamentary group during Saturday’s meeting. The National Assembly could then elect Hungary’s next president on 11 August. With the Tisza parliamentary group holding more than the two-thirds majority required for the election, the new head of state is expected to be elected in the first round of voting.

Betting markets have also been closely watching the race. At the time of reporting, András Baka was reportedly the favourite on Polymarket, with 85 per cent of participants betting on him becoming the Tisza candidate, while Botond Fülöp was in second place with 13 per cent. However, such figures should not be treated as a prediction or evidence of the party’s decision. They reflect the expectations of people participating in a speculative betting market.

Energy situation temporarily stabilises

Meanwhile, the government has reported a temporary improvement in Hungary’s energy and water situation following a period of severe pressure caused by the heatwave and low water levels. The government has therefore ended its appeal for voluntary reductions in energy consumption.

The heat alert has also been reduced from the third to the second level from Saturday. However, Magyar warned that the improvement may not last and that restrictions could potentially return if conditions deteriorate again.

The situation at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant remains uncertain. The complete restart of the facility could take more than a month, although water levels are expected to improve significantly over the weekend.

Regional airports receive HUF 5.5 billion emergency support

The government has also approved a HUF 5.5 billion support package for three regional international airports: Debrecen, Hévíz-Balaton Airport in Sármellék and Pécs-Pogány Airport. Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said the additional funding was necessary to prevent the companies operating the airports from becoming insolvent.

Without the emergency support, the operators could have gone bankrupt this year, potentially forcing the airports to shut down and putting around 250 jobs at risk. Vitézy said the airports play an important role in tourism, regional economic development and competitiveness. However, their current passenger numbers do not allow them to operate sustainably in the long term.

The government has therefore ordered a comprehensive review of the airport operators and the preparation of a new operating concept. “The aim is not to throw another lifeline to the regional airports every year, but to operate them according to a genuine development and business concept,” Vitézy said. Hévíz-Balaton Airport alone is set to receive HUF 1.2 billion in state support this year.

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

Government proposes major changes to primary education

Another major announcement concerns Hungary’s primary schools. The Ministry of Education and Children’s Affairs has published a 14-point proposal package aimed at making lower-primary education more child-centred and focused on learning through experience.

The recommendations are not mandatory. Individual schools can decide which elements to introduce based on their local circumstances, pupils and educational programmes. The proposals include more flexible school days, longer breaks for movement and recreation, more project-based learning and greater use of museums, libraries and outdoor locations.

They also call for a more reasonable approach to homework. In the first year of primary school and in full-day schools, compulsory written homework at home should preferably be avoided, while weekend and holiday assignments should only be given in exceptional circumstances.

Other recommendations include:

shorter, potentially 35-minute lessons;

more outdoor activities and movement;

greater emphasis on arts, music, drama and creative activities;

more hands-on science and mathematics;

daily storytelling and reading aloud;

more flexible afternoon activities;

stronger developmental feedback instead of focusing solely on grades;

and clearer measures to prevent bullying and create safer school environments.

The ministry says schools can already begin implementing the recommendations in the academic year starting in September.

World.title: US Senate backs huge tariffs on Russian energy buyers – Hungary could be in the firing line
World.content:
The US Senate has overwhelmingly approved a major new Russia sanctions package that could impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and natural gas, potentially putting Hungary in the firing line.

The bill, named in honour of the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, passed by an 86-11 vote on Friday. According to CNN, it would introduce mandatory sanctions against Russian President Vladimir Putin, Russian oligarchs and state-owned companies, as well as foreign businesses supporting Russia’s defence industry.

However, one of the most significant elements of the legislation is the possibility of imposing tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods imported into the United States from some of the largest buyers of Russian energy.

Hungary could be among the countries affected

The legislation targets the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas. China and India are expected to be the most significant countries affected, but Hungary could also find itself on the list.

Hungary remains heavily dependent on Russian energy. According to European Commission data, Russian gas accounted for around 74 per cent of Hungary’s gas imports in 2025. The country’s dependence on Russian oil is even greater, with Russian crude reportedly accounting for more than 90 per cent of Hungary’s total oil imports last year.

The proposed legislation could therefore create a significant problem for Budapest. There is, however, an important potential exemption concerning natural gas. Countries importing less than 15 per cent of Russia’s total gas exports could avoid the additional tariffs if they are also taking significant steps to reduce their dependence on Russian gas.

This distinction is important for Hungary. Although Russian gas makes up a large share of Hungary’s own imports, Hungary’s total purchases represent only a fraction of Russia’s overall gas exports. The country could therefore potentially meet the first condition for an exemption. The second condition could prove more difficult.

Budapest would need to show it is reducing Russian energy dependence

The European Commission has acknowledged that Hungary has signed long-term gas supply agreements with American and European companies. Once deliveries begin, these contracts could cover around 12 per cent of Hungary’s annual gas consumption.

Nevertheless, Brussels has assessed Hungary’s overall progress in reducing its dependence on Russian energy as limited. That could become crucial if the US legislation is ultimately adopted in its current form.

Washington would have to decide whether Hungary’s efforts to diversify its gas supplies are sufficient to qualify for the exemption. In other words, simply arguing that Hungary does not import 15 per cent of Russia’s total gas exports may not be enough.

The situation is potentially more serious when it comes to oil. Unlike natural gas, the proposed legislation does not provide a similar 15 per cent exemption for Russian crude oil. Hungary imported roughly 5–5.5 million tonnes of Russian crude in 2025, equivalent to approximately 100,000–110,000 barrels a day.

Although the temporary shutdown of the Druzhba oil pipeline has forced Hungary to seek alternative supplies this year, Russian crude remains by far the dominant source of oil for the country.

Have you read this? PM Magyar: After Ukraine war, EU will return to Russian gas

Trump could still grant exemptions

There are several factors that could soften the impact of the legislation. The proposed tariffs would initially target countries that knowingly continue making new purchases of Russian oil or gas from the 30th day after the legislation takes effect.

The US President would also retain the power to grant exemptions to individual countries, provided the administration explains why doing so would be in the interests of the United States. This could become particularly relevant in Hungary’s case.

The former Hungarian government has previously claimed that Budapest secured a full and open-ended exemption from US sanctions affecting Russian energy delivered through the TurkStream gas pipeline and the Druzhba oil pipeline.

However, it’s unclear whether that earlier arrangement would automatically protect Hungary from the new tariff mechanism. The proposed legislation could create a separate legal framework specifically targeting countries that continue buying Russian energy.

A very different bill from the original proposal

The measure has changed substantially during more than a year of negotiations. The original version unveiled in 2025 was considerably tougher and reportedly envisaged minimum tariffs of 500 per cent, with far fewer exemptions. The latest version reduces the potential tariff to 100 per cent and gives the US Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, a key role in determining the final tariff rate.

The bill also gives the Trump administration considerable discretion over whether and how aggressively to implement the measures. Some senators had raised concerns that the legislation could hand the US administration excessive power to impose tariffs. An amendment seeking changes to the tariff provisions was ultimately rejected.

Zelenskyy watched the Senate vote

The timing of the vote carried particular significance. Graham had spent more than a year working on the sanctions package and announced in Kyiv, just one day before his death, that an agreement had finally been reached with the White House and his Senate allies.

Following his death, colleagues described the legislation as one of his most important political achievements. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attended Graham’s funeral in Washington and subsequently met senators at the Capitol. He also watched the procedural vote from the Senate gallery.

Zelenskyy has argued that stronger sanctions against Russia could both restrict Moscow’s ability to finance its war and send an important message to Ukraine and Europe.

Zelensky and Trump in the White House on 28 July 2026. Photo: Anadolu Agency

Never miss a headline: join our newly-launched Messenger group!

The bill still needs House approval

Despite the Senate vote, the new sanctions are not yet law. The legislation must still pass the US House of Representatives before it can reach the President. The House is currently on its summer recess and is not expected to return until September.

This gives Hungary and other potentially affected countries additional time to lobby Washington and seek changes or exemptions. For Budapest, however, the Senate vote is already a warning sign: if the legislation becomes law in anything close to its current form, Hungary’s continued reliance on Russian oil and gas could expose it to significant new US trade pressure.

World.title: 18-year-old Hungarian man suspected of killing Austrian man in anti-gay attack
World.content:
An 18-year-old Hungarian man is suspected of killing a 29-year-old Austrian man in Lower Austria, with investigators examining the possibility that the attack was motivated by the victim’s sexual orientation.

The victim was found dead early on Thursday in a house in Langenzersdorf, north of Vienna. The Hungarian suspect was arrested at the scene and reportedly gave a full confession on Friday. According to Austrian newspaper Krone Zeitung’s report, the two men had met online and arranged to meet at a house in Langenzersdorf while its owners were away.

Police investigate possible hate crime

The Korneuburg Public Prosecutor’s Office has confirmed that the case is being investigated as a possible hate crime. Spokesperson Gudrun Bischof told Austrian media that investigators believe the victim’s perceived sexual orientation may have been a motive for the killing.

The suspect reportedly lured the 29-year-old man to the house, which he was looking after in the absence of the owners. According to reports, the victim suffered severe injuries to his face and died at the scene.

Krone reported that the suspect practised taekwondo and allegedly used his martial arts skills during the crime. No weapon has been found, according to the report. Police were called to the property after an emergency alert. When officers arrived, the older man was lying on the floor with severe facial injuries and could no longer be saved.

The 18-year-old was arrested without resistance.

Links to ‘paedophile hunter’ groups

Austrian media have reported that the Hungarian suspect was allegedly associated with so-called “paedophile hunter” circles.

These groups claim to target paedophiles, but authorities have previously linked some of them to attacks on gay men based on the false equation of homosexuality with paedophilia.

According to reports, members of such groups have used social media to identify and lure men they believe to be gay before confronting, humiliating, assaulting or robbing them.

Austria has previously investigated similar attacks

The case comes amid wider scrutiny in Austria of groups accused of carrying out attacks under the guise of “paedophile hunting”.

A series of raids launched at the request of prosecutors in Graz last year across seven Austrian provinces resulted in numerous arrests. Those targeted included people suspected of hate crimes and individuals allegedly involved in attacks against members of the LGBTQ+ community.

Investigators in those cases reportedly uncovered allegations of victims being robbed, humiliated and physically assaulted, in some cases seriously.

According to HVG, following the death in Langenzersdorf, Austrian LGBTQ+ rights organisation HOSI Wien, the Social Democratic Party (SPÖ) and the Greens have called for the country’s national action plan against hate crime to be fully implemented as soon as possible.

The case is being investigated as a suspected murder and possible hate crime.

World.title: New Hungarian foreign-policy priorities set out for relations with Putin’s Russia, MAGA world, EU, V4, NATO and Balkans
World.content:
What is underway at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs may prove to be more than a simple change of leadership: it could amount to a restructuring that reaches to the institution’s foundations.

The institute has been transferred from the Prime Minister’s Office back to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Its new director-general is Botond Feledy, while András Rácz has been appointed his deputy, responsible for research and academic affairs.

Botond Feledy (l) and András Rácz (r) Photo: Prtscr/Youtube

Both researchers have been outspoken critics of the Orbán governments in recent years, condemning their confrontational approach towards the EU and conspicuously close ties with Russia. In an interview, they have now outlined the priorities they believe should guide Hungary’s foreign policy — and the role they envisage for a revitalised Institute of International Affairs.

A complete break with Orbán’s foreign policy

Feledy told InfoRádió that the institute was being rebuilt “from the ground up”. The aim is to create a background institution that does more than communicate political decisions after they have been taken. Instead, it would support the Foreign Ministry with analysis and expertise before decisions are made, bringing perspectives into the process that are less prominent within the ministry’s own structure.

In an interview with 444, also published yesterday, the pair said they were planning a complete break with the American- and MAGA-focused foreign policy direction associated with Balázs Orbán, the Prime Minister’s political director. Rather than operating along ideological lines, the new leadership wants the institute to focus on preparing decisions and to draw a clear distinction between professional analysis and political propaganda.

Orbán and Trump in the White House. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

The changes could also involve staff. Feledy said some employees would remain at the institute, while others would be asked to leave. The organisational structure would not simply be imposed from above, however: the new system would be developed together with the institute’s staff.

The leadership also intends to retain the institute’s status as a non-profit private limited company, arguing that this could provide greater flexibility when testing new technologies, including the use of artificial intelligence in public administration.

The EU may once again become a central concern

One of the most significant shifts in foreign policy is likely to concern Hungary’s relationship with the European Union. Feledy said that the institute had accumulated little expertise on EU affairs in recent years, and that this would have to change.

Hungary is a member of both the EU and NATO, he noted, meaning that advancing the country’s interests within the Union is not an ideological question but a fundamental national interest. Some 80 per cent of Hungary’s trade is conducted in that direction, he said.

The institute therefore plans to build new research capacity, primarily in EU affairs. Greater attention could also be paid to issues that have received less prominence in Hungary’s foreign-policy debate, including digital sovereignty, cyber and economic security, the protection of critical infrastructure, migration and the geopolitical consequences of climate change. Water management could also become a priority, given both the climate crisis and the current water-related emergency.

At the same time, the institute would retain its traditional strengths, including research into the Balkans and the post-Soviet space. It also plans to develop new expertise on China and East Asia.

Rebuilding relations in central Europe — particularly with Poland, Austria, the Czech Republic and Slovakia — could likewise receive greater emphasis.

Hungary’s foreign policy strategy may also be renewed. The current strategy, drawn up in 2011, would be replaced by a new document, in the preparation of which the institute would play a role. The leaders said civil-society organisations and other professional bodies would also be involved.

No break with Russia, but servility is over — and Ukraine must be rebuilt

In the case of Russia, the proposed shift would involve a change in the style of the relationship rather than a complete foreign-policy reversal.

Rácz said there was no short-term alternative to maintaining pragmatic relations, primarily because of Hungary’s energy dependence. But he argued that there was no need to maintain such a close and “servile” relationship with the Russian leadership as that demonstrated by the ties between former foreign minister Péter Szijjártó and Sergei Lavrov in recent years.

Szijjártó and Putin. Photo: Facebook/Szijjártó

The researcher added that the relationship between Szijjártó and Lavrov, Russia’s foreign minister, had been even closer than the Hungarian public currently realised.

Have you read this one? Did Minister Szijjártó brief Lavrov during EU talks and offer to forward documents? Leaked recordings here!

The approach to Ukraine is more cautious. The new leadership does not expect a rapid breakthrough, but Rácz said that “something has already begun”.

On minority rights, the priority should be the implementation of existing agreements rather than the conclusion of new ones. They also said that the concessions secured in this area had been achieved not by the Orbán governments but through pressure from the EU.

The change, therefore, would not take the form of a single dramatic foreign policy U-turn. Instead, it points to more professional and less ideological decision-making focused on the EU, stronger regional ties and a more pragmatic approach to relations with Russia and Ukraine.

The reformed Institute of International Affairs could become one of the main centres of expertise behind that new foreign policy direction.

World.title: Romanian shipyard delivers hull of largest cable-laying ship in Japan
World.content:
The VARD shipyard in Tulcea, eastern Romania, has completed the construction of the hull of “Discovery,” the largest vessel intended for the installation of submarine cables and the first such project delivered by the VARD group for the Japanese market.

The ship, valued at over USD 200 million, will have an important role in the development of infrastructure for offshore wind energy and the transport of electric energy through submarine cables.

The construction of the vessel’s hull was carried out in Romania, at the VARD shipyards in Tulcea and Brăila, and after launching, it was towed to the VARD Langsten shipyard in Norway, where the specialized equipment was installed, and the final tests were carried out before delivery. The vessel was officially handed over to the Japanese company Toyo Construction at the end of June and is currently heading to Japan, where it will be based in the port of Ishikari Bay.

“Discovery” was designed to meet the specific conditions in Japan, where the water depth increases rapidly near the coast. The vessel can operate both in shallow waters and offshore, where future floating wind farms will be installed.

The vessel is approximately 151 meters long, 28 meters wide, and can transport up to 9,000 tons of submarine cables, distributed in two carousels with capacities of 4,000 and 5,000 tons.

On board, the ship has a main crane with a lifting capacity of 400 tons and an auxiliary crane of 100 tons. The vessel is also equipped with a dynamic positioning system, a heliport and equipment for the operation of remotely operated underwater vehicles.

In addition to the installation of submarine cables, “Discovery” can also be used for offshore construction works, including the installation of foundations for wind turbines and anchoring operations for floating turbines.

The vessel is equipped with a hybrid propulsion system, in which diesel engines are used to produce electric energy, while propulsion is provided by electric motors. The system includes batteries and the possibility of shore power supply during stationing, in order to reduce fuel consumption and emissions. Up to 90 crew members and technicians can work on board.

The Japanese government has set the rapid expansion of offshore wind energy capacities as an objective in the coming period, and this vessel will be used for the installation of the submarine electric cables necessary to connect the new farms to the energy grid.

For VARD, the project marks the first delivery to the Japanese market in the segment of specialized vessels for the offshore wind industry. In recent years, the VARD Tulcea shipyard has specialized in the construction of the hulls of some of the most complex vessels intended for the offshore industry, including vessels for the installation of submarine cables and for the development of offshore wind energy projects.

Several of the most advanced vessels of this type currently used worldwide were built in Romania and subsequently equipped at the VARD group’s shipyards in Norway.

World.title: Romania’s eMAG to come under sole control of Naspers after EU approval
World.content:
The European Commission has approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the acquisition of sole control over Dante International of Romania by South African investment fund Naspers Limited.

"The Commission concluded that the notified operation does not raise competition concerns, as the companies are not active on the same markets or on markets that are in a vertical relationship, and the impact on the market structure is limited. The transaction was examined under the simplified merger control procedure," the EC stated in a press release.

Last month, businessman Iulian Stanciu announced the sale of his stake in the eMAG Group to global consumer internet and technology investment group Prosus, 17 years after taking over the company and 14 years after signing the partnership with Naspers, the owner of Prosus.

After the sale, eMAG will continue its development and extensive investment plans, with RON 1.2 billion budgeted in this fiscal year alone for technology, logistics and financial services, with the support of Prosus and an experienced management team, company representatives stated. They also noted the regional growth potential of e-commerce, which remains significant, with growth rates of up to three times in the coming years, compared to the current penetration rate of 11-12% of total retail.

"The investments will be directed predominantly toward logistics and delivery infrastructure, AI and financial services, consolidating the foundation for a strong digital economy in the region. I want to thank Iulian for his dedication, vision, and for keeping us focused on the customer and on continuous personal development," said at that time Tudor Manea, CEO of eMAG Group, cited by News.ro.

At group level, eMAG recorded in fiscal year 2025 a turnover of RON 11.4 billion (USD 2.64 billion), up 11% compared with the previous financial year. The eMAG Group portfolio includes the eMAG brand, the Fashion Days online store, Romania’s 100% online hypermarket Freshful, the IT and electronics specialist store PC Garage, the Romanian national and international express courier company Sameday, the Depanero repair workshop, the most relevant recommerce platform in South-Eastern Europe Flip, as well as the financial services company HeyBlu.

World.title: Eurostat: Romania allocated only EUR 18.8 per inhabitant to R&D in 2025, lower than in 2015
World.content:
European governments allocated an estimated EUR 130.2 billion, or 0.69% of their combined GDP, to research and development in 2025, according to a Eurostat analysis published on Friday, August 7.

The sum represents an increase of 2.4% compared to 2024 (EUR 127.14 billion) and an increase of 60.5% compared to 2015 (EUR 81.13 billion).

In 2025, on average, government budget allocations for research and development at EU level amounted to EUR 288.9 per inhabitant, an increase of 57.7% compared to 2015 (EUR 183.2 per inhabitant). Luxembourg (EUR 917.2 per inhabitant) recorded the highest budget allocations for research and development per capita among the EU member countries. It was followed by Denmark (EUR 627.1) and Germany (EUR 553.5).

At the opposite end, the lowest values were recorded in Romania (EUR 18.8), Hungary (EUR 57.4) and Malta (EUR 73.7). Moreover, compared to 2015, Romania (-9.6%) was the only EU country that recorded a decrease in budget allocations for research and development expressed in euros per inhabitant, from EUR 20.8 in 2015 to EUR 18.8 in 2025.

The other EU countries recorded increases ranging from +14.7% in Sweden (from EUR 363.4 per inhabitant in 2015 to EUR 416.7 in 2025) to +495.5% in Bulgaria (from EUR 15.5 to EUR 92.3).

As regards the distribution according to socio-economic objectives, 37.3% of the amount was allocated to the general advancement of knowledge, financed mainly through a global public grant known as public general university funds, used by public higher education institutions to support their activities. In addition, 18.4% of R&D funds were allocated to the general advancement of knowledge from sources other than the general university funds, 9.5% to industrial production and technology, 6.7% to health, and 5.8% to defense.

World.title: EIB lends EUR 100 million to BRD Sogelease to increase financing for businesses in Romania
World.content:
The European Investment Bank (EIB) is lending EUR 100 million to the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale to expand financing for businesses in Romania.

The goal is to facilitate financing for Romanian SMEs and Mid-Caps, which face greater hurdles in accessing long-term funding than their counterparts in many other European Union countries, EIB said.

The operation will enable BRD Sogelease to provide funding to Romanian companies seeking business expansion, productivity improvements and sustainable development.

Of the total loan, 15% is earmarked for green projects such as energy efficiency, renewable energy and sustainable transport.

Around 80% of the EIB loan is projected to be deployed in less-developed areas known in the EU as “cohesion regions.”

The new operation builds on previous EIB loans to BRD Sogelease IFN that total EUR 305 million over the past decade.

“In today’s rapidly changing economy, access to finance is a key enabler of competitiveness,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris. “By partnering with BRD Sogelease, we are mobilizing investment where it matters most: among Romanian entrepreneurs. This financing will help businesses become more resilient, more innovative and better prepared for the opportunities of tomorrow.”

“Our long-standing partnership with the European Investment Bank reflects a shared commitment to supporting the growth and resilience of the Romanian economy. This new financing facility will enable us to provide SMEs and Mid-Caps with enhanced access to long-term funding on attractive terms, helping them invest in expansion, innovation, productivity and sustainable development,” said BRD Sogelease GM Gabriel Mihai.

BRD Sogelease IFN SA is the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale, one of the leading banks in Romania with total assets of RON 96.3 billion as of June 2026. Established in 2001, BRD Sogelease IFN provides financial lease and other asset-based financial solutions to over 10,000 SME and Small-Cap clients in Romania.

World.title: Platform for foreign workers coming to Romania up and running, authorities say
World.content:
Romania’s Interior Ministry announced on Thursday, August 6, that the platform WorkinRomania.gov.ro is now up and running, simplifying the process of hiring foreign workers.

The platform aims to make it easier for immigrant workers to enter the domestic labor market. Among its benefits is the facilitation of the relationship between the employer and the future employee.

The platform helps both Romanian employers looking for a workforce and aids the state in managing more efficiently the employment of new workers coming from other states. “Less bureaucracy, shorter deadlines and the possibility to track each application in real time,” the Ministry noted, cited by Agerpres.

The services of this platform include: permanent access to one’s own electronic file; the possibility to track each stage of the procedure; automatic notifications regarding requests for additional documents or the adopted solutions; reduction of waiting times; increased transparency of the entire administrative process. The platform also connects future employees with the Trade Register, the Employee Records Register, as well as with IT systems for the checks provided by law.

The platform also centralizes the actions of several Romanian state institutions.

The General Inspectorate for Immigration within the Ministry of Internal Affairs handles the procedures within its competence regarding the regime of foreigners and the right of residence for employment purposes; it analyzes and resolves applications regarding the granting and extension of residence

The right of residence for employment purposes, issues the specific documents and participates in the electronic exchange of data necessary for substantiating administrative decisions.

The National Agency for Employment operationally administers the module intended for the registration and authorization of employers and agencies for the placement of foreigners and configures the workflows related to these procedures;

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through the national visa system and the eViza platform, participates in the workflows regarding the granting of long-stay visas for employment;

The National Agency for Fiscal Administration provides the information necessary for the fiscal checks provided by law;

The Ministry of Education and Research, through the National Center for the Recognition and Equivalence of Diplomas, contributes to the verification of qualifications and diplomas, in the cases provided by legislation.

The platform offers useful information for employers, placement agencies and foreign workers, available also in English. Interested persons can find on WorkinRomania.gov.ro all the information they need for creating and validating an account on the platform, the registration and authorization conditions, the necessary documents and the method of using the electronic services available on the platform.

At the same time, users have a support chat service, available both in text and voice format, which provides assistance and guidance in the use of electronic services, in Romanian and other languages.

In terms of security, the program is included in the Ministry’s Services Hub, specially designed to keep personal data safe at the level of each county.

Although Romania set an official quota of around 90,000 newly admitted foreign workers for 2026, employer demand significantly exceeds that ceiling. In some years, requests have reportedly been more than double the approved quota. Still, filling vacancies is only part of the challenge. A large share of newly arrived workers subsequently seek opportunities in other EU member states, where wages, working conditions, and social benefits are often more attractive.

World.title: Thriller starring Nicolas Cage to open this year's horror and fantastic film fest in Biertan
World.content:
The Full Moon Horror and Fantastic Film Festival, presented by the Transilvania International Film Festival, returns to Biertan for its 11th edition, bringing three days and three nights of premieres, cult films and open-air screenings.

The festival opens with the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son, starring Nicolas Cage. Another highlight of this year’s edition will be the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă, featuring live music by Dubase, preceded by an acoustic performance by Ana Coman and her guitar as part of Full Moon Unplugged.

At Bastion Open Air, the programme kicks off on Friday, August 14, with Nightborn, the new film by Finnish director Hanna Bergholm, known to horror audiences for Hatching. Selected for the competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, the film follows a couple who move into an isolated house in the Finnish woods, where the arrival of their first child awakens a disturbing presence. The evening continues with The Rocky Horror Picture Show, the horror musical that has become one of cinema’s great cult phenomena. The story behind the film will also be explored from behind the scenes in the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, screening on Saturday at Cinema Ion Hobana.

On Saturday, Bastion Open Air will screen Her Private Hell, the new film by director Nicolas Winding Refn, as well as the original Dutch version of the thriller The Vanishing. The programme also includes the 1993 American remake, also directed by George Sluizer, giving audiences an opportunity to compare the two versions.

On Sunday, Carrie returns to the Bastion screen. Directed by Brian De Palma and based on Stephen King’s novel, the classic marks 50 years since its release.

On Friday, August 14, Méliès Open Air will host the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son. Directed by Lotfy Nathan, the supernatural thriller stars Nicolas Cage as Joseph, alongside FKA twigs as Mary and Noah Jupe as their teenage son.

On Saturday, August 15, audiences are invited to the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă. Made in 1933 by Jean Mihail, the first Romanian-language talking film tells the story of travelers forced to spend the night at a railway station believed to be haunted. The film will be screened with live music performed by Dubase.

The Méliès programme concludes on Sunday, August 16, with The Virgin of the Quarry Lake, directed by Laura Casabé. Inspired by the prose of writer Mariana Enríquez, the film blends adolescence, jealousy and black magic against the backdrop of Argentina’s 2001 crisis.

The selection continues at Cinema Karloff and Cinema Ion Hobana, with titles including The Turkish Coffee Table, Gaua, Species, Roqia, Veins, The Uncertainty Principle, Feels Like Home, Anemoneciacs and Transylvania Tapes.

The program also includes Romanian short films, the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, and repeat screenings of The Carpenter’s Son, Nightborn and Her Private Hell.

The festival takes place between August 14 and August 16.

World.title: Romania’s Banca Transilvania extends EUR 71.4 mln loan for Entek Elektrik PV park
World.content:
The largest bank in Romania, Banca Transilvania, announced that it will finance the development of the Eco Sun Niculești photovoltaic park, Entek Elektrik’s first investment in local green energy production, with EUR 71.4 million.

It is one of the largest bilateral financings granted to a photovoltaic project under development in the country. Once completed, the park, located in Dâmbovița County, will have an installed capacity of approximately 205 MW. The total value of the project is estimated at EUR 100 million.

“Projects of this scale contribute to strengthening energy independence and modernizing the Romanian economy. We are pleased to support Entek Elektrik’s first investment in renewable energy production in Romania and to continue the solid partnership that we have built together,” said Cosmin Călin, Deputy General Manager Large Corporate, Banca Transilvania.

The investment in the Eco Sun Niculești project is made through Entek Elektrik Üretimi A.Ş., the renewable energy company of the Koç Group, and its main shareholder is Türkiye Petrol Refinerileri A.Ş. (Tüpraş), the largest industrial company in Turkey and the seventh largest refinery operator in Europe.

In Turkey, Entek owns an energy capacity portfolio of 550 MW. The company aims to further expand its renewable energy portfolio and seeks to become one of the leading green energy producers in Turkey.
